raw.title: AI Engineering Lead, GenAI Platform
raw.description:
About 9fin

9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.

Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.

Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.

We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.

The Opportunity

The AI Engineering team at 9fin is building the next generation of AI capabilities that will power our products for years to come. We're looking for an Engineering Lead to lead the GenAI Platform team, building the shared foundations that enable product teams to develop and operate AI-powered products and agents.

Reporting to the Head of AI, you'll own the team's development, technical direction and delivery. You'll shape the platform strategy and roadmap, working with product and engineering teams to understand their needs and decide where shared capabilities will have the greatest impact.

You'll combine people leadership with strong engineering judgement, staying close to architecture and code while giving engineers the support and autonomy to do their best work.

Every day is different, but here's an example of the kind of things you'll work on:

  • Lead and grow the team through hiring, coaching, feedback and clear expectations for performance and development.

  • Set the GenAI platform's direction and priorities, evaluate technical approaches and adapt the roadmap as product needs and evidence evolve.

  • Own the delivery and operation of reliable, secure and scalable platform capabilities, balancing quality, performance, cost and speed of development.

  • Make the GenAI platform easy for other engineers to adopt and extend through effective APIs, tooling, documentation and clear ownership.

  • Partner with AI and evaluation specialists to establish how platform changes are tested, measured and released.

  • Work with product, engineering and security colleagues to resolve dependencies, communicate trade-offs and turn emerging needs into sustainable capabilities.

What Makes This Role Different

You'll join an evolving GenAI platform with substantial scope to shape its next stage. You'll help decide what the platform should provide, which approaches to adopt and how the team should grow as 9fin's AI ambitions develop.

Your impact will reach across product teams. By building shared capabilities that engineers trust and choose to use, you'll help teams deliver AI products more quickly and operate them with confidence.

You'll own both people leadership and technical direction, developing the team while remaining closely involved in the engineering decisions that determine the platform's success.

About You

This role will be a great fit if you:

People Management

  • Have experience directly managing software engineers, including hiring, performance management and career development.

  • Can build a team with clear priorities, give useful feedback and support engineers to take ownership of their work.

Platform Engineering

  • Have built shared platforms or developer tools that other engineering teams adopted, and understand what makes those teams successful.

  • Can translate product needs into reusable capabilities and balance immediate delivery with longer-term platform development.

Production LLMs & Agentic AI

  • Have built or operated complex LLM-powered applications or agent systems in production.

  • Understand the challenges of non-deterministic systems, including evaluation, quality regressions, tool use, reliability, security and cost.

Backend, Cloud & Operations

  • Have a strong backend or infrastructure engineering background, with ownership of distributed production systems in the cloud.

  • Understand how to operate services reliably, including monitoring, incident response, performance and cost management.

Collaboration & Technical Leadership

  • Have the technical depth to review designs and code, assess alternatives and help engineers work through difficult problems.

  • Communicate trade-offs clearly, build effective partnerships across teams and use evidence to make decisions in ambiguous situations.

Bonus Points

Experience with any of the following would be highly advantageous:

  • Event-driven architectures or long-running asynchronous workloads

  • Secure execution environments and access controls

  • AI evaluation, experimentation or observability

  • Platforms handling sensitive data in finance or other high-trust environments

Benefits

We’re a scaling start up, and we enjoy sharing our success, when the company succeeds, we always reinvest that in our people. We also offer huge amounts of responsibility, an abundance of opportunity for growth and a platform to truly excel.

Financial & Insurance

  • Competitive Salary (our salary bands are benchmarked at the top end of the market)

  • Equity

  • Pension (your minimum contributions are 4% with 9fin matching up to 7%)

  • Private Medical Insurance

  • Paid sick leave with Income Protection for long periods of illness

  • Group Life Assurance

  • Season Ticket Loan & Cycle to Work schemes

Time off

  • 25 holiday days per year

  • Local public holidays (with the ability to exchange them for alternative days)

  • Work abroad for up to 3 months a year

  • 1 month paid sabbatical after 5 years of service

  • Enhanced parental leave & flexible working arrangements available

Training & Culture

  • Professional learning and development budget

  • AI experimentation budget

  • Quarterly team socials

  • Summer and Winter company social events

Hybrid Policy

9fin is a hybrid company, and the office is a regular part of how we work. From January 2027, all employees will work from their designated 9fin office on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Some teams may be asked to be in the office more often, where the nature of their work calls for it. For the rest of the week, you may work from wherever works best for you and your team. Your Talent Partner will share hybrid working details for this role.

9fin is an equal opportunities employer

At 9fin we are dedicated to building and promoting a fair and inclusive workplace where everyone can reach their full potential and truly belong. We recognize that building diverse teams enables a more creative and productive environment. If you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t perfectly align with the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might just be who we’re looking for — either for this role, or perhaps another.

raw.title: GTM Engineer
raw.description:
About 9fin

9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.

Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.

We're looking for a GTM Engineer to build and run the systems behind 9fin's next-generation go-to-market engine. You will own Clay and Gong end to end and use them, together with Claude and our CRM, to move 9fin towards a world where reps don't decide who to contact: they open a curated list of to-dos with hyper-personalised messages, review, and approve.

This is a new, high-impact role in Revenue Operations. You will report to the Head of Revenue Operations and work closely with Marketing Operations and the Director of GTM Transformation. You will own the architecture, the workflows and the adoption, and have real influence on how our GTM stack evolves, including newer tools such as an AI inbound agent.

Key Responsibilities:

Clay and AI GTM orchestration

  • Own Clay end to end: design, build, document and maintain workflows, Functions and Audiences across our prioritised use cases, such as inbound enrichment, scoring and routing, job change, closed-lost re-engagement, signal-based pipeline generation, TAM sourcing, CRM enrichment and hygiene, event prep, and renewal risk signals.

  • Deep expertise in Clay-native building. Strong examples of using judgment and creativity underneath your Clay builds. Show us your waterfall design, credit economics, signal selection, data modeling, and clean CRM handoff.

  • Build and run Clay workflows from Claude (via the Clay CLI or MCP), and help shape the Claude-based command centre that gives reps and AMs on-demand research, briefs and messaging.

    • Agentic extension examples: Ability to build Clay workflows using Claude Code with the Clay MCP or API.

  • Help define the long-term architecture and roadmap: which system holds which data, how signals flow between Clay, Salesforce, Gong and Claude, and how Clay can become our AI GTM orchestration layer.

  • Deliver the end state for reps: a prioritised daily list of actions with hyper-personalised messages they only need to review and approve. Start with AI that assists, then automate as confidence in data and output grows.

  • Manage enrichment credits, data providers and cost per workflow, and measure each workflow against pipeline and revenue outcomes.

Gong ownership

  • Be the product owner of Gong: configuration, integrations, permissions, trackers, scorecards and dashboards, plus the sequencing and outreach workflows (Gong Engage).

  • Drive adoption across Sales, SDR, AM and CS teams through onboarding, training, office hours and usage reporting, and help resolve user issues.

  • Turn Gong data into insight: win/loss analysis, competitor mentions and knowledge gaps, objection and messaging trends, and product feedback for Product and Sales leadership.

  • Feed Gong insights back into Clay and Salesforce, for example call-derived competitor renewal dates and closed-lost reasons that trigger re-engagement plays or Gong generated MEDDPICC.

  • Track new Gong features and releases, and recommend and roll out the ones that improve how we sell.

Wider GTM funnel and systems

  • Participate in evolving the end-to-end GTM flow, from lead capture through MQL, SQL and closed-won, working with Marketing Ops on lead management, scoring, routing and attribution.

  • Help build the next-generation GTM engine. This includes evaluating and implementing complementary tools, such as evolving Qualified into an inbound AI agent.

  • Protect data quality in Salesforce and across the stack, because AI amplifies both good and bad data.

  • Partner with RevOps, Marketing Ops and the Director of GTM Transformation on priorities, and collaborate with Sales, SDR, CS, Product and Engineering teams.

  • Document processes and train the GTM teams on new workflows and tools.

Skills & Experience

Requirements

  • 4+ years in Revenue Operations, Marketing Operations, Sales Operations, growth operations or GTM engineering at a B2B SaaS company building GTM systems across a modern GTM stack that includes CRM, enrichment, sequencing, marketing tools, and data pipelines.

  • 1+ years of hands-on experience building and running Clay in production (workflows, enrichment, scoring, CRM sync), ideally in a B2B SaaS GTM team.

  • 1+ year of hands-on experience administering Gong or an equivalent conversation intelligence tool, including AI trackers, dashboards, AI analysis, Engage/Sequences and driving team adoption.

  • Hands-on configuration experience with Salesforce or HubSpot (objects, fields, flows, data model, integrations).

  • Practical experience implementing AI in GTM workflows: prompt design, LLM-based research and messaging, and tools such as Claude, MCP or agents. We would like to hear what you have built and what you learned.

  • AI quality control: experience with human-in-the-loop design and measuring AI output quality (testing prompts, tracking approval and edit rates).

  • Analytical mindset: able to turn call and pipeline data into clear findings, such as win/loss, competitive gaps and product feedback.

  • Strong communicator who can train non-technical users, document what you build and work across Sales, Marketing, Product and Finance.

  • Self-starter who is happy owning an area that is still being defined, and who ships, measures and iterates.

Nice to have

  • Experience rolling out GTM tools from scratch at a scaling B2B SaaS company.

  • Experience with sales engagement, intent and enrichment tools (Apollo, 6sense, Bombora, Zapier, Qualified or similar).

  • Experience with lead scoring, routing and funnel reporting (MQL to SQL to Won).

  • Comfortable with APIs, webhooks and JSON, and able to debug integrations. Light scripting (JavaScript or Python) is helpful.

  • Account-based, finite-TAM experience: multi-threading named accounts where quality is more important than volume and strong sense of brand reputation in everything that goes out.

  • Custom signal sourcing: experience building signals from niche sources (fund moves, deal activity, regulatory filings).

  • First-party data as signal: Ability to leverage 9fin’s own product usage and content engagement. Experience piping product data into GTM plays.

  • Expansion and renewal plays: Previous experience finding renewal risk and creating AM/CSM workflows to prevent churn.

  • UK/EU outbound compliance: Working knowledge of GDPR and/or PECR.

Our benefits

We're a scaling start up and we enjoy sharing our success. When the company succeeds, we always reinvest that in our people. We also offer huge amounts of responsibility, an abundance of opportunity for growth and a platform to truly excel.

raw.title: Business Development Lead
raw.description:
Accurx is solving healthcare productivity for the NHS.

For decades, the NHS has struggled with fragmented systems that make simple tasks feel impossible. At Accurx, we’re changing that by building a single, system-wide platform that helps every patient get gold-standard, efficient, and joined-up care.

What started as a way for GPs to text a patient has now evolved into an all-in-one digital toolkit used by 98% of GP practices.

Our platform now powers Total Triage to manage patient demand, and Self-Book, which lets patients schedule their own appointments in seconds. We’ve automated routine care with Patient Questionnaires for long-term conditions, while Accumail finally allows staff-to-staff communication to happen instantly across different care settings. We’re now pushing the boundaries of the consultation itself with Accurx Scribe, our AI-powered note-taker that drafts medical notes in real-time.

We’re not just shipping features. We’re giving clinicians their time back and ensuring every patient journey is as smooth as it should be.

Sounds mega, right? Here's where you come in...

As our Business Development Lead for the North, you’ll be a player-coach driving mid-market sales across PCNs, GP practices and federations: closing deals yourself while building and coaching a high-performing outbound team as we launch new products across the region.

Based in London, with regular travel across the North of England.

  • Build an outbound engine: Set up high-volume cadences and buyer-signal plays to scale adoption across the North

  • Lead from the front: Close your own key deals while coaching a team of BDAs and BDMs to hit team targets

  • Grow new products: Drive expansion across our product suite, including Scribe, plus a few things we can’t share yet that will change how primary care works

  • Turn data into direction: Map the market, forecast pipeline and set clear commercial priorities

  • Stay close to users: Get out to regional events and webinars, and talk directly with primary care teams

  • Put AI to work: Use tools like Notion AI to sharpen targeting, capture insights and automate admin, so your team spends more time with users

  • Work across teams: Partner with Marketing, BD and Customer Success to convert deals and grow the region

You should apply if...

  • You’ve carried a number: You have an SDR, AE or sales management background and a track record of hitting targets

  • You love developing people: You have some experience managing or coaching salespeople, and you hold the bar high

  • You know outbound at scale: You’re hands-on with structured cadences and high-volume mid-market pipelines

  • You’re fluent in data: You can turn spreadsheets and datasets into decisions and pitches

  • You can forecast: You set targets and build pipeline forecasts your team can trust

  • You get stuff done: You move with urgency and build repeatable processes in a fast-changing startup

  • Bonus points if you know the sector: You’ve sold into the NHS, primary care or the public sector

What’s in it for you?

You’ll join a high-performing team on a mission to solve healthcare productivity, building a platform used by around 300k NHS staff every week, supporting the care of over 50 million NHS patients every year. We set a high bar, move fast, and give people the ownership and support to do the best work of their careers

  • £75,000 - £95,000 salary, plus a discretionary recognition bonus for exceptional performance and impact, nominated by managers and awarded by our leadership team

  • Equity: £30,000 in equal share options, so you share in the value you help create

  • Benefits to suit you: adjust your healthcare cover, your pension or life insurance, whatever stage you’re at in life

  • Built for collaboration: We are an office-first culture and ask that you’re in our (dog-friendly) Shoreditch office for a minimum of 3 days a week

  • Close to our users: Regular hackathons, plus dedicated time to visit GP practices and other healthcare settings to see first-hand how our products are used

  • Time off: You’ll get 28 days of holiday (plus bank holidays) and up to 4 weeks to work from anywhere per year

  • Support at home: We offer enhanced parental leave, fertility support and parental loss support

  • We have our very own chefs: Free healthy breakfasts, snacks and lunches, plus a weekly sweet treat

Compensation: £75K – £95K • Offers Equity

You will run the core finance engine to a high standard, while taking this window of opportunity to raise the bar on commercial reporting, providing real margin insight, and ensuring finance has a genuine seat at the table in commercial decision-making.

  • Elevating the finance function: Moving beyond just keeping the lights on to fundamentally changing what "good" looks like for us and raising the bar in our reporting capability.

  • Driving trading insights: Developing core trading metrics and improving the speed, quality, and usefulness of commercial reporting to give leadership clear visibility of progress and risk.

  • Running the core engine: Overseeing all accounting, financial operations, treasury, and compliance, while managing the annual audit, budget, and quarterly forecasts.

  • Commercial business partnering: Acting as the lead finance partner to the commercial team by embedding yourself in planning and influencing decisions, rather than just reporting on them after the fact.

  • Margin and cost optimisation: Owning key trading initiatives focused on margin improvement

  • Automating for the future: Working alongside our data team to automate reporting through our data infrastructure and transition away from a reliance on spreadsheets.

  • Team leadership: Managing and guiding an established, high-performing team of two direct reports (FP&A Manager and Finance Ops Manager), helping them increase their business impact.


You should apply if...

  • You have proven experience operating autonomously at a Finance Director, Head of Finance, or senior FP&A level, including line management of a finance team.

  • Prior experience in an interim role where you've left a high-performing function even better than you found it.

  • You are a fully qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA, or equivalent).

  • You have a strong track record as a genuine business partner to commercial or trading functions, with specific examples of influencing decisions through financial insight.

  • You have experience working within a mature-stage B2B SME, ideally in a fast-growing, PE/VC-backed business scaling between £30m and £200m.

  • You are comfortable taking full ownership of the complete finance remit, spanning accounting, treasury, compliance, audit, and FP&A.

  • You have experience collaborating with data teams to build, improve, and automate commercial reporting systems.

  • You are a driver, not a passenger who can operate with minimal direction

raw.title: Senior Account Manager
raw.description:
Our Mission

Join us in shaping the future of paid search intelligence.

Adthena is an award-winning search intelligence platform powered by patented AI technology and a team of dedicated experts. We help brands, marketers, and agencies dominate their competitive landscapes with unparalleled insights into the paid search market. Our Whole Market View, Smart Monitor, and Local View solutions give clients the clarity to optimize spend, increase ROI, and stay ahead of the competition.

Trusted by global brands like Citibank, L’Oréal, and Volvo, and backed by Updata Partners, we’ve been redefining search intelligence since 2012.

In 2025, Adthena continued its winning streak, earning 8 major search industry awards. Highlights include Best AI Search Software Solution at the US Search Awards, Best Search Software Tool at the European Search Awards, and Best Software Innovation at the Global Search Awards.

Ready to make an impact in an industry-leading company? Let’s do it together.

Why Join Us?

We offer the best of both worlds: the maturity of a well-established company combined with the energy, agility, and impact of a scaling tech organisation.

We’re smaller than large-scale enterprises, offering more autonomy, less red tape, and accelerated growth.

Here’s what we offer:

  • Strong Culture: Our quarterly surveys show a 93% average approval rating for company culture, with an overall eNPS of 27.

  • Award-Winning Product: US 2025 Search Awards for Best AI Search Software Innovation

  • Stock Options: Our employees do incredible work, so as we grow, everyone shares the rewards.

  • Trust-Based Vacation: Take as much time off as you need, when you need it.

  • Flexible Work: Work how and where you do your best, with full autonomy over your day.

  • Career Growth: Bespoke training and career development via "Sherpa plans” to guide your growth.

  • Family Care Package: Up to 6 months fully paid maternity leave, and 2 months paternity leave.

  • Home Office Stipend: $200 for your ideal remote setup.

  • Swag Welcome Gift: $70 credit to grab some merch.

  • Birthday Day Off: Celebrate your special day.

  • Regular Socials: Summer & Christmas parties, annual and quarterly offsites, monthly meet-ups. See here for more info.

  • Volunteer Days: Make a difference with paid volunteer time each quarter. See here for more info.

About the Role

Reporting to: Anna Dutton, Director, Account Management, EMEA

Location: London or surrounding areas, with a hybrid work arrangement of 1-2 days in the office per week.

Interviews: 3 stages

Start Date: January 6th 2027

More info: See FAQ below, our candidate hub, or reach out to

About your Team

Adthena is a ‘Customer Value’ oriented business. As such, the Customer team is critical to our success. In our London office, this team consists of Account Management and Customer Success roles - both of which are critical to the success of our clients.

We work closely together to leverage each other's skills and abilities, ensuring that our clients are successfully achieving their goals. We work as a close-knit, highly functional team and contribute to the wider business by working closely with Sales and Marketing to encourage business alignment.

What you’ll do at Adthena

As a Senior Account Manager, you own medium and large accounts and are responsible for protecting and growing revenue across multiple brands, markets, and stakeholders. You confidently lead renewals, commercial negotiations, and upsell conversations, often shaping larger and more complex deals.

At this level, you’re strategic and proactive in how you manage your portfolio: spotting risks early, driving long-term value, and contributing to client plans that influence retention and growth. You work closely with internal teams, lead executive business reviews, and act as a trusted advisor to senior stakeholders.

Responsibilities

You retain client revenue by proactively managing renewals and risks.

  • Ensure timely proactive contract renewals and negotiate terms where necessary

  • Proficient at uncovering client requirements via discovery techniques. A strong understanding of questioning techniques.

  • Foster and build strategic relationships to understand and record Adthena’s impact on outcomes and results.

  • Working in conjunction with multiple internal stakeholders across the business, including Customer Success, Finance and Product, to make both tactical and strategic EBR plans.

  • Identify flags and risks quickly and escalate these through appropriate channels

  • Create and execute recovery plans for clients who are deemed at risk.

  • Negotiate commercials and terms of engagements

  • Monitor client health and forecast retention rates

You partner with clients to help them achieve long-term success with Adthena.

  • Ownership of mid-market and enterprise customers, totalling £1.8m in ARR.

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with economic and senior stakeholder

  • Capture client goals and link Adthena usage to clear, measurable outcomes

  • Adhere to processes and engagements as outlined in AM Playbook

  • Act as a trusted advisor, an extension of the client’s team, delivering strategic insights and best practices where necessary.

  • Partner with your CSM to shape Success Plans and guide clients toward long-term value

  • Plan and lead service reviews with clarity and confidence

You grow revenue by spotting upsell opportunities and aligning value to need.

  • Hit ~10% annual growth target across your portfolio

  • Grow clients across products, brands and markets.

  • Ensure client awareness of product innovations and services available.

  • Use data and account insights to surface expansion potential

  • Effectively communicates own interests and priorities in a negotiation, and can deploy and manage different negotiation tactics.

  • Lead on positioning and negotiation of commercial upsells, using a number of different negotiation tactics

Required Experience:

  • 4+ years of experience in Account Management, preferably in a SaaS environment

  • Strong commercial understanding, negotiation and objection handling skills

  • Proven ability to hit upsell / retention KPI’s and nurture Customers long term

  • Strong communication skills, both verbal and written

  • Ability to engage with senior stakeholders, including C-Level

  • Ability to think on their feet, problem solve creatively and build compelling business cases

  • Strong fact-finding, active listening and discovery skills

  • Attention to detail with a sense of urgency and accountability

  • CRM management

  • Experience working across a large and varied portfolio of clients, which include enterprise customers

  • Previous experience in relationship management

  • Management of renewal cycle and commercial negotiations

  • Comfortable working with data, with the ability to identify trends and make insight-driven recommendations

Bonus Points If You Have:

  • Experience in Search Marketing or Digital Advertising

Our Core Values

All Adthenians are expected to align closely with our ‘Core Values’.
What it means...

  • Get Shit Done: We're big on taking action, owning our challenges, and finding solutions.

  • Freedom with Responsibility: We take charge of results to recognition. We know that our hustle not only moves the needle for the company but also sets us up for personal success.

  • Deliver Remarkable Quality: We care about exceeding expectations in the work we do and aim to always do our best work as individuals and as a team.

  • Smart & Always Improving: We strive daily to expand our knowledge and become better at what we do.

raw.title: Head of Sales, UK & Europe — Agentis Asset Management Services
raw.description:
Our Firm

Asset Management Services (“AMS”) is the asset management practice of Agentis Capital Advisors, a global infrastructure advisory and investment platform. AMS manages more than 120 infrastructure assets representing over $35bn in enterprise value across renewables, public-private partnerships, digital and social infrastructure. We support our clients over the life of their assets through four service pillars:

  • Financial Model Management – We build, standardise, enhance and maintain the financial models behind our clients’ funds and portfolio companies

  • Financial Services Management – We run the accounting, budgeting, lender compliance and financial reporting for project companies

  • Operations Management – We oversee the day-to-day management of assets, including contract administration, performance monitoring, and board and stakeholder support

  • Fund Operations & Reporting – We maintain the fund-level valuation models, NAV and exit calculations, and leadership and LP reporting

AMS gives private markets and infrastructure investors one consistent, auditable and trusted view of their portfolios, delivered as a managed service. Our clients include leading infrastructure funds, pension funds, developers and project companies. Our guiding principles of excellence, client success, commitment, people and entrepreneurship set us apart.

The Opportunity

Private-markets managers and large asset owners run their portfolios on hundreds of inconsistent models, built by different advisors in different formats. Valuation, investor reporting and portfolio oversight are slow, manual and hard to audit. AMS solves this. We take over a client’s portfolio models, rebuild them to one standard on our technology-enabled platform, and deliver a live, fund-level view of the whole portfolio. We maintain and enhance it with our specialists on an ongoing basis.

We are looking for a Head of Sales, UK & Europe, based in London, to take this service to market and expand our client base. This is a hands-on, player-coach role, reporting to the Agentis Capital Managing Partners.

This role suits a commercially driven seller who has sold value-added services into funds (e.g., fund administration, back-office, data, valuation or portfolio-monitoring software and services), selling to CEOs, heads of asset management, CFOs, COOs and finance teams of private-markets managers. You want to own a territory and build a business, not inherit a book.

Our Differentiators

  • The first dedicated sales leader for a new AMS service line, shaping how it goes to market from day one

  • A differentiated product to sell: an exclusive, technology-enabled modelling and portfolio-reporting platform, delivered by Agentis professionals as a managed service and not as another software licence

  • Ability to build on Agentis’s long-standing relationships with infrastructure funds, pension funds and asset owners

  • A competitive base plus uncapped commission tied to the recurring revenue you bring in

  • The opportunity to hire and lead additional sales professionals as the business grows

  • An entrepreneurial culture with a flat structure and direct access to Partners and senior leadership, where good ideas are acted on quickly

Key Responsibilities

Build and Run the UK & European Pipeline

  • Own the UK and European target universe: private-markets fund managers (infrastructure and renewables first, then real estate and private equity), pension and institutional direct investors, and large asset-portfolio owners

  • Run a disciplined outbound campaign: prioritise and tier targets, secure first meetings and keep a steady weekly cadence of new conversations

  • Use Agentis’s existing relationships, working with Partners to convert warm introductions into qualified opportunities

  • Keep the CRM accurate as the system of record for contacts, meetings, pipeline stage, forecast and next steps

Win and Close Mandates

  • Lead the full sales cycle, from discovery and demonstrations to pilots, proposals, pricing, negotiation and signed multi-year mandates

  • Sell to multiple stakeholders: CFOs, COOs, heads of portfolio/asset management, valuation and investor relations, and the risk, IT and procurement teams who must approve the service

  • Run structured pilots and proofs of concept that turn into paying, recurring engagements

  • Address data-security, information-handling and technology questions with the AMS delivery team, including due-diligence questionnaires

  • Expand existing clients from an initial portfolio into wider fund, valuation and reporting work

Shape the Go-to-Market

  • Feed market insight into the sales narrative, buyer personas, objection handling, pricing and packaging

  • Help develop sales collateral, case studies, demonstrations and the website, using the platform’s outputs as proof points

  • Represent AMS at industry conferences and events across the UK and Europe, and build the service’s profile in the market

  • Track competitors and adjacent offerings, and report what is winning and losing deals

Build the Sales Team

  • As the business grows, recruit, onboard and lead additional sales professionals

  • Coordinate with the North American sales lead on shared global clients, consistent messaging and pipeline reporting

Partner with Delivery

  • Work closely with the AMS modelling and delivery team so that what is sold can be delivered well and on time

  • Ensure a smooth handover from sale to delivery during onboarding, set realistic client expectations and support client change management

  • Report weekly to the Partners and AMS steering group on pipeline, conversion, forecast and market feedback


Skills and Experience

  • A substantial and proven track record in B2B sales or business development, including selling value-added services, data or software into funds or institutional investors

  • Experience selling fund administration, fund accounting, back-office, valuation, portfolio-monitoring, investor-reporting or financial-data solutions to private-markets managers is strongly preferred

  • A proven ability to open new doors and close complex, consultative, multi-stakeholder sales with long cycles and recurring revenue

  • A working understanding of how funds and portfolio companies are valued, modelled and reported

  • An existing network of finance and asset management leaders at UK and European private-markets managers, pension funds or asset owners is a strong asset

  • Comfort selling a technology-enabled service, and explaining data-security and AI-governance safeguards with credibility to risk-averse buyers

  • Self-motivated and entrepreneurial: comfortable building process, collateral and pipeline from scratch in a start-up setting within an established firm

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication and presentation skills

  • Infrastructure, renewables or real-assets experience is an asset

  • Competitive compensation arrangement including an uncapped commission on recurring revenue

  • Eligibility for the Agentis employee ownership programme and access to principal investment opportunities alongside Partners, subject to programme terms

raw.title: Account Executive, Partnerships – SME & Growth
raw.description:
About Airwallex

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

 

Learn more about your team

SME & Growth at Airwallex is about more than closing deals. We help small and mid-market businesses solve real financial challenges across borders: getting paid globally, managing multi-currency accounts, paying suppliers, and running spend across markets from a single platform. You're not selling a feature. You're helping founders and finance leaders replace fragmented financial operations with one global system that actually scales.

It's a function for sellers who like to build, not follow a script: curious, resourceful, and comfortable figuring things out in markets that are still wide open. You get real autonomy to create value, build relationships, and move opportunities forward.

If you want to sell a serious product, solve real problems for ambitious businesses, and build your career fast, this is a place to do it.

How you'll make impact

You'll help turn partner-referred opportunities into successful customer relationships across the UK SME market. By combining consultative selling with strong partner collaboration, you'll help growing businesses solve their cross-border financial challenges with Airwallex.

  • Own the full sales cycle for partner-referred SME opportunities, from qualification and consultative discovery through commercial negotiation, closing and initial onboarding.

  • Convert high-intent referrals into active, growing Airwallex customers by understanding each business's cross-border financial setup, operational challenges and growth plans.

  • Build deep product expertise across multi-currency business accounts, global transfers, corporate cards, treasury management, spend management and payment processing.

  • Partner closely with GTM Partner Managers and referral partners to communicate Airwallex's value proposition, strengthen referral relationships and move opportunities forward.

  • Work cross-functionally with Legal, Risk, Compliance, Revenue Operations and Onboarding to execute commercial agreements and deliver a smooth customer experience.

  • Exceed revenue and account activation targets through effective, value-based selling, while sharing best practices that improve partner-sales conversion.

You'll work from our London office three days a week.

What we're looking for

Essentials

  • 3+ years of B2B sales experience in fintech, commercial banking or B2B SaaS.

  • Demonstrated experience selling financial solutions such as cross-border FX, treasury, business banking, payments or corporate cards to SME customers.

  • A track record of consistently meeting or exceeding OKRs or KPIs in a consultative selling environment.

  • Strong commercial and strategic instincts, with the ability to understand customer needs and recommend tailored solutions.

  • Proficiency with CRM platforms such as Salesforce and standard sales enablement technology.

  • Strong analytical, written and verbal communication skills.

  • A bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.

Preferred

  • Experience working directly with referral partners, ecosystem partners or strategic alliances to drive sales pipeline.

  • A solid working understanding of API integrations.

  • Experience managing complex pipelines and multi-stakeholder deals in a fast-paced environment.

  • A strong track record of cross-functional alignment with Risk, Legal and Onboarding teams.

You'll thrive here if

  • You have a track record of hitting your numbers, and you're motivated by stretch goals.

  • You're comfortable making decisions with incomplete information and moving quickly anyway.

  • You own the outcome and you don't wait for permission to fix what's broken.

  • You enjoy working closely with people across multiple countries and time zones as part of one connected, global team, including flexing your hours occasionally to make that connection work.

  • You value in-person collaboration and are happy being in the office three days a week.

Applicant Safety Policy: Fraud and Third-Party Recruiters

To protect you from recruitment scams, please be aware that Airwallex will not ask for bank details, sensitive ID numbers (i.e. passport), or any form of payment during the application or interview process. All official communication will come from an @airwallex.com email address. Please apply only through careers.airwallex.com or our official LinkedIn page.

Airwallex does not accept unsolicited resumes from search firms/recruiters. Airwallex will not pay any fees to search firms/recruiters if a candidate is submitted by a search firm/recruiter unless an agreement has been entered into with respect to specific open position(s). Search firms/recruiters submitting resumes to Airwallex on an unsolicited basis shall be deemed to accept this condition, regardless of any other provision to the contrary.

Equal opportunity

Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Airwallex is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We don’t regard color, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

raw.title: Associate Director, Operational Risk Management
raw.description:
About Airwallex

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

 

About the team

The Global Risk team at Airwallex plays a critical role in enabling the company's growth by building a strong, scalable, and globally consistent approach to risk management.

The team works across the business to define risk appetite, develop frameworks and policies, support strategic decision-making, and provide oversight of key risks as Airwallex expands across products, markets, and regulatory environments.

You'll be part of a highly collaborative group that partners closely with Product, Engineering, Operations, Commercial, Financial Crime Compliance, Regulatory Compliance, and Legal teams to help Airwallex grow responsibly and with confidence.

This is a team where you'll tackle complex, high-impact challenges, shape how risk is managed at a global fintech, and help build the foundations for long-term scale.

How you'll make impact

You'll own the Group's Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) and Incident Management framework as part of the Second Line of Defence, and provide independent, consolidated oversight of how the First Line identifies, assesses, and manages risk across Group entities.

  • Own the Group RCSA and incident management frameworks: Maintain the methodologies, standards, policies, taxonomy, guidance, templates, and supporting procedures for the Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) and for identifying, recording, investigating, and reporting operational risk events, keeping them current and aligned with Group operating models, risk appetite, local entity requirements, and relevant regulatory expectations.

  • Drive consistency across the Group: Promote consistent risk assessment, incident classification, and ownership across business units and Group entities.

  • Provide independent review and challenge: Challenge First Line risk assessments, control ratings, incident classification, root-cause analysis, and remediation plans, ensuring they are timely, evidence-based, proportionate, and comparable across the business.

  • Govern the lifecycle and drive actions to closure: Support governance of RCSA frequency, approvals, and evidence standards, and track actions arising from RCSAs and incidents through to completion, escalating overdue items with clear accountability.

  • Turn data into insight and decision-ready MI: Analyse RCSA, incident, and loss data to identify trends, themes, and systemic control weaknesses, escalate repeat issues to the right owners and governance forums, and produce clear reporting and recommended actions for Operational Risk reporting, governance forums, and relevant risk management committees.

  • Support regulatory notification: Work with Regulatory Compliance, Regulatory Legal, and First Line teams so material incidents are assessed and notified to the relevant regulators on time, in line with Group and local regulatory expectations.

  • Enable the First Line: Give practical guidance on risk identification, assessment, incident reporting standards, and root-cause methodologies. Run workshops, training, and coaching so that RCSAs are a useful management tool rather than a compliance exercise and high-quality incident reporting becomes business as usual.

  • Maintain a clear 1LoD / 2LoD line: Keep ownership and accountability between First Line risk and control owners and Second Line oversight explicit and well documented.

You'll report to the Head of Operational Risk and work from our London or Amsterdam office three days a week.

What we're looking for

You will own the design, execution, and continuous optimization of our global fraud strategy, policies, detection systems, and operational workflows across Airwallex’s financial infrastructure. In this role, you will lead a high-performing team responsible for stopping fraud in real time while keeping friction low for legitimate, high-growth global businesses. Airwallex processes billions in cross-border payments, multi-currency corporate cards, merchant acquiring, and embedded finance products. You and your team will directly defend our ecosystem against card fraud, account takeover (ATO), merchant bust-out, payment scams, and synthetic identities.

You will partner directly with Engineering, Data Science, Product, Legal, and Compliance and interface closely with Second Line Risk to build and operate scalable, AI-native fraud detection models, effective triaging processes and operational guardrails.

  • Define & Execute 1LoD Global Fraud Strategy: Direct and build out the operational fraud strategy across all Airwallex products (Global Accounts, FX, Acquiring, Cards, and Embedded Finance / BaaS). Translate enterprise risk appetite set by the board and 2LoD Risk into actionable rules, detection logic, operational policies, and loss-prevention workflows.

  • Lead & Scale the 1LoD Fraud Team: Build, lead, and mentor a world-class team of fraud strategists, analysts, and operations specialists responsible for rule writing, alert triage, incident response, and dispute operations.

  • Optimize Risk vs. Conversion: Own and execute real-time fraud decisioning rules, loss-mitigation frameworks, and chargeback monitoring programs. Drive precision in risk controls to reduce fraud losses without introducing unnecessary friction for legitimate customers.

  • Drive Product & AI/ML Execution: Co-own the fraud product roadmap with Data Science and ML Engineering teams. Directly inform and test next-generation models for real-time transaction monitoring, device fingerprinting, behavioral biometrics, and anomaly detection.

  • Own Partner & Scheme Operational Compliance: Ensure operational adherence to fraud rules, monitoring programs, and threshold limits established by card schemes (Visa, Mastercard, local schemes), banking partners, and regulators across all active markets.

  • Incident Management & Root Cause Remediation: Lead real-time response to complex or high-value fraud incidents. Conduct post-mortems, deploy immediate policy/rule fixes, and implement long-term structural remediations.

  • Metrics & Loss Budget Ownership: Own operational KPIs, fraud loss performance against targets, False Positive Rates (FPR), triage SLAs, and chargeback recovery rates. Serve as the primary operational presenter on 1LoD performance to risk committees and leadership.

Essentials

  • 10+ years of hands-on Fraud Management experience in fintech, payment processing, acquiring, or modern banking infrastructure, with direct experience leading operational 1LoD teams and holding loss budget accountability.

  • People Leadership: Proven track record of scaling, mentoring, and directing high-performing strategy and operational fraud teams in fast-paced environments.

  • Deep Domain Expertise: Comprehensive operational knowledge of merchant acquiring fraud, card issuing fraud, CNP chargebacks, account takeover (ATO), and cross-border payment typologies.

  • Card Scheme Mastery: Deep practical expertise in Visa/Mastercard dispute management, scheme monitoring programs (e.g., VFMP, VAMP, ECM), and payment gateway risk mechanics.

  • Data & Technical Fluency: Hands-on experience working directly with complex data environments and decision engine tooling (SQL, Python/R, real-time risk platforms, rule engines).

  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Demonstrated ability to drive operational execution across Product, Engineering, Data Science, Legal, 2LoD Risk, and external banking partners.

Senior Total Rewards Partner, Total Rewards

How you'll make impact

As Airwallex scales globally and prepares for its next stage of growth, you’ll own and evolve the Total Rewards agenda across compensation, benefits, job architecture, benchmarking, equity governance and pay transparency.

  • Own and evolve global compensation frameworks, salary structures, geographic differentials, market positioning, compensation cycles and financial models that support hiring, retention, executive decision-making and international expansion.

  • Build and improve job architecture and leveling frameworks that support organisational scalability, internal equity and talent mobility.

  • Shape regional and global benefits programmes, including plan design, annual renewals, broker and insurer negotiations, benchmarking and cost optimisation, while balancing employee value, fiscal discipline and local market requirements. Hands-on benefits administration isn’t the primary focus of this role.

  • Partner with executive leadership, People Partners and Talent Acquisition to turn complex reward data into clear recommendations, challenge decisions that conflict with business strategy, market data or regulatory requirements, and lead Total Rewards initiatives from scoping and design through implementation.

  • Support international market expansion by developing competitive, compliant and locally relevant compensation and benefits frameworks across global markets.

What we're looking for

Essentials

  • 7+ years of progressive experience in Total Rewards, Compensation, or Benefits, ideally within high-growth technology or fintech environments.

  • Proven track record of designing, building, and scaling global compensation frameworks, benefits programs, and equity structures in hyper-growth organisations.

  • Strong expertise in compensation strategy, including market benchmarking, job and salary architecture, geographic pay differentials, compensation cycles, and financial modelling.

  • Experience designing benefits programs and leading annual renewals, including broker and insurer negotiations. Hands-on benefits administration is not a primary focus.

  • Practical experience managing compensation planning and equity programs, leading system implementations or migrations, and working with HR technology platforms such as Workday, BambooHR, Carta, Shareworks or Pave.

  • Advanced analytical capabilities, with the ability to translate complex data and financial models into actionable insights and executive recommendations.

  • Proven ability to influence and communicate Total Rewards decisions with senior leaders, People Partners, and Talent Acquisition, demonstrating sound business judgement and confidence in challenging decisions that conflict with business strategy, market data, or regulatory requirements.

  • A builder mindset, with the ability to operate independently, navigate ambiguity, and develop scalable solutions across global markets and time zones.

Preferred

  • Experience in a late-stage private, pre-IPO, or recently listed company, particularly navigating equity program transformation, strengthening rewards governance, and preparing for public-market readiness.

  • Experience building scalable Total Rewards programs from the ground up in a fast-paced, high-growth environment, with end-to-end ownership and strong accountability.

  • Experience advising C-suite and senior leadership stakeholders on compensation, benefits, equity and rewards governance.

  • Strong analytical and financial modelling skills, including scenario modelling and assessment of financial implications.

  • Experience partnering effectively across diverse cultures, functions and international teams, navigating time zones and varying local market requirements.

  • Experience translating complex compensation, benefits and equity concepts into clear, actionable messages for business leaders, People teams and employees.

  • You're comfortable making decisions with incomplete information and moving quickly anyway.

  • You communicate clearly and directly across cultures, and you're thoughtful about how context shifts meaning across borders.

  • You know when to align and when to just decide. Collaboration isn't a way to avoid accountability.

  • You own the outcome and you don't wait for permission to fix what's broken.

  • You hold yourself to a high standard even when no one is watching. Quality and accountability aren't external expectations, they're internal ones.

  • You say what you mean. You're direct, but you lead with respect.

About Us

At algo1, we are reinventing one of the world’s most familiar experiences: the in-store grocery trip. We are building an AI-native product that understands each shopper, responds to their context in real time and makes an everyday experience less stressful, more personal and more engaging.


We’re backed by leading investors and founded by two entrepreneurs: one with a track record of building companies, and the other a recognised leader in data and analytics. Together, they have brought together frontier AI researchers and engineers, product and strategy leaders, and senior operators from major UK and US grocery businesses.


The people who join now will have an opportunity to shape the product, the culture, and what algo1 becomes.

The Role
We’re looking for an experienced, hands-on People Operations Manager to help us build and run the people side of algo1 as we grow.

This is a remote, part-time role, working approximately 3-4 hours each day, five days a week. There will be the occasional need to visit our London office to meet key colleagues. You’ll report to our Chief Operating Officer and work closely with our leadership team and hiring managers across the business.

We need someone who is equally comfortable handling the day-to-day essentials of HR administration and providing thoughtful, practical support on broader people matters. One day you might be preparing a contract, organising onboarding or updating employee records. The next, you could be helping a manager prepare for a performance review, working through a people issue or improving one of our HR processes.

You’ll ideally have worked in a startup or small, fast-growing business before, so you’ll understand that there isn’t always a playbook. You’ll know when to follow a process, when to improve one, and when to use your judgement to find a pragmatic solution.

This is a role for someone who enjoys getting things done, takes pride in the details and wants to make a meaningful contribution to a growing business.

What You’ll Own

  • People administration and employee lifecycle. Own the day-to-day people administration, including offer letters, employment contracts, employee records, documentation and changes throughout the employee lifecycle. Ensure everything is accurate, organised and up to date.

  • Hiring, onboarding and off-boarding. Coordinate the operational side of bringing people into and out of the business, ensuring contracts, checks, documentation and handovers are completed smoothly and people have a positive experience.

  • Right to work and immigration. Manage right to work checks and coordinate visa and sponsorship processes where required, maintaining accurate records and ensuring the business meets its obligations.

  • Performance and employee relations. Coordinate performance review processes, support managers with feedback and performance conversations, and help manage employee matters with appropriate documentation, follow-up and escalation.

  • HR guidance and compliance. Act as a first point of contact for everyday people questions, providing practical guidance to managers and employees. Maintain our people policies and processes, ensuring they remain appropriate and compliant as the business grows.

  • People systems and reporting. Own our HR systems and people data, maintaining accurate employee records and ensuring information is accessible, reliable and well organised.

  • Culture and people initiatives. Support employee engagement and wider people initiatives, helping to build a positive, thoughtful and high-performing working environment.

  • Process improvement and operational support. Identify opportunities to simplify, automate and improve how we manage people operations. Work closely with the COO on ad hoc people and operational projects as needed.

About You

Must Have

  • Relevant HR experience. You have a solid background in HR (or ‘People’) Operations, ideally in a generalist or standalone role where you’ve had broad responsibility across the employee lifecycle.

  • Confidence using HR systems, DocuSign and spreadsheets.

  • Strong understanding of UK employment practices. You have a good working knowledge of UK employment law, HR compliance and best practice, and understand when specialist advice is needed.

  • Sound judgement and discretion. You’re comfortable handling sensitive and confidential matters, approaching difficult situations objectively and communicating with empathy and professionalism.

  • A highly organised, detail-oriented approach. You’re methodical, reliable and able to manage multiple priorities without losing sight of the details.

  • An independent, hands-on mindset. You take ownership, use your initiative and are equally comfortable working through tasks independently as collaborating with managers and senior leadership.

  • Clear communication skills. You’re able to build trust across different levels of an organisation and adapt your communication style to the situation.

Nice to Have

  • Startup experience. You’ve worked in an early-stage or small, fast-growing business and understand the realities of building processes while operating in an environment where priorities and structures can change quickly.

  • Experience supporting UK visa and sponsorship processes, including Skilled Worker sponsor licence requirements.

  • A CIPD qualification or equivalent relevant experience.

  • Experience establishing or improving people operations in an early-stage business.

  • An interest in using AI and automation to make people processes more efficient.

How We Work
We’re a fast-moving startup, and we value people who are curious, pragmatic, organised and comfortable taking ownership.

There is flexibility in how those hours are structured, with a working pattern agreed together. You’ll need to be accessible during agreed UK working hours and comfortable collaborating virtually with our team.

We believe great people operations don’t need to be complicated. We want someone who can bring experience and good judgement, keep the essentials running brilliantly and help us build the right processes as we grow.


What We Offer

  • Competitive salary (pro rata).

  • 25 days’ annual leave (pro rata), plus applicable bank holidays.

  • A predominantly remote role.

  • A flexible, part-time working pattern across five days a week.

  • Real ownership and the opportunity to shape our people practices.

  • The chance to work with an ambitious team building an AI-native product from the ground up.

raw.title: Principal Product Designer: UX/UI
raw.description:
About Us

At algo1, we are reinventing one of the world’s most familiar experiences: the in-store grocery trip. We are building an AI-native product that understands each shopper, responds to their context in real time and makes an everyday experience less stressful, more personal and more engaging.

We’re backed by leading investors and founded by two entrepreneurs: one with a track record of building companies, and the other a recognised leader in data and shopper analytics. Together, they have built a team of frontier AI researchers and engineers, product and strategy leaders, and senior operators from major UK and US grocery businesses.

The people who join now will have an opportunity to shape the product, the culture, and what algo1 becomes.

The Role

You'll report to our Head of Design, who sets the overall design direction across our consumer and business applications, brand and website. You'll be our most senior hands-on product designer, owning the UX, UI and design system of our consumer applications, with significant influence over product direction.

We're building something with no established design playbook: a consumer experience that connects the digital and physical worlds of grocery shopping. The challenge is that a store isn't a website. Shoppers are moving, browsing shelves and making decisions in seconds. The store must remain the main event, with our technology playing a supporting role rather than competing for attention.

The hardest part is making this feel intuitive for everyone, from digitally confident shoppers to people who rarely use technology in stores. You'll need exceptional consumer mobile design skills, the curiosity to rethink familiar interaction patterns and the judgement to make sophisticated AI feel effortless.

You'll work closely with product, engineering and machine learning to shape what we build, not just how it looks. You'll have the opportunity to test your ideas with real shoppers, improve existing experiences and invent new ones as we build towards scale. Success will be measured by how much easier and more engaging you make shopping, not by how many screens you design.

This is a senior individual contributor role. You won't manage people initially, but you'll help hire and mentor the designers who join next, set the quality bar and establish how the team works.

How you work matters as much as what you design. We're agentic-first and everyone has access to max-tier AI tools, so you'll never be rate-limited. You'll use AI throughout the design process, from exploration and prototyping to design-to-code and QA, and help us discover better ways to build.

What You'll Own

  • Consumer UX and UI. Own the quality of our mobile consumer experience, from complex journeys and interaction patterns to clear, polished, production-ready screens. Make every interaction feel simple, intuitive and consistent.

  • Connected shopper journeys. Design experiences that move naturally between home and store. Bring digital discovery, planning and personalisation into physical shopping without distracting from the products on the shelves.

  • Product thinking and innovation. Work with product and engineering to define problems, challenge assumptions and shape the roadmap. Invent new interaction patterns where conventional mobile UX doesn't translate to the physical world.

  • The design system. Own the components, tokens, patterns and documentation that keep our consumer experience consistent as we scale. Keep Figma and code aligned, manage contributions and prevent design drift.

  • Shopper research and measurable improvement. Observe and test with real shoppers across different ages, abilities and levels of digital confidence. Use usability testing, product analytics and UX audits to identify friction, prioritise improvements and measure engagement and task success.

  • AI interaction quality. Design how AI behaves within the shopping experience: when it helps, how it communicates and when it stays out of the way. Make intelligent features understandable, useful and always under the shopper's control.

  • Raise the design bar. Lead design QA, accessibility reviews and critique. Establish effective AI-native design workflows, mentor other designers and make sure what ships meets the quality bar.

About You

Must Have

  • Exceptional consumer mobile design. You've led UX and UI design for a high-quality, complex consumer mobile product. Your portfolio demonstrates outstanding visual and interaction craft, including excellent hierarchy, layout, typography and attention to detail, alongside strong product thinking and measurable improvements to real user experiences.

  • First-principles thinker. You challenge established UX conventions, simplify complex problems and can invent new interaction patterns when existing ones don't work. You're comfortable balancing innovation with familiarity and ease of use.

  • Design-system ownership. You've maintained and evolved a design system in production, working closely with engineering on components, tokens, documentation, consistency and adoption.

  • Evidence-led product thinking. You combine user research, usability testing, accessibility principles and product analytics to make better decisions. You can demonstrate how your work improved usability, engagement or other meaningful outcomes.

  • Technical fluency. You understand modern design-to-code workflows and work effectively with front-end engineers to ensure the experience that ships matches the design intent.

  • AI-native mindset. You actively use AI tools throughout your design process, experiment with new ways of working and know where human judgement and craft remain essential.

  • High agency and ownership. You take responsibility from problem definition through to shipped experience, influence product decisions and maintain exceptional standards in a fast-moving environment.

Nice to Have

  • Physical-world experiences. Experience designing for retail, in-store screens, kiosks, connected devices or products that bridge digital and physical environments.

  • Front-end development. HTML, CSS or React skills, with the ability to contribute directly to a coded design system.

  • Product analytics. Experience with funnels, session recordings, experimentation and A/B testing.

  • Motion and interaction design. The ability to use motion, transitions and feedback to make interfaces more intuitive.

  • Early-stage startup experience. You've helped build a product or design practice while the company and team were growing.

How We Work

We’re a startup, so this is a high-intensity environment. The people who thrive here are curious, proactive, and love building. If you’re happiest when you’re creating, experimenting, and moving fast, you’ll fit right in.

We draw our energy from being together, so this is primarily an office-based role. It suits someone who enjoys the quick conversations and shared momentum that comes from building together. Our office is on what we think is the best garden square in London, just a couple of minutes from Tottenham Court Road, so it's easy to get to and a great place to be.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity.

  • 25 days’ annual leave.

  • The opportunity to shape a new consumer experience with the potential to reach millions of shoppers.

raw.description:
About Antithesis

We take cutting edge software-testing technologies and make them useful for finding real bugs in our customer’s software, allowing them to make more reliable software and ship with confidence.

Historically we’ve focused on the hardest testing problems, providing deterministic simulation testing of whole distributed systems, finding and helping people to understand bugs that would have been a nightmare to find in production.

As more and more code is written by agents, everyone is starting to realise just how important software verification is, and we’re in the process of expanding the problems and companies we target, and are providing an increasingly broad suite of open source and commercial testing tools for a much wider variety of problems and audiences.

We’re well funded, deeply technical, and committed to improving the quality of software across the board. If you’d like to help us do that, we’d love to hear from you.

About the Role

You'd be joining a small London-based team building out a new Antithesis product, focusing on a more downmarket and diverse set of customers than our main product. We’re rapidly iterating and expect to be shipping some time early in the new year.

We're looking for an engineer at the Senior to Staff level to help us make that system dependable. This will be “devops” in the traditional sense, though more dev than ops: You'll be a member of the engineering team, not a separate operations function, working in the same repository as everyone else, but your primary area of responsibility will be how the system runs in production. That means AWS, deployment, observability, alerting, and the on-call that comes with them.

There will be some on-call, shared with the rest of the team, and part of the job will be helping us define how that works. This is the first product Antithesis is shipping primarily out of the UK, and we want to get things right from the start to make it sustainable and quiet. We’re thinking of this role as less about being the person that gets paged, and more being the person who tries to make sure that nobody does.

Likely much of this will have already been prototyped by the time you join, but there will be a lot of latitude to make big changes to how that works.

What You'll Do

  • Own our AWS environment.

  • Define and build out our observability and alerting

  • Ensure our continuous deployment story is robust and stress-free in an environment where we expect to change production many times a day.

  • Build and maintain our infrastructure for our fleet of testing VMs for running customers’ code.

  • Take charge of our incident response and make sure we learn from incidents so we don’t repeat them.

What We're Looking For

An ideal candidate would have most of the following:

  • You have been responsible for a production system on AWS, including being on call for it, and you have opinions about what you would do differently.

  • Fluency with infrastructure as code and CI/CD.

  • Practical experience of observability.

  • You have built alerting that people trusted.

  • Experience operating Postgres: backups, upgrades, migrations, and what happens when they go wrong.

  • Solid Linux, container and networking fundamentals.

  • You are comfortable directing AI coding agents and skeptical of what they produce.

Bonus:

  • Experience running agentic systems in production.

  • Sandboxing or isolating untrusted code (microVMs, gVisor, or similar), or security work on a multi-tenant platform.

  • Being the first infrastructure engineer on a team, or building an on-call rotation from nothing.

  • Cost management for bursty, compute-heavy workloads.

  • Nix.

About Our Team

Our team spans CS degrees, philosophy, mathematics, everything in between, or nothing formal at all. What everyone shares is a high bar for engineering quality. We work primarily in-person because it's how we build trust and tackle hard problems together.

Location: This position is onsite, based in our London, UK office.

Visa Sponsorship: We are unable to provide visa sponsorship or immigration support for this position. Candidates must be authorized to work in the applicable country without current or future sponsorship requirements.

About Artificial

Help shape the future of specialty insurance

At Artificial, we’re building the next generation of technology for the specialty (re)insurance market. Our mission is to transform how brokers and carriers operate in complex markets by removing operational barriers and enabling smarter, faster decision-making.

We use modern technology to solve real challenges for some of the world’s leading brokers and insurers. By automating the repetitive and structuring the complex, we help our partners unlock new opportunities for innovation and growth.

You’ll be joining a collaborative team that values curiosity, ownership, and continuous learning. We work in an environment where ideas are heard, support is built-in, and outcomes matter. Everyone here has the chance to make a tangible impact on our products, our customers, and the industry.

In February, we raised $45M (£33M) in Series B funding from lead investor CommerzVentures, new investor Move Capital, as well as all existing shareholders. This investment round gives us the room to grow with confidence, continue to innovate, and ensure that Artificial remains the first choice for brokers and carriers seeking a smarter way to trade digitally.

Join us, and take the chance to be a part of something that will change the landscape of insurance for generations.

About the role

We're looking for a Senior Product Security Engineer to make our applications, and the platform they run on, secure. This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll work inside our engineering teams, review how our platforms are designed, find where they are weak, and help get them fixed.

Much of the job is setting up practices we don't yet have. You'll make threat modelling a normal part of how we plan and build, introduce vulnerability management across our applications and AWS infrastructure, and automate security testing at every stage of the delivery pipeline. We want checks that run on every change, so engineers find problems early and fix them in their own teams without everything having to route through you.

We're investing in AI-assisted engineering across the company, and we have a working group exploring where it helps us build better software. Security is part of that work from the start. You'll join the working group, set the guardrails and automated checks that hold every change to the same standard however it was written, and use the same tools in your own work.
