We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Why the Cohere TPM role?

As our Generative Machine Learning organization has continued growing, we are looking for more Technical Program Managers to join the team!

At Cohere, TPMs are pivotal to our success, being seen as operational experts specializing in cross-functional efforts. Great TPMs at Cohere are well-rounded, executing with precision at the tactical level, while partnering with senior leaders and shaping the big picture at a strategic level, and the opportunities are endless in growing the scale and impact of their work. Cohere’s TPMs would often be described as organized, execution-oriented, pragmatic leaders who are adaptable to the needs of the company and the programs they lead.

As a reward for the depth and breadth of expertize that you bring to the table, you will get to work alongside some of the most talented AI researchers and industry experts in the world on building cutting edge AI technology. No day will be the same as the one before, and the dynamic high growth environment will be absolutely perfect for anyone excited about solving novel problems, bringing structure to oftentimes chaotic and fast-paced environments, and ambitious about scaling their own impact and growth alongside the company!

Please note: While we are remote-first and accept candidates from all over the world, we are highly prioritizing hiring for people who are within 1-2 hours of British Standard Time (BST).

As a Machine Learning Technical Program Manager, you will:

  • Establish, improve, and scale foundational processes that allow the Generative Modeling teams to execute better, faster, and more predictably

  • Scale the operational capacity and effectiveness of the Modeling TPM team in collaboration with the Modeling TPM lead to ensure the function can remain lean and effective during a period of the program portfolio complexity and size continuing to rapidly increase

  • Flexibly adapt to the needs of the company, programs, and the team from tackling long-horizon programs that can span quarters or even years to jumping onto often highly ambiguous short-term challenges that can have company-wide impact

  • Partner directly with leaders within and outside of the Modeling organization on efforts to design, train and improve our core generative models

  • Lead cross-functional, oftentimes company-wide programs and strategic initiatives, collaborating and coordinating with cross-functional teams such as Product, Engineering, Legal, Platform, Infra, Policy, and Finance

  • Operate as an organizational expert in improving engineering execution rigor and operations on the ground, while contributing to the strategic layer in areas such as long-term strategic planning with senior modeling leadership

  • Map out dependencies and risks, and ensure that cross-functional execution across the program runs smoothly, communicating status with non-technical and technical stakeholders and senior management

  • Both own and enable a useful communication flow of priorities, ideas, and knowledge throughout and beyond the Modeling organization in line with your programs

  • Respond quickly to program-level changes, clarifying new scope, and managing resource needs in response to evolving priorities

You may be a good fit if you have:

  • 5-10 years as a Technical Program Manager AND 5+ years of experience working directly on AI/ML. Strong preference for candidates that have worked directly in building foundation models.

  • In-depth knowledge of machine learning, particularly when it comes to Natural Language Processing & Large Language Models (LLMs). Bonus points for experience with Multimodal AI.

  • Experience with working in a chaotic, fast paced, low structure environment. We need someone who is pragmatic, can roll up their sleeves when needed, and can function at the tactical and strategic level to do whatever it takes to make Cohere’s models succeed

  • Personal hands-on understanding of the unique challenges of managing projects and programs in the AI/ML development space as opposed to traditional software program management

  • Managed projects & programs requiring a strong general business acumen, such as coordinating with Finance on reporting needs or Policy on regulatory compliance matters — the broader your experience beyond ML technical program management, the better!

  • (optional, but preferred) Have technical experience in a hands-on capacity. We don’t necessarily need someone with hands on experience training models, but you need to feel comfortable sitting in the same rooms with some of the best researchers in the world, working on highly complex, cutting edge ML problems

If some of the above - other than the ML TPM experience - doesn’t line up perfectly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply! If you consider yourself a thoughtful worker, a lifelong learner, and a kind and playful team member, Cohere is the place for you.

We welcome applicants of all kinds and are committed to providing both an equal opportunity process and work environment. We value and celebrate diversity and strive to create an inclusive work environment for all.

Full-Time Employees at Cohere enjoy these Perks:

  • A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

  • Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

  • RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

  • 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

  • Annual enrichment benefits:

    Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.

    Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

  • 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

  • Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.

How and Where We Work:

  • Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

  • For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

  • For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

  • Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.


We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form, and we will work together to meet your needs.

We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.

Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an ----- or ----- email alias. Condukt is the next-generation compliance platform for financial services, offering an agentic solution powered by real-time data for business identity.

Always-on and policy-aware, Condukt enables financial institutions and fintechs to gain actionable insights into business verification - unlocking growth, increasing efficiency, and strengthening compliance.

We were founded by former operators and builders with deep experience in banking, payments, and lending. Today, our team spans across London and Porto, bringing together engineers, product owners, and operators from companies like Revolut, Meta, Block (Square), SumUp, American Express, Yandex, and OakNorth.

Trusted by leading regulated entities, including Wise, Tide, Mollie, Shift4, Flatpay, and myPOS, Condukt is backed by top investors, including Lightspeed Venture Partners and MMC Ventures.

 

Position Overview

As a GTM Associate, you’ll sit at the centre of Condukt’s commercial engine, generating new pipeline across financial services and working hand in hand with our Account Executives to turn it into revenue.

You’ll build opportunities from the ground up: reaching high-growth fintechs and financial institutions with well-researched outreach, qualifying inbound interest quickly, and running first discovery conversations. Your work doesn’t end at the first meeting. You’ll stay on the deal with our Account Executives, help build the customer relationship and, as you grow, lead smaller deals end to end alongside an AE.

As an early-stage, fast-growing company, we value people who take ownership, move with urgency, and are excited to help build both a market-leading product and a repeatable enterprise sales motion. You’ll work closely with our AI Deployment Strategists, Product, Engineering, and Leadership to shape how we sell, who we sell to, and how we win.

If you’re at the start of your commercial career, energised by meeting new people, and keen to take on more responsibility fast, this role is for you.

 

What you’ll do:

  • Own early-stage pipeline creation with fintechs and financial institutions that match our ideal customer profile

  • Research and map target accounts, identifying the right C-level Risk & Compliance, Operations, and Product leaders to engage

  • Help build and run our outbound motion, with sharp, well-researched messaging across email, LinkedIn, phone and events. Test creative formats beyond the usual sequences, and turn what works into a repeatable playbook

  • Respond fast to inbound interest and qualify every lead on fit, urgency and decision-makers

  • Lead discovery calls, support AEs on live deals and, as you grow, lead smaller deals end to end

  • Bring what you hear from the market back to Product and Leadership, helping shape who we sell to and spot new market opportunities

  • Pick up whatever the business needs next: priorities will shift as we scale, and you’ll help shape where we go

What you bring:

  • 1-3 years in a client-facing or target-carrying role, with a proven record of booking net-new meetings

  • Genuine energy for meeting people, and the confidence to pick up the phone, walk into a room of strangers and start the conversation

  • Resilience in the face of rejection, and the drive to keep going for the wins

  • Ability to learn fast, handle ambiguity and change course when priorities shift

  • Hands-on attitude, with a focus on outcomes rather than titles

  • Intellectual curiosity about the compliance space

  • Fluency with AI and data tools to work faster and smarter

  • Strong organisation across follow-ups, sequences and your CRM

  • Low-ego, collaborative approach and openness to feedback

  • Genuine interest in fintech and how financial institutions onboard customers and manage risk

  • Excellent written and spoken English

  • The right to work in the UK

Bonus:

  • Sales experience preferred, but not required for the role

  • Background in fintech, banking, payments, or lending ecosystems

  • Second language proficiency (German, French, and Dutch, especially valued)

 

Our offer:

  • Tackle meaningful problems with real-world impact

  • Competitive salary and equity package

  • Flat hierarchy with direct access to the founders

  • Hybrid, 3 days a week in our London office

  • Top-of-the-line equipment

We’re looking for a Senior Compliance Consultant to help our clients navigate regulatory change, horizon-scan upcoming regulation, and overcome regulatory challenges so they can transform their businesses and meet their strategic growth objectives.

This is a versatile, high-impact role at the intersection of regulation, client advisory, practical delivery and product strategy. Your mission is to deeply understand our clients’ needs and regulatory obligations, and to deliver solutions that help them achieve their compliance and business outcomes. You’ll stay ahead of the risk and compliance landscape, translating regulatory change into clear guidance for our customers and concrete requirements for our Product team.

Whether you’re shaping a client’s regulatory strategy or influencing our product roadmap, you’ll bring deep knowledge and hands-on experience of financial crime compliance, along with strong commercial awareness. Acting as an in-house consultant, you’ll connect long-term regulatory horizons with granular operational realities.

 

As an early-stage, fast-growing company, we value people who take ownership, move comfortably between complex challenges, and have the judgement to turn them into sharp, practical solutions. You’ll also work on long-horizon strategic projects, such as building government relationships and expanding Condukt’s global data footprint, where progress is measured in weeks, not months.

If you thrive in dynamic environments where no two days look the same, enjoy tackling a constant stream of new and complex problems, and want to help shape how financial institutions and fintechs approach compliance, this role is for you.

  • Produce high-quality, client-ready deliverables, such as gap analyses, risk assessments, onboarding and monitoring frameworks, policies and decision papers

  • Run workshops with client stakeholders, from compliance teams to the C-suite, turning discussion into practical next steps

  • Partner with Product to translate regulatory and client needs into the signals, data and capabilities we build

  • Contribute to business development and thought leadership with a clear, well-argued point of view on regulation, through proposals, client pitches, whitepapers, briefings, webinars and industry events

 

What you bring:

  • 4+ years’ experience in financial crime compliance, gained in a consultancy, a regulator or a regulated financial services firm

  • Deep domain expertise in risk and compliance, ideally across KYB/KYC, AML/CFT or business onboarding in financial services

  • A track record of advising financial institutions and fintechs on risk, compliance or regulatory matters, with a toolkit of structured frameworks you can adapt to a fast-growing company

  • Experience leading client engagements and producing polished, client-ready deliverables

  • Experience advising on vendor assessment and selection, including running or contributing to RFP processes

  • Proven ability to build trusted relationships with C-suite stakeholders, regulators and government agencies

  • Strong commercial awareness: you can turn regulatory requirements into solutions clients see real value in

  • A legal background, or solid working knowledge of financial regulation and how legislation translates into operational requirements

  • Sound judgement and tact in sensitive situations: you know what to communicate, to whom and when

  • The analytical rigour to dig into complex legislation and question established interpretations

  • A self-starter mindset that thrives in fast-moving, high-ownership environments

Bonus:

raw.description:
Meet DeepL

DeepL is a global AI product and research company focused on building secure, intelligent solutions to complex business problems. Over 200,000 business customers and millions of individuals across 228 global markets today trust DeepL's Language AI platform for human-like translation, improved writing and real-time voice translation.
Founded in 2017 by CEO Jaroslaw “Jarek” Kutylowski, DeepL now has around 1,000 passionate employees and is supported by world-renowned investors including Benchmark, IVP, and Index Ventures.

Our goal is to become the global leader in trusted, intelligent AI technology, building products that drive better communication, foster connections, and create a meaningful impact. To achieve this, we need talented people like you to join our journey. If you’re ready to shape the future of AI and grow your career in a fast-moving, purpose-driven environment, DeepL is your next destination.

What sets us apart

What sets us apart is our blend of cutting-edge AI technology, meaningful work, and a culture where people truly thrive. We’re a team of innovators, researchers, and creators driven by a shared purpose to unlock human potential by making work simpler, smarter, and more connected.

When we share what it’s like to work at DeepL, the reactions are overwhelmingly positive. This might be because of our technology that helps millions of people and businesses communicate and work better every day, or because of the trust, curiosity, and care that shape our culture.

What we know for sure is this: being part of DeepL means joining a team dedicated to innovation, growth, and well-being. Discover more about life at DeepL onLinkedIn,Instagram, and our Blog.

Meet the team behind this journey

Our Finance team plays a critical role in ensuring accurate financial reporting and supporting the business across our nine legal entities. The team manages the full spectrum of general ledger activities, working closely with Tax, external stakeholders, and colleagues across Finance to ensure a smooth and reliable month-end close. We value collaboration, accountability, and analytical thinking, with a shared curiosity to understand the story behind the numbers.

Your responsibilities

Month-End Closing (9 entities)

  • Own the month-end close for your assigned tasks, from posting to review, in line with the closing calendar

  • Prepare and book prepaid expenses and accruals, and maintain the supporting schedules

  • Prepare and book the CIT accrual

  • supporting of posting and reconcile bank transactions, and clear open items

  • Perform FX revaluation and currency translation, and prepare data for consolidation

  • Prepare and post manual journal entries in line with the approval process

  • Support IFRS-related postings (e.g. IFRS 15) in line with group accounting policies

  • Support local GAAP adjustments (e.g. HGB) where required for statutory reporting

  • Support the Tax team with VAT reconciliations

  • Perform balance sheet reconciliations and investigate variances

  • Run analyses of P&L and balance sheet movements, and explain variances to stakeholders

Year-End Closing & Audit

  • Support the year-end close and the preparation of statutory and group reporting

  • Support the group audit by preparing schedules and providing documentation and explanations to auditors

Collaboration & Knowledge Sharing

  • Work closely with Controlling/FP&A, Tax, Treasury, Procurement and the AP and Revenue teams to ensure accurate and timely closing inputs

  • Act as a point of contact for complex GL topics and share knowledge through documentation and onboarding of new colleagues

  • Review the work of more junior team members and provide guidance where needed

Process & Controls

  • Ensure compliance with internal controls and accounting policies

  • Keep documentation audit-ready and maintain closing checklists

Systems, Automation & Process Improvement

  • Work with our current ERP system and contribute to the implementation of our new ERP system (e.g. process design, testing, data validation, user feedback)

  • Use AI tools to make accounting work more efficient, for example for analysis, reconciliations and documentation

  • Identify and drive automation and improvement opportunities in the closing process

Qualities we look for

  • Hands-on experience with AI tools in your daily work

  • Tech-savvy, with an interest in digital tools and process automation

  • Degree in Accounting, Finance or a related field, or equivalent experience

  • Several years of experience in general ledger accounting, ideally in an international, multi-entity environment

  • Solid knowledge of accrual accounting, reconciliations, fixed assets, intercompany accounting and foreign currency accounting

  • Experience with NetSuite ERP and advanced proficiency in Google sheets skills

  • Strong analytical skills, attention to detail and a structured way of working

  • Ability to manage several entities and deadlines at once and to prioritize under time pressure

  • Proactive, communicative and comfortable working in an international team

  • Willingness to share knowledge and support colleagues

  • Fluent English

Nice-to-have

  • Knowledge of IFRS, particularly IFRS 15, 16, 9 and 2

  • Knowledge of local GAAP (e.g. HGB)

  • Experience with an ERP implementation or migration

What we offer

  • Diverse and internationally distributed team: joining our team means becoming part of a large, global community with people of more than 90 nationalities. We're more than just colleagues; we're a group of professionals with a shared mission to connect diverse cultures. Our global presence is growing–we've doubled in size nearly every year, with our employees based in the UK, Germany, the Netherlands, Poland, the US, and Japan, and we continue to expand our network.

  • Open communication, regular feedback: as a language-focused company, we value the importance of clear, honest communication. We value smooth collaboration, direct and actionable feedback, and believe that leading with empathy and growth mindset makes us better together.

  • Hybrid work, flexible hours: we offer a hybrid work schedule, with team members coming into the office twice a week. This allows you to engage directly with your team and experience the unique energy of our workspace, while still enjoying the flexibility and comfort of working from home. With flexible working hours and trust in your productivity, we are in sync with your team’s general locations and time zones to foster effective and seamless collaboration.

  • Virtual Shares - An ownership mindset in every role. We believe everyone should share in our success, and that’s why every employee receives Virtual Shares, linking your contribution directly to DeepL’s growth and rewarding you with a stake in our future.

  • Regular in-person team events: we bond over vibrant events that are as unique as our team, from local team and business unit gatherings, to new-joiner onboardings, to company-wide events that bring us all together–literally.

  • Monthly full-day hacking sessions: every month, we have Hack Fridays, where you can spend your time diving into a project you're passionate about and get the opportunity to work with other teams–we value your initiatives, impact, and creativity.

  • 30 days of annual leave: we value your peace of mind. With 30 days off (excluding public holidays) and access to mental health resources, we make sure you're as strong mentally as you are professionally.

  • Competitive benefits: just as our team spans the globe, so does our benefits package. We've crafted it to reflect the diversity of our team and tailored it to align with your unique location, to ensure you feel supported every step of the way.

If this role and our mission resonate with you, but you're hesitant because you don't check all the boxes, don't let that hold you back. At DeepL, it's all about the value you bring and the growth we can foster together. Go ahead, apply—let's discover your potential together. We can't wait to meet you!

We are an equal opportunity employer

You are welcome at DeepL for who you are - we appreciate authenticity here. Our product is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all succeed, contribute, and think forward! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our diversity that we will find the power to break down language barriers in the world.

From developing standout content to shaping larger brand campaigns, we work closely with internal teams, agencies, and creative partners to bring DeepL's story to life in meaningful and engaging ways.

As our brand continues to evolve, there's plenty of room to make an impact, challenge conventions, and help define what's next for DeepL's social presence.

  • Create standout content: Concept, produce, and publish social-first content across formats, including short-form video, motion graphics, static assets, carousels, and copy, collaborating with creative partners where needed.

  • Own social strategy and execution: Lead our editorial calendar, publishing, and channel strategy, developing creative concepts and formats that grow our audience and engagement.

  • Lead agency and creative partners: Manage our social agency, freelancers, and production partners, setting clear briefs, guiding creative execution, and ensuring consistently high-quality output.

  • Tell compelling stories: Turn product launches, technology breakthroughs, customer stories, and company moments into content that makes complex ideas accessible and engaging.

  • Stay ahead of culture and technology: Spot emerging trends and creative opportunities, and experiment with GenAI tools to push the boundaries of content creation.

  • Build and engage our community: Work with our agency and partners to foster meaningful conversations, identify relevant creators, and explore collaborations that introduce DeepL to new audiences.

  • Measure and improve: Use performance data, audience insights, and social listening to understand what resonates and continuously sharpen our creative approach.

  • Bring our brand to life: Collaborate across Communications, Brand, Marketing, and Product on storytelling and creative campaigns, with opportunities to contribute to broader brand projects as the role evolves.

Qualities we look for

  • 5+ years of experience in social content creation, creative production, design, or a related role, ideally at a technology, AI, or design-led company.

  • A standout portfolio showcasing social content you've conceived and created yourself, with strong examples of visual storytelling and creative execution.

  • Exceptional visual taste and design instincts, with a sharp eye for typography, composition, motion, and brand consistency.

  • Strong hands-on creative skills in design, video, or motion, with proficiency in relevant tools such as Figma, Adobe Creative Suite, or video editing software. You can produce polished content independently and direct specialists across other formats.

  • Deep social fluency and cultural awareness. You understand what works across platforms, what makes content resonate, and how brands can participate authentically in cultural conversations.

  • Strong storytelling and writing skills, with the ability to make complex ideas simple, engaging, and human.

  • Creative judgment and agency management experience. You can develop creative direction, brief external partners, give actionable feedback, and maintain a high bar for quality.

  • An experimental, self-directed mindset. You're comfortable exploring GenAI creative tools, move quickly, and enjoy building and refining new approaches.

raw.description:
Artificial Intelligence. Actual Impact.

At Docebo, we’re using AI to change how people learn at work—and we mean actually change it. We’re an AI-powered learning platform that helps organizations create, deliver, and manage training all in one place. But our real mission goes deeper: we help teams move faster, work smarter, and focus on the work that truly matters. Our platform is built with intelligent, time-saving tools that personalize learning, eliminate busywork, and turn training from a checkbox into a superpower. The result? Better experiences for learners and real results for businesses.

We’re shaping the future of learning with a team that isn’t afraid to challenge the status quo. If you're excited by the idea of using AI to make work-life better for real people–you’ll feel right at home here. And it’s not just what we build, it’s how we show up. At Docebo, our values aren’t just posters on the wall—they guide how we work every day. We call it the Docebo Heart: trust by default, assume positive intent, and create space for different perspectives to thrive.

So… what are you waiting for? Join 900+ Docebians around the world and help us reinvent the way people learn, because learning never stops.

🚀 The Adventure Ahead

As the founding Manager of Product Consulting, you will build and lead a trailblazing regional team of product experts who design directly alongside our Customer Account Executives. raw.description:
About the Company
 
e.l.f. Beauty's purpose is to make the world a better place for every eye, lip, and face. 
 
Our deep commitment to clean, cruelty free beauty at an incredible value has fueled the success of our flagship brand e.l.f. Cosmetics since 2004 and driven our portfolio expansion. In our Fiscal year 26, we had net sales of $1.6 Billion and our business performance has been nothing short of extraordinary with 7 consecutive years of net sales growth. This consistent, category-leading growth is a testament to the strength of our team, strategy, and portfolio of brands. 
 
Our total compensation philosophy offers every full-time new hire competitive pay and benefits, bonus eligibility (paid at 200% of target over the last seven fiscal years), equity, flexible time off, year-round half-day Fridays, and a hybrid 3 day in office, 2 day at home work environment. We believe the combination of our unique culture, total compensation, workplace flexibility and care for the team is unmatched across not just beauty but any industry. 
 
Visit our Career Page to learn more about our team: https://www.elfbeauty.com/work-with-us

Title: Director, EMEA Insights

Status: Hybrid

Department: Global Insights

Location: UK Office

Reporting Relationship: VP, Global Insights

Position Summary

e.l.f. Beauty is looking for a Director, EMEA Insights to join our dynamic, fast-paced, high-growth company. The ideal candidate will have a consumer and community-first mindset with a strong background in executing consumer research and synthesizing market data to analyze and articulate consumer trends and business impacts. This person is highly self-motivated, inherently curious, and strategic yet detail-oriented, with a passion for analyzing data, surfacing insights, and storytelling with data to drive business decisions.

The position will report directly to the Vice President, Global Insights. 

The Director, EMEA Insights is responsible for overseeing the EMEA-focused market and consumer insights functions, including market analysis, competitive intelligence, product insights, consumer research, audience segmentation, trends, and foresight, to drive actionable, data-driven growth through compelling storytelling. This individual will be adept at connecting dots across multiple data sources and strategically distilling and disseminating those actionable insights to all levels in the organization. This individual will be a thought leader and work collaboratively with cross-functional partners, acting as the voice of the EMEA consumer in making strategic connections between broad-based trends and marketplace opportunities. The ideal candidate is data-driven, results-oriented, has excellent communication skills, and is comfortable operating across all levels of the business, from strategic to tactical.

This position is based in e.l.f.’s London office with a hybrid 3-day in office schedule.

Responsibilities:

  • Strategically distill insights from diverse data sources and present them to senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams in a compelling narrative with concise and actionable findings and implications.
  • Leverage multiple data sources to connect dots and develop a comprehensive understanding of the business environment including brand performance, competitive brands and products, social dynamics, consumer behavior, demographic/audience factors, and macroeconomics, keeping a pulse on consistently evolving trends and foresight within and beyond beauty. Disseminate insights and strategic recommendations throughout the organization at all levels.
  • Leverage syndicated data tracking resources (e.g. NielsenIQ, Circana, Euromonitor, WGSN, Shopper Insights, Mintel, Spate, GfK) for frequent analysis of trends and identifying whitespace opportunities.
  • Lead the evolving EMEA consumer profile and audience segmentation initiatives across the brand portfolio.
  • Analyze social media conversations and trends, translating to actionable recommendations for marketing teams.
  • Own end-to-end creation of Insights presentations (e.g., PowerPoint), i.e., from storyline through final edits.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders in brand, innovation, digital, creative, sales, and Integrated Marketing Communications functions, surfacing insights and analytics to further promote and enable consumer-centric, data-driven decision-making in EMEA markets.
  • Develop and maintain relationships with external data and research partners (NielsenIQ, Circana, Mintel, YouGov, etc.), while consistently evaluating potential new data and research partners.
  • Drive the exploration and implementation of innovative research, trend tracking and social listening methodologies, including AI, to create next generation insights approaches and methodologies.
  • Partner with US-based Global Insights team to connect dots and unify insights that drive the business.

Requirements:

  • Minimum 10+ years of experience in consumer research, market analysis, and data insights and analytics, inclusive of experience leading a multi-disciplinary consumer and market insights team.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Market Research, Business Analytics, Data Analytics, Marketing, or a related quantitative field. A master's degree or MBA is a plus.
  • Strong ability to analyze and synthesize disparate information from multiple data sources into a holistic story with strategic implications and recommendations. Capable of turning complex information into simple and understandable messaging.
  • Adept at designing and executing multi-country end-to-end quantitative and qualitative consumer research (i.e., survey development, discussion moderation), with the ability to generate relevant and actionable insights connected to consumer needs and business strategies.
  • Experience with multiple types of custom research, including positioning, segmentation, innovation concepts, advertising/concept testing, consumer journeys, path to purchase, brand health tracking, etc.
  • Outstanding ability to navigate syndicated data sets (e.g., NielsenIQ, Circana, Euromonitor, GfK, Shopper Insights) beyond pulling numbers, to analyze and distill the most relevant insights.
  • Strong leadership skills with the ability to work independently and effectively across multiple projects, without sacrificing accuracy and attention to detail, in an extremely fast-paced environment.
  • Inherently curious, proactive, and enjoys digging beyond the surface to uncover insights. Exceptional at finding trends and the story in the data, articulating the “so what,” and translating insights into strategic, actionable recommendations.
  • Passionate about customer-centricity and data-driven strategy, with the ability to effectively communicate and influence key stakeholders.
  • Outstanding analytical, critical thinking, and organizational skills with extreme attention to detail. Ability to focus on both strategy and execution.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication and data story-telling skills, including the ability to clearly present findings and recommendations to diverse stakeholders. Has executive presence with a high degree of comfort working with and presenting to senior leaders.
  • Adept at utilizing AI tools for efficiency and enhanced deliverables.
  • Thrives in ambiguity, with strong prioritization and project management skills.
  • Localized knowledge of EMEA regions to surface local trends and execute relevant research.
  • Proficient in MS Office core suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook)
  • Experience with data visualization tools (Tableau, Power BI, etc.).
  • Experience using data analytics tools and languages such as SQL, SPSS, etc.
  • Consumer goods industry experience preferred.
  • Passionate about the beauty industry.
The base salary range for this role is listed above. 
 
Total compensation includes base salary, annual company-based performance bonus, and equity. Under e.l.f.’s annual bonus program, employees are eligible to earn up to 200% of their target bonus when company performance exceeds defined goals. In addition, e.l.f. provides a variety of other benefits to employees, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a retirement savings plan, gender neutral parental leave, and unlimited paid time off. The amount of total compensation (including base salary) offered will be based on a wide range of factors, including geographic location, experience, specific skills, and qualifications.
 
Compensation components are subject to change at the company’s discretion
 
This job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed in this position. It also reflects the general details considered necessary to describe the principal functions of the job identified, and shall not be considered, as detailed description of all the work required inherent in the job. It is not an exhaustive list of responsibilities, and it is subject to changes and exceptions at the supervisors’ discretion.
 
e.l.f. Beauty respects your privacy. Please see our Job Applicant Privacy Notice (www.elfbeauty.com/us-job-applicant-privacy-notice) for how your personal information is used and shared.

raw.title: Content Lead
raw.description:
Content Lead

Reporting to: CMO

Location: London (hybrid, 4 days a week in the office)

Salary: £80,000-£100,000 + equity

About Electric Twin

Most organisations make their biggest decisions on a thin slice of evidence - a handful of customer calls, one survey, instinct when the data runs out. Electric Twin changes that. We build synthetic audiences: simulations of real groups of people, grounded in research data. Teams ask them questions, test ideas and explore how people might respond, and get answers in minutes that would otherwise take weeks.

The work is grounded, and the science is real. We've run over 40,000 evaluations across populations covering 155 countries. Independent academic research with Professor Michael Muthukrishna at the LSE found our outputs come back roughly 10,000x faster than traditional methods, at 95% accuracy. Customers including The Times, Sage, Virgin, Vodafone and Wingstop use Electric Twin to bring customer insight into decisions about campaigns, products, pricing and strategy.

Electric Twin was founded by Dr Ben Warner (former Chief Data Advisor to the UK Prime Minister) and our CEO, Alex Cooper (a former senior military commander and Director of Mass Covid Testing in the pandemic). We're backed by Atomico, LocalGlobe, Mercuri and angels including Marc Andreessen. We're a team of engineers, AI researchers, behavioural scientists and operators - careful with the science, careful with the responsibility.

The role

We're hiring our first Content Lead to own content at Electric Twin, from the strategy through to what goes out each week.

Our ambition is to make understanding people a normal part of making decisions. Content is central to that: helping people understand a new category, showing what's possible and giving them evidence they can trust.

There's a lot to work with: research, founder perspectives, customer evidence, existing content, and scientists and customers with interesting stories to tell. What's missing is one person who sets the direction and runs the operation day to day.

You'll work closely with our CMO and our product marketer. Our Head of Growth runs the engine - the channels and programmes that reach and convert our audience. Product marketing and content provide the fuel. Product marketing owns positioning and messaging. You’ll take it, turn it into compelling stories and get them out across every channel.

This is a hands-on role. You'll set the strategy and direct agencies and freelancers, and you'll also spend a meaningful part of your week writing and editing.

What you'll do

Strategy

  • Own our content strategy. Take our positioning, messaging pillars and core messages, and decide what we turn them into, where each piece goes and how it lines up with our SEO, AI and PR work.

  • Shape the category narrative. Synthetic audiences are new to most of our buyers. Help them understand the category, see what's possible and find evidence they can trust.

  • Plan content across the buying journey. Earn attention at the top of the funnel, then build out the mid-funnel, where we have the biggest gap today, with content that helps people evaluate us. Know what each piece is for and what it should help someone do next.

Writing and publishing

  • Write and edit. Founder LinkedIn posts, articles, website copy, reports, campaign content and nurture emails. Make complex ideas clear and relevant to the people we want to reach.

  • Develop our founders' voices. Work with our founders, Ben and Alex, to turn their experience and perspectives into distinctive content, particularly on LinkedIn.

  • Repurpose and distribute. Take research, customer stories, product launches and product marketing insight, and adapt them for each channel. Work with growth to get them in front of the right people.

  • Run the editorial plan. Own the publishing calendar across LinkedIn, the blog and email, so everyone knows what’s going out and when.

Building the function

  • Build the content operation. Briefs, editorial standards, production workflows, approvals and a reliable publishing rhythm. Use AI to build repeatable systems for researching, creating, adapting and distributing content, while keeping it accurate, original and high quality.

  • Direct external support. Brief and manage our agency partners and freelancers, set clear priorities and hold their work to a high standard.

  • Partner with performance. Work closely with growth, bringing a good understanding of how content drives growth. Track how it contributes to reach, engagement, organic discovery and pipeline, and use that to decide what we make next.

Your first six months

  • Set our content strategy - building on our positioning, messaging pillars and the content we already have.

  • Take full ownership of the editorial plan, with a consistent publishing rhythm across LinkedIn, the blog and email.

  • Fill the mid-funnel, so buyers evaluating Electric Twin have the content they need to move forward.

  • Make Ben and Alex distinctive voices on LinkedIn, with a regular cadence of posts that sound like them.

  • Launch nurture email beyond product comms.

  • Get the content operation running, with clear briefs, editorial standards, AI workflows, and agency partners and freelancers producing work to a high standard.

What we're looking for

Experience

  • You've owned content strategy and delivery at a B2B technology company, and can show how your work helped build its reputation and commercial growth.

  • You've built or substantially improved a content operation in a fast-moving company where processes and priorities were still taking shape.

  • You've worked with founders or senior leaders, capturing their thinking and developing a voice that sounds like them.

  • You've owned channels end to end, from the idea through to publishing, learning and iterating. You've created content for awareness, consideration and evaluation, and you understand SEO, search intent and what works natively on each channel.

  • You've partnered with product marketing and growth, and briefed and managed agencies and freelancers. You have a network of freelancers and agencies you can call on to scale our content.

Skills and approach

  • An excellent writer and editor. You find the interesting angle, interview experts well and turn complicated subjects into clear, engaging content.

  • Comfortable with strategy and execution. You can produce a high-level plan on your own, then write the first piece yourself.

  • You've used AI to build repeatable content workflows, and you can judge when the output is good enough and when it isn't.

  • Careful with the details. You're comfortable getting to grips with AI, research and technical subjects, you ask good questions and you check claims carefully.

  • You take ownership and think ahead. You spot what needs doing, make a recommendation and see it through, and you give people time to contribute.

  • You're happy taking feedback and you make getting things done easy.

  • Experience producing video content for social channels including YouTube and TikTok.

What we offer

  • £80,000-£90,000 base

  • Meaningful equity in a high-potential seed-stage company

  • Unlimited leave. Take the time you need

  • Generous matched pension contributions

  • Private healthcare

  • Cycle to work scheme

  • Founding content hire with real influence over how the function is built

  • Direct access to and collaboration with world-class founders

  • Hybrid working from our London office (4 days in office a week)

  • Flexible working around life commitments. We value outcomes over presenteeism

When you apply, please share examples of your writing and a content strategy or operation you've built, explaining your contribution and what it achieved.

raw.title: Events Manager
raw.description:
Reporting to: CMO
Location: London
Salary: £50,000 - £60,000

At Electric Twin, we help organisations understand how their customers might respond before they make a decision. Our synthetic audiences let teams ask questions, test ideas and explore different possibilities in minutes.

Events are an important part of how people discover us, experience our product and build relationships with our team. From international conferences and exhibitions to private dinners, roundtables and partner events, we want every event to have a clear purpose and be delivered brilliantly.

We’re looking for an Events Manager to take ownership of our events strategy and delivery. You’ll help decide where we show up, what we do there and how we turn each event into valuable relationships, compelling content and commercial opportunities.

Why join us now

Electric Twin was founded in 2023 by Dr Ben Warner, former Chief Adviser on Digital and Data to the UK Prime Minister, and our CEO Alex Cooper, a former senior military commander who led the UK’s mass testing effort during COVID.

Today, we’re a team of more than 35 people based in London, bringing together engineers, AI researchers, behavioural scientists and commercial teams. Our customers include The Times, Sage, Virgin and Wingstop, and we’re backed by investors including Atomico, LocalGlobe and Mercuri.

Our ambition is to make understanding people a normal part of making decisions, helping organisations consider how their choices will affect the people who matter.

Events have emerged as one of our most important growth channels this year, and they’ll play an even bigger role in 2027. You’ll build on what we’ve learned to shape a calendar and an approach that we can scale: choosing the right opportunities, delivering memorable experiences and making sure every event has thoughtful follow-up and measurable results. And very importantly, building a delivery system that can scale.

You’ll report to the CMO and work closely with Operations, Partnerships, Sales and the wider marketing team. This is a hands-on role, with space to try new ideas and shape the approach as we grow.

What you’ll do

  • Shape our events strategy. Build and manage an events calendar that supports our marketing and commercial priorities. Recommend which conferences to attend, sponsor or speak at, and where we should create our own events.

  • Own delivery from start to finish. Manage venues, organisers, suppliers, stands, production, registration and on-site delivery. Work closely with Operations on travel, accommodation, shipping and other logistics, keeping responsibilities and deadlines clear.

  • Make every event feel like Electric Twin. Own the brief for what we produce and how it looks, from stands and signage to presentations, demos and supporting materials. Work with design, content and product marketing to deliver a consistent, high-quality experience.

  • Build the content around each event. Coordinate invitations, promotion, speaker preparation, photography, video and post-event content so the value extends beyond the people in the room.

  • Get the right people there. Partner with Growth, Sales and Partnerships on target audiences, guest lists, outreach and pre-booked meetings. Develop joint events that help us reach relevant audiences through our partnerships channel.

  • Drive event follow-up. Agree the follow-up plan before each event, then ensure contacts and conversation notes are captured in HubSpot, assigned to the right people and followed up promptly. Track progress with Sales through to meetings and opportunities.

  • Own the events budget. Forecast the full cost of each event, negotiate with organisers and suppliers, track commitments and actual spend, and recommend where to invest.

  • Report on results and improve the approach. Set objectives and measures for each event. Give the CMO clear updates on delivery, budget, risks and results, including audience quality, meetings, qualified opportunities and pipeline contribution. Run debriefs and apply what you learn.

How we work

We’re building something ambitious, and we like working with people who have ideas and get stuck in. You’ll find scientists, engineers and commercial people who are curious about the world, serious about their work and also happy to question how we do things.

We operate as a team, we help each other out and make sure we keep our eyes on the prize.. You’ll have room to make decisions and try things. We will learn together and keep improving. We also have an expectation that you’ll follow through and keep people in the loop. We care about doing good work - and we enjoy working together.

Your background looks something like

  • You’ve managed B2B events from planning through to delivery and follow-up, ideally within a technology or growing business.

  • You have experience across conferences, exhibitions and smaller hosted events such as executive dinners or roundtables.

  • You’ve helped shape an events calendar and can explain why an event deserves the time and budget.

  • You’re confident managing budgets, negotiating with suppliers and keeping several projects moving at once.

  • You know how to brief creative and content teams, and have a good eye for how a brand should appear in person.

  • You’ve worked closely with Sales and marketing teams on invitations, lead capture, follow-up and reporting.

  • You’re comfortable using a CRM such as HubSpot and turning event data into useful recommendations.

  • Experience delivering international events, particularly in the UK and US, would be valuable.

  • You know how to turn one offs into systems with AI.

As a person, you…

  • Are organised! You take ownership and everyone is informed and on track.

  • Are able to anticipate, spot what needs improving and are keen to make it better
    Care about the details, from the quality of a presentation to whether every guest receives the right follow-up.

  • Have sound commercial judgement and ask what each event should achieve.

  • Build good relationships with colleagues, partners, speakers and suppliers.

  • Stay calm when plans change and are happy to get stuck in on the day.

  • Enjoy combining creative ideas with disciplined planning and delivery.

If you’re curious, we we’d love to hear your experience.

raw.title: Growth Associate
raw.description:
As Sales Development Representative, you sit at the front of how Electric Twin grows. You decide which accounts deserve our attention, get us into rooms with the people who run insights, brand and strategy at large organisations, and hand the sales team conversations worth having.


You'll report into Sales with a dotted line into Marketing. Lead generation comes from Marketing, so there is a steady flow of inbound interest, event contacts and campaign responses to work. Your job is to turn that flow, plus your own account research and outbound, into qualified meetings that convert.


This is a broad remit for an Growth Associate. You won't just be working a queue. You'll own the territory map, decide where the effort goes, and build the outbound systems that make the next quarter easier than the last.


It suits someone early in a sales career who is genuinely curious about how large organisations make decisions, comfortable writing to senior people, and organised enough to run a patch rather than react to whatever lands in the inbox.

What You'll Do

  • Own the TAM map. Build and maintain our view of the total addressable market: who fits the ICP, how many of them there are, and where the concentration sits by sector, geography and company size. Keep it current as the product and the category move. This is the document the rest of GTM plans against.


    Identify and work focus accounts for ABM. Choose the named accounts worth a coordinated push. Research the buying group inside each one: who owns insights, who owns the budget, who feels the pain. Work with Marketing to sequence air cover and outbound so an account hears from us in a joined-up way. You will also own the ABM motion, ensuring the demand we drive on top of the funnel by sector is harnessed downstream and turned into leads. 


    Map signals to the funnel. Define the signals that tell us an account is in motion: leadership changes in insights or brand, hiring patterns, funding, agency reviews, content engagement, event attendance, competitor mentions. Then map those signals onto the funnel so we know where our ABM accounts sit and how they move through the funnel. You will co-ordinate with our growth lead to execute focused ABM campaigns for those insights. An account that has read one blog post needs something different from one whose Head of Insights has just downloaded the accuracy whitepaper. Getting that routing right is what ensures we deliver relevance at scale.

     

    Run outbound that sounds like a person. Build and run multichannel sequences across email, Lemlist, LinkedIn and phone. Write plainly, in first person, with a real reason for the message and a low-stakes ask. Test angles, track what earns replies, and retire what doesn't.

     

    Turn events into pipeline. Work with Marketing on the conferences, roundtables and industry events we attend. Build the target invite list, run pre-event outreach to book meetings into the diary, work the room on the day, and drive the follow-up afterwards so every conversation is logged and progressed. Events only pay back if someone owns the week after them.

     

    Set up and qualify meetings. Run first conversations that establish whether there is a real problem, a budget, a timeline and a route to a decision. Qualify honestly, including out. A well-reasoned disqualification is worth more to the team than a meeting that wastes an AE's afternoon.

     

    Hand over properly. Brief the AE before every meeting: what the account does, what triggered the conversation, who is in the room, what they said, and what good looks like from here. Stay close after handover so nothing stalls in the gap.

     

    Keep HubSpot clean. Log activity, maintain accurate contact and account records, and keep pipeline stages honest. Our forecasting, our signal routing and our marketing attribution all rest on what you enter.

     

    Close the loop with Marketing. You'll hear objections, language and competitor mentions before anyone else. Feed that back so campaigns, content and messaging reflect what the market is actually saying. Flag which sources produce meetings that convert and which produce noise.

Tools you'll use

  • We run a full AI stack and we expect whoever takes this role to get properly fluent in it, then push it further than we have.


    HubSpot for CRM, pipeline and reporting. Clay for enrichment, list building and capturing the signals that drive account routing. lemlist and Instantly for outbound sequencing and deliverability. n8n and similar workflow automation for joining the stack together so data moves without anyone copying it by hand. Claude Code for building your own tooling: research agents, enrichment scripts, briefing generators, whatever removes the repetitive part of the job.


    We'd rather hire someone who reads the docs and builds the automation than someone who arrives already knowing every logo on that list.

Your First Sixth Months

  • Month one. Learn the product properly. You get to know our ICP and sit in on customer calls and demos. You get  to know the current pipeline, the stack, and the ABM accounts already in motion.


    Months two and three. Deliver the first version of the TAM map and a shortlist of ABM focus accounts. Agree the signal set with Marketing and get the first routing rules live. Start running outbound sequences and booking qualified meetings. Own follow-up for at least one event end to end.


    Months four to six. Hit a consistent monthly meeting target. Have a repeatable outbound motion that isn't dependent on you improvising each week, signal routing running automatically rather than manually, and a clear view of which segments and messages convert.

What You'll Bring

  • Above everything, we're looking for a fast learner and a systems thinker. Someone who sees a task done three times by hand and builds the workflow that removes it, who is comfortable picking up an unfamiliar tool and having it working by the end of the week, and who thinks in terms of the whole funnel rather than their own inbox. The stack is only as good as the person wiring it together, and the right hire will take it several steps beyond where we've got it.


    Beyond that: you should be able to think about a market, write clearly to senior people, and stay organised without being chased. Some SDR, BDR or comparable commercial experience helps, as does familiarity with HubSpot or a similar CRM. Interest in market research, insights, brand strategy or behavioural science is a real advantage, because you'll be talking to people who do this for a living.

raw.title: Production Support & Monitoring Engineer
raw.description:
About Exegy

Exegy is a global leader in intelligent market data, advanced trading systems, and future-proof technology. Exegy serves as a trusted partner to the complete ecosystem of the buy-side, sell-side, exchanges, and financial services technology firms around the globe. Headquartered in St. Louis with regional offices in North America, the UK/Europe and Asia Pacific, Exegy has the global footprint to deliver world-class support and managed services to its customer base of elite financial market participants.

Job Summary

Exegy is seeking a highly motivated Production Support & Monitoring Engineer to ensure the reliability, performance, and availability of its production systems. This role involves monitoring critical systems, resolving incidents, and implementing preventative measures to maintain operational excellence. You will collaborate with internal teams to address technical challenges and optimize production environments. This position requires strong technical expertise, problem-solving skills, and a proactive mindset to minimize downtime and enhance system performance.

This is an exciting opportunity for a detail-oriented professional to contribute to the success of a global leader in market data solutions.

Responsibilities

  • Monitor production systems and infrastructure, ensuring uptime and performance metrics are met

  • Troubleshoot, diagnose, and resolve production issues in real time, minimizing service impact

  • Manage incident response, including escalation, root cause analysis, and post-mortem reporting

  • Collaborate with engineering teams to develop and implement monitoring tools, alert systems, and automated recovery processes

  • Analyze system logs, metrics, and trends to proactively identify potential risks or issues

  • Execute software deployments, configuration changes, and system upgrades with minimal disruption

  • Maintain and refine operational runbooks, escalation procedures, and best practices.

  • Drive continuous improvement by identifying areas for process optimization and operational efficiency

  • Participate in an on-call rotation to provide 24/7 support for production systems

Our Ideal Candidate Has:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent work experience

  • 3+ years of experience in production support, system administration, or monitoring role

  • Strong technical skills in Linux/Unix environments, with experience in troubleshooting and debugging

  • Hands-on experience with monitoring tools (e.g., Nagios, Prometheus, Grafana, Splunk) and incident management platforms

  • Scripting experience (e.g., Python, Bash) to automate monitoring and reporting tasks

  • Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills, with the ability to work under pressure in a fast-paced environment

  • Solid understanding of networking, system performance, and application monitoring concepts

  • Exceptional communication and collaboration skills to coordinate with cross-functional teams effectively

raw.title: Merchandise Planning & Analytics Analyst
raw.description:
Farfetch is a leading global marketplace for the luxury fashion industry, connecting customers in over 190 countries with items from more than 50 countries and over 1,400 of the world’s best brands and charming boutiques from around the world. Farfetch opens a world of luxury for endless expressions of style, delivering a truly unique shopping experience and access to the most extensive selection of luxury on a global marketplace. 

LONDON
Our London office is located in Old Street, London’s tech hub, and is home to a wide range of teams. Our open space is ideal for collaborative work and sharing ideas. We also have a large outdoor terrace, which is the perfect spot to have a team lunch or host events.

COMMERICAL
We're partnering with global brands and the most influential and renowned boutique curators to bring our customers an unrivalled range of fashion to empower their individuality. We’re relationship builders, we’re solution finders and we’re analysts. We work with all areas of the FARFETCH business to improve our social and environmental impact while delivering business success. We want to empower our consumers to buy better, improve our operational footprint, and explore new business models that improve our impact. 

THE ROLE
The Merchandise Planning & Analytics team supports the growth of key supply channels and brand partnerships on FARFETCH through commercial planning and data-driven insights.
As a Merchandise Planning & Analytics Analyst, you will support the team in analysing business performance, identifying opportunities to optimise supply and maximising sales. You will contribute to pre-season planning and in-season trading, while developing analytical tools and processes to support better commercial decision-making.
Working closely with colleagues across Brand Partnerships, Business Development, Online Merchandising, Marketing, Operations, Product and Business Insights, you will help translate data into actionable insights and recommendations.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Analytics

  • Analyse sales, stock and demand performance across brands, channels, regions, categories and products, identifying key trends and commercial opportunities.

  • Produce actionable insights and recommendations to optimise supply, improve product availability and maximise sales.

  • Develop and maintain dashboards, reports and analytical tools, working with BI and other technical teams to improve business visibility.

  • Support analysis of key commercial initiatives, including markdown optimisation, next-day delivery and exclusive products.

  • Present findings through regular trade meetings, business reviews and project updates.

  • Support with ad-hoc analysis and requests from senior management and business development

    • Planning

  • Support Merchandise Planning & Analytics managers in pre-season planning for key brand partners, using historical performance and demand trends to inform supply and assortment recommendations.

  • Refresh and maintain sales forecasting and planning models, supporting target setting and scenario analysis.

  • Monitor sales and stock performance against targets and forecasts, identifying risks and opportunities.

  • Identify supply opportunities and recommend actions to improve product availability and maximise sales.

  • Support ongoing forecasting and planning updates, contributing to the development of more effective planning models and processes


    • WHO YOU ARE

  • Collaborative, flexible and approachable, with pride in the quality of your work and an understanding that how you work is just as important as what you deliver.

  • Previous experience in Merchandise Planning, Buying, Demand or Supply Planning, Analytics or Consulting, ideally within the fashion or luxury industry.

  • An understanding of the fashion and luxury industry and its commercial drivers.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with experience in data analysis using large data sets .

  • Excellent planning and organisational skills, with strong attention to detail.

  • Commercially minded, with the ability to translate data into actionable insights.

  • Proactive and curious, with the ability to identify opportunities and challenge existing ways of working.

  • Comfortable managing competing priorities and working to deadlines in a fast-paced environment, ability to escalate challenges to management

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the understanding of how  present findings clearly to different audiences.

  • Technical skills for processing and analysing large amounts of data:

  • Excel (mid level) and SQL (preferred, basic level) .

  • Looker or equivalent BI tools (desirable).

  • Flexible Benefits Program

Broker Development Manager
raw.description:
About Flock

Road accidents kill and injure people, damage vehicles, and cost businesses fortunes. But traditional insurance does nothing to prevent them - it just pays out claims when they happen. At Flock, we’re changing that. Using telematics, AI, and real-time data, we proactively help our fleet customers prevent crashes. We obsessively focus on keeping drivers safe, and we put our money where our mouth is - paying out millions of pounds per year to fleets that get safer over time.

We were acquired by Admiral in May 2026. Now we combine the backing of the UK’s leading motor insurer with startup energy and speed. We’re growing fast with bigger plans than ever, and we’re hugely optimistic that our approach will save many more lives in the decade ahead.

We’re on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us!

 

About the role

Brokers bring in nearly all of Flock’s business, so they’re central to how we grow. As a Broker Development Manager, you’ll look after a panel of key broker partners with real growth potential, deepen the relationships we already have and build new ones as we move into new sectors. You’ll report to our Head of Distribution.

You’ll show brokers what our connected fleet proposition does for their clients: it cuts risk and cost and keeps drivers safer. We’re AI-first, so you’ll use AI every day to research brokers, prepare for meetings and spot opportunities across your panel, leaving more time for the conversations that win business.

 

What you’ll be doing

  • Be the main face of Flock for a panel of key broker partners and grow the business you do together.

  • Drive a high volume of quality submissions from your panel.

  • Grow the panel, onboarding new brokers quickly and getting them trading.

  • Find new ways to promote Flock’s appetite and proposition as we expand into new sectors.

  • Build data-led growth plans for each account and follow them through.

  • Support day-to-day trading so brokers win and keep business with Flock, keeping conversion and retention high.

  • Work with underwriting, product and other teams across Flock towards shared growth goals.

  • Use AI daily for broker research, meeting prep and pipeline analysis.

 

What you’ll need

  • At least five years managing broker relationships in insurance, with a strong reputation in the market.

  • An existing network of broker contacts you can bring to Flock from day one.

  • A strong understanding of the commercial broker market, competing carriers and how broker businesses work.

  • A track record of beating revenue targets and working well with teams across a business.

  • A consultative sales approach that matches Flock’s proposition to what each broker needs.

  • Pace and energy: you move fast, spot opportunities and solve problems.

  • Comfortable using AI at work and curious about where else it could help you win business.

Nice to have: experience building broker networks in Commercial Motor Fleet, an active broker panel in commercial insurance, or a record of taking new technology or products to brokers.

 

Benefits

  • 25 days of holiday (+ Bank Holidays) 🏖 

  • Share Incentive Plan 📈

  • Workplace Pension 💰

  • Private Medical Insurance 🏥 (including Dental 🦷 Optical 👓 & Mental Health 💆‍♀️ support options)

  • Various Salary Sacrifice Schemes - Holiday Purchase, Tech, Gym, Cycle to Work, Electric Vehicle, Private Medical Insurance for families 💵

  • Enhanced Parental Leave and Pay 🐣

  • £1000 toward relevant professional qualifications 🎓

  • £500 per annum towards learning and development 🌱

  • 3 days paid leave for L&D purposes 🌻

This role is expected to be field based rather than office based, working with brokers across Bristol and the surrounding region, so visits to client sites, conferences and broker offices count towards office days. As long as you’re meeting brokers consistently each week, time at our Central London office, a few minutes from Moorgate and Liverpool Street, can be weekly or monthly.

Making the world quantifiably safer takes more than good data. It takes a team where different perspectives are heard, and that’s a priority here. We insure fleets and drivers from every background, and we know a team built the same way makes sharper decisions and a better product for our customers. So we hire on merit, full stop, and we actively encourage applications from everyone. If you don’t tick every box, apply anyway. Just come as your genuine self: the qualities and experiences only you bring are exactly what we want.

Road accidents kill and injure people, damage vehicles, and cost businesses fortunes. But traditional insurance does nothing to prevent them - it just pays out claims when they happen. We’re on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us!

We’re an AI-first business, so whatever the role, we want people who reach for AI by default, stay curious about what it can do, and use it to work faster and think bigger.

THE ROLE

Engineering Lead for the Acquisition team. You’ll report to our Head of Engineering. You’ll work closely with the PM to lead the team toward its goals, owning delivery, operational reliability and developer experience. You’ll ship production code and provide technical coaching and leadership to the engineers around you, not line management. You’ll also shape how the team uses AI tools and coding agents to ship faster without lowering the quality bar.

WHAT WE THINK IS MOST EXCITING ABOUT THE ROLE:

Lead a team building products that directly drive Flock’s growth

  • Own delivery and technical quality for the Acquisition team, working hand in hand with the PM to ship features that directly impact how fleets find and choose Flock.

  • Write high-quality, well-tested TypeScript and own end-to-end delivery to production

Partner with product to drive impact

  • Work closely with the PM, the Engineering Leadership Team and stakeholders to translate business goals into clear technical scope, success metrics and delivery plans.

Grow engineers around you

  • Lead by example through code, design discussions and pairing.

  • Coach and mentor engineers across the team to raise standards and share ownership of technical direction.

Shape how the team works, not just what it builds

  • Drive improvements to developer experience, CI/CD, observability and release practices that make the whole team faster and more confident.

  • Make pragmatic trade-offs that balance reliability, performance and cost across AWS services.

  • Decide how the team uses AI, from coding assistants to agent workflows in review and release, keeping engineering judgement where it matters.

Curious how we build the future of fleet insurance? Dive into our Product & Engineering Blog, packed with technical deep-dives, behind-the-scenes stories, and real insights from the team you’d be joining.

A LITTLE MORE ON WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING:

As an Engineering Lead at Flock you’ll own delivery and technical direction for the Acquisition team, co-leading with the PM to ship products that directly drive growth, while raising the bar for the engineers around you.

API-Driven Development

  • Integrate with and contribute to the development of RESTful APIs exposed via API Gateway.

Serverless & Cloud Infrastructure

  • Use your AWS experience (Lambda, API Gateway, SQS, EventBridge, DynamoDB, S3, CloudWatch) to support and extend the Acquisition team’s services and pipelines.

  • Work with infrastructure-as-code tools like Terraform or CDK for provisioning and managing cloud resources.

Collaboration & Agile Delivery

  • Co-own the team’s success with the PM, jointly leading projects from scoping and planning through to delivery and measuring impact.

  • Give engineers the space and ownership to lead projects themselves, asking the right questions to challenge their thinking and help them land on the right solution.

Code Quality & Technical Standards

  • Deliver high-quality, well-tested code and act as a force-multiplier, raising standards through code reviews, pairing and design discussions.

  • Champion practical testing, type-safe APIs and pragmatic patterns that shape long-term technical direction across the team.

  • Set the example on AI-assisted development and coach engineers on where it genuinely speeds the team up and where human judgement needs to stay in the loop.

Working closely with your PM, you’ll bring clarity to complex problems and help define sharply scoped, impactful deliverables. Your success won’t be measured by your own output alone, but by the output, quality and growth of the whole team around you.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO FLOCK:

ESSENTIAL

  • Proven ability to co-lead a team alongside a PM, taking joint ownership of delivery, quality and outcomes, not just your own output.

  • Significant experience with AWS and modern serverless (Lambda, API Gateway, SQS, EventBridge, DynamoDB, S3, CloudWatch) or other cloud platforms.

  • A pragmatic approach to technical decisions, balancing reliability, observability, performance and cost, and bringing engineers along on the reasoning.

PREFERABLE

At Flock, we’re changing that. Using telematics, AI, and real-time data, we proactively help our fleet customers prevent crashes. We obsessively focus on keeping drivers safe, and we put our money where our mouth is - paying out millions of pounds per year to fleets that get safer over time.

We were acquired by Admiral in May 2026. Now we combine the backing of the UK’s leading motor insurer with startup energy and speed. We’re growing fast with bigger plans than ever, and we’re hugely optimistic that our approach will save many more lives in the decade ahead.

We’re on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us!

 

About the role

As a Senior Motor Fleet Underwriter, you’ll manage and grow a large portfolio of fleet business, using data and AI to assess risk and tailor cover to each client. You’ll help us move into new segments, including emerging mobility, as we build one of the UK’s largest fleet MGAs. You’ll report to our Head of Motor Underwriting.

You’ll work closely with brokers, mentor junior underwriters and help shape our products, wording and processes. AI is part of the underwriting process itself: you’ll use it to pull risk data out of submissions and triage cases faster, leaving your time for the judgement calls that need an experienced underwriter.

 

What you’ll be doing

  • Manage and develop a large portfolio of motor fleet business and contribute strongly to team targets.

  • Build strong, supportive relationships with brokers.

  • Help unlock growth in new market segments, including emerging mobility.

  • Collate and analyse portfolio data so our Head of Motor Underwriting can track performance.

  • Improve how we gather risk information from clients, so quoting and onboarding run smoothly for clients and brokers.

  • Spot where our policy wording and cover can improve, and raise it with our Head of Motor Underwriting.

  • Train and develop people in the Underwriting and Operations teams, and spread underwriting knowledge across Flock.

  • Use AI to extract and check risk information and speed up quoting, keeping your own judgement on every decision.

 

What you’ll need

  • Extensive experience underwriting motor fleet insurance.

  • A track record of building strong broker relationships.

  • Confidence working with data to monitor and analyse a portfolio.

  • Up-to-date knowledge of the motor fleet market and the curiosity to keep up as it changes.

  • Experience training or mentoring others.

  • Comfortable using AI in your underwriting work, and curious about where else it can help.

Benefits

We work hybrid, typically three days a week in our Central London office (fewer office days can be accommodated for longer commute times), a few minutes from Moorgate and Liverpool Street. Making the world quantifiably safer takes more than good data. It takes a team where different perspectives are heard, and that’s a priority here.
