offer.title: Head of People Tech, Data & AI

raw.title: Head of People Tech, Data & AI
raw.description:
Mission

Neko Health is a health technology company that opened its first clinic in Stockholm in 2018, founded by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne.

In one hour, our scan combines radiation-free imaging, heart and circulation measurements, and same-visit blood results with time to talk it through with a clinician, so people can act on what matters before symptoms appear. We design and build our own hardware, software and clinical protocols, and more than 100,000 members have already had a scan, with 75% booking and prepaying their next one before they leave.

As a team, we chase 10X, not 10%, and we’re looking for people who think the same way to help us scale what we’ve started in Sweden, the UK, and now the US. Join the clinicians, engineers and business builders making prevention a routine part of care.

Role Purpose

Our members' experience in the clinic is delivered by our people, so people systems and people data are core to how Neko runs, not a back-office report. This role brings People technology, people data and the AI tools our People function builds under one leader. You'll own the architecture of how it all fits together: our HRIS, applicant tracking system, a new ticketing system, identity and access, integrations, automation and analytics, across HQ, our clinics and several countries, and how all of it connects to the rest of Neko.

You'll lead a small team of HR technology engineers, people data specialists and product builders who already design and ship AI tools and automations used across the company. You'll work very closely with Corporate Engineering, People Operations and Payroll. Your team builds and runs the systems; you decide what good looks like and stay close enough to the work to tell.

Most of this is being built now, and the scope grows with every clinic we open. It also comes with something very few people in this field get to do: connecting people data to member experience, so we can see how staffing, training and performance in our clinics show up in member feedback and NPS, and act on it.

What You'll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months

• Set one architecture for people systems, data and workflows, with clear ownership, shared definitions and build-versus-buy decisions

• Build scalable workflows inside and outside Workday, including our new ticketing system, together with Corporate Engineering

• Create a trusted source of truth for people data, with self-serve analytics that leaders actually use and clear rules on who can see what

• Bring people data into executive and board decisions, from what we measure and why to how it is presented (Impact, not activity)

• Connect workforce data to the headcount planning Finance and Operations run for clinic openings

• Put a shared AI foundation in place, with privacy and GDPR built in, that teams outside People build their own tools on (Chase 10X, not 10%)

• Ship the first data products behind performance, progression and feedback, and the first measured link between people data and member experience (Member-first, always)

Minimum Qualifications

• Senior experience shaping people technology, people data or internal platforms in a complex, multi-country organisation, at a level where you set the direction, not only run the systems

• A technical foundation, from engineering, data or systems integration: you understand how data flows, how integrations work and how systems talk to each other

• You know HR systems such as Workday well enough to design around them and to direct the people who configure them. You don't need to have led an HRIS team or configured Workday yourself

• You are AI-forward in practice: you use AI in your own work every day and have put AI tools, automations or agents into real use for other people, and you can explain where they helped and where they didn't

• Judgement on data models, metrics and definitions, and on which decisions are hard to reverse

• You can take a technical picture or a data story to executives and turn it into a decision

• You have led specialists or engineers, and you measure yourself by what other teams can do without you

• Able to work from our London or Stockholm office 2–3 days a week

Preferred Qualifications

• AI in production, not only prototypes: agents, knowledge integrations, evaluation and access control for agents

• Led complex migrations or integrations across systems and countries

• A background in data or people analytics

• Experience with large shift-based or frontline workforces

• Built privacy and access rules for employee data from the start

Organization and Way of Working

You'll report to our Director of Rewards and Enablement, and your closest partner outside People will be Corporate Engineering. The team works on European time and meets in our London and Stockholm hubs.

About titles at Neko

We use a simplified internal title framework that prioritises clarity over hierarchy, so the title on this posting may differ from your internal title. We’ll be open about the scope and level of the role throughout the process, so you know exactly what you’d be taking on.

raw.title: Mobility and Compliance Lead
raw.description:
Mission

Neko Health is a health technology company that opened its first clinic in Stockholm in 2018, founded by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne.

In one hour, our scan combines radiation-free imaging, heart and circulation measurements, and same-visit blood results with time to talk it through with a clinician, so people can act on what matters before symptoms appear. We design and build our own hardware, software and clinical protocols, and more than 100,000 members have already had a scan, with 75% booking and prepaying their next one before they leave.

As a team, we chase 10X, not 10%, and we’re looking for people who think the same way to help us scale what we’ve started in Sweden, the UK, and now the US. Join the clinicians, engineers and business builders making prevention a routine part of care.

Role Purpose

We are looking for a Mobility and Compliance Lead to be the champion of mobility policy and compliance across Neko as we scale. You will make sure that everyone who joins Neko from another country, relocates between our locations, or works across borders for us can do so lawfully and with a seamless experience, and that the business is never exposed to right-to-work, immigration or cross-border employment risk.

This role sits at the point where detail meets people. You will get into the detail of immigration rules, relocation packages and cross-border obligations, and you will be the visible, reassuring face of mobility for candidates, new joiners, employees and leaders. When the answer is no, or not by that date, you will say so clearly, explain why, and show what the compliant alternatives are.

You will lead through ownership, expertise and influence, working closely with People Enablement, Rewards, Talent Acquisition, HR Business Partners, Finance, Legal and our external advisers.

What you'll do in the first 6-12 Months

Own mobility policy and the programme behind it

  • Run and oversee Neko's Global Mobility Programme day to day: company-initiated relocations, self-initiated moves, long-term assignments and business travel, applying the Global Mobility Guideline consistently and fairly

  • Partner with Rewards, who own the guideline, to keep it current, fit for scale and clear on the edge cases, including short-term remote work abroad

  • Manage the mobility process end to end: feasibility review, approval, vendor engagement, assignment and relocation letters, repayment agreements and post-move check-ins

  • Manage our immigration, relocation and tax vendors, brief them well, hold them to timelines and quality, and keep costs visible

Protect the business on right to work and immigration

  • Run pre-offer mobility and right-to-work checks with Talent Acquisition, giving a clear outcome before any offer goes out (clear, hold or stop) and a realistic earliest safe start date

  • Own work permit, visa and sponsorship casework across the UK, Sweden, Germany, Belgium, Switzerland and Ireland, and flag where US requirements differ

  • Keep right-to-work evidence in Workday complete and audit-ready, and track permit expiries and renewals well before they lapse

  • Give the business a straight answer when a plan cannot work, and hold the line on compliance even when timelines are tight

Manage cross-border compliance risk

  • Assess the wider consequences of a move or remote working arrangement: permanent establishment, social security, payroll, tax reporting, posted worker and business visitor rules

  • Work out how each arrangement behaves under direct employment and under an employer of record, and raise the gaps early

  • Consider both our HQ and Clinic populations, including professional registration and licensing for clinical roles and the impact of shift patterns

  • Keep a clear audit trail for every decision: the facts, the source, the reasoning and who approved it

  • Escalate complex or high-risk cases promptly to the Head of People Enablement, Europe, and to external counsel where needed

Create a seamless experience for our people

  • Be the front-facing point of contact for candidates, new joiners, employees and leaders: explain what happens next, who is doing what, and by when

  • Run kick-off calls and pre-move briefings, and prepare the documents people need, such as relocation letters, invitation letters and employment certificates for visa applications

  • Build clear self-serve guidance, FAQs and SOPs in the People Hub and the People Enablement SOP manual, so routine questions are answered without a ticket

Build for scale

  • Improve how cases are tracked, reported and automated with People Tech, across Workday, Ashby and our case tools

  • Report on the mobility pipeline, cycle times, spend and risk, so that leaders can plan hiring and openings with eyes open

  • Spot patterns across cases and turn them into policy, process or tooling changes

What good looks like

  • No one starts work without a verified right to work, and no permit lapses unnoticed

  • Offers go out with a mobility outcome and a start date that holds

  • Candidates and employees say the experience was clear and well supported, including when the answer was no

  • Every case has a documented, defensible decision trail that stands up to audit

  • Routine questions are handled through self-serve guidance, and your time goes to the hard cases

Minimum Requirements

  • Substantial experience in global mobility, immigration or right-to-work compliance, ideally in a fast-growing, multi-country organisation, or in an immigration adviser, law firm or mobility provider

  • Working knowledge of immigration and right-to-work requirements across several of the UK, Sweden, Germany, Belgium, Switzerland and Ireland, and an understanding of the US

  • Understanding of relocation programme design and delivery, including the tax, social security and payroll implications of moving people across borders

  • An analytical mind: you can read a complex case, find the risk in the detail, and build a clear recommendation from the evidence

  • Confident and credible with candidates, employees and senior stakeholders, able to deliver a firm no calmly, with reasons and alternatives

  • Strong problem-solving instincts and good judgement on when to escalate

  • Meticulous record keeping and comfort with trackers, reporting and audit trails

  • Experience with Workday

  • Fluent English; Swedish or another European language is an advantage

Nice to Have

  • Experience in a healthcare, medtech or other regulated environment, including registered clinical professionals

  • Experience managing sponsor licence obligations or employer of record arrangements

  • A formal immigration or mobility qualification

  • Background in process automation or people analytics

About titles at Neko

We use a simplified internal title framework that prioritises clarity over hierarchy, so the title on this posting may differ from your internal title. We’ll be open about the scope and level of the role throughout the process, so you know exactly what you’d be taking on.

In one hour, our scan combines radiation-free imaging, heart and circulation measurements, and same-visit blood results with time to talk it through with a clinician, so people can act on what matters before symptoms appear. We design and build our own hardware, software and clinical protocols, and more than 100,000 members have already had a scan, with 75% booking and prepaying their next one before they leave.

As a team, we chase 10X, not 10%, and we’re looking for people who think the same way to help us scale what we’ve started in Sweden, the UK, and now the US. Join the clinicians, engineers and business builders making prevention a routine part of care.

Role Purpose

Neko Health is scaling fast across Europe, and our People Enablement function needs to scale with it. As a People Enablement Lead, you'll own payroll and the employee lifecycle end to end for Sweden and Germany, including staying ahead of compliance and statutory updates as they land in either market.

You'll work hands-on inside our core People function, partnering closely with HRBPs, Talent Acquisition, Rewards, and Finance. You'll operate inside our Trigger/Approve/Execute model: HRBPs trigger and approve people decisions, you execute them with speed, accuracy, and a clean audit trail. We want a problem solver and a doer: someone who takes ownership and drives initiative, not someone who waits to be told what to fix.

We're not just talking about AI in People, we're building it into how the work gets done. Everyone on the team is empowered to build their own artifacts, skills, and automations: a live payroll reconciliation tracker, a scheduled compliance check, a dashboard that answers a recurring question before it reaches the inbox. If you can see the manual work, you're expected to build the tool that removes it, not wait for someone else to.

What you'll do in the first 6-12 Months

  • Own payroll and the employee lifecycle end to end for Sweden and Germany, coordinating with local providers on the published cutoff schedule.

  • Track and act on compliance and statutory updates across both markets before they become a problem.

  • Reconcile payroll inputs and outputs against Workday, catching discrepancies before payday, not after.

  • Own day-to-day administration of onboarding, offboarding, employee changes, and mobility cases across Sweden and Germany.

  • Coordinate right-to-work checks, relocation logistics, and entity/contract implications with HRBPs.

  • Execute approved Workday data changes, maintaining accurate records and a clean audit trail.

  • Build, document, and maintain scalable operating procedures and playbooks for Sweden and Germany, replacing manual workarounds with structured process that scales as Neko scales.

  • Build your own AI-powered tools and automations, trackers, checks, dashboards, to remove manual work in payroll, mobility, and Workday, and share them with the team.

  • Identify recurring queries and operational inefficiencies, and propose better ways of working, including where HRBP self-serve can take on routine data entry.

  • Contribute to the quarterly request-volume audit and SOX-relevant controls.

Minimum Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in People Operations, HR Operations, or HR Administration in a fast-growing company.

  • Hands-on Swedish payroll and HR/employment operations experience, at L3 practitioner level.

  • Workday experience, essential to this role.

  • Working knowledge of the Employer of Record (EOR) market, including how EOR arrangements affect payroll processing and compliance ownership.

  • Strong knowledge of employment law and payroll practice, and confidence keeping that knowledge current as regulations change.

  • A European outlook: you think across markets, not just one.

  • A strong sense of ownership: you drive initiative rather than wait for direction, and build improvements that scale as Neko scales, not one-off fixes.

  • Exceptional attention to detail: you reconcile, double-check, and don't let things slip.

  • Strong documentation skills and the ability to create clear, repeatable operational procedures.

  • Curious about AI tools and comfortable experimenting with them to remove manual work, even without a technical background.

Nice to Have

  • Germany or other European market payroll/HR experience.

  • Experience with implementations or transformations.

  • Experience building agentic or automated workflows into People processes.

  • Comfortable building from scratch, without established process to lean on.

About titles at Neko

We use a simplified internal title framework that prioritises clarity over hierarchy, so the title on this posting may differ from your internal title. We’ll be open about the scope and level of the role throughout the process, so you know exactly what you’d be taking on.

raw.description:
Company

Neuphonic is building the future of on-device voice AI.

We develop ultra-low-latency neural text-to-speech systems that enable super-realistic, human-like speech directly on devices. Our focus is on building efficient generative audio models and infrastructure that can run on CPU-constrained hardware, enabling real-time voice interaction without relying on large cloud infrastructure.

By dramatically reducing latency and compute requirements, we are making natural conversational AI possible on phones, embedded devices, browsers, and edge systems. This requires building high-performance systems that bridge machine learning, real-time audio processing, and distributed infrastructure.

Neuphonic was founded in April 2024 and is backed by leading B2B venture capital firms in Europe. Our customers include OEM handset manufacturers, chip manufacturers, and consumer AI companies building the next generation of voice-enabled products.

Our vision is a world where voice becomes the most natural interface for AI, enabling seamless, intuitive interactions that are accessible to everyone.

We’re solving challenging problems across real-time machine learning, edge inference, streaming systems, and ultra-low-latency infrastructure. If you enjoy working in a fast-moving environment and turning technical ideas into something people want to talk about, you’ll feel at home here.

Role

We’re looking for a Marketing Generalist to help build Neuphonic’s brand and grow awareness of our technology.

This is a hands-on role for someone who is excited about AI, startups and technology, and wants to work across a broad range of marketing activities. You’ll work closely with the founders and wider team to help turn what we are building into interesting content, campaigns and moments that get people talking about Neuphonic.

We’re looking for someone who is proactive, creative and highly organised. You don’t need to come in with a fully formed marketing playbook. What matters more is that you are curious, move quickly and are happy to take an idea and make it happen.

Your work will include:

  • Creating and publishing content across LinkedIn, X, our website and other relevant channels

  • Helping plan and execute product launches, open-source releases and company announcements

  • Turning technical work from our engineering and research teams into clear, engaging content

  • Coming up with creative ideas to increase awareness of Neuphonic and our products

  • Helping organise events, demos, conferences and other marketing activities

  • Supporting campaigns and identifying interesting companies, communities and audiences to reach

  • Writing case studies, blog posts, newsletters and other marketing materials

  • Tracking the performance of campaigns and content and learning what works

  • Keeping our website, social channels and marketing materials up to date

  • Jumping into ad hoc projects and helping wherever needed as the company grows

This is a broad role with lots of ownership. Some weeks you might be helping launch a new model, others you might be creating content from a research paper, organising an event or testing a new campaign.

You have

  • Around 2–5 years of experience in marketing, content, growth, communications or a similar role

  • Ideally, experience working at a startup and helping it grow or scale

  • Excellent written communication skills and the ability to explain ideas clearly and simply

  • A genuine interest in AI, technology and startups

  • Strong organisational skills and attention to detail

  • The ability to take ownership of a task and drive it through to completion

  • A creative mindset and lots of ideas for how to make technical products interesting

  • A willingness to learn quickly and get involved in lots of different areas

  • Comfort working in a fast-moving environment where priorities can change

In addition, one or more of the following would be particularly valuable:

  • Experience as an early marketing hire or working in a small, fast-growing team

  • Experience creating content for a technology or startup audience

  • Familiarity with LinkedIn, X, newsletters or other content channels

  • Experience with tools such as Figma, Canva, Webflow, Framer or similar

  • An interest in developer marketing, open source or technical communities

  • Experience helping with events, product launches or campaigns

  • Basic understanding of analytics and measuring marketing performance

Most importantly, we’re looking for a do-er. Someone who doesn’t need a perfectly defined brief before getting started, is happy to try things, and takes pride in getting good work out into the world.

Location: London (King’s Cross) - in-office role.

Benefits

  • Help us set the company culture - you’d be joining us as part of our founding team. Help us set and guide the company culture! Whether it’s breakfasts, reading groups or games nights. Give us your ideas and we’ll make it happen together.

  • Competitive salary and equity - we want to make sure you’re rewarded not just in financial terms but also have a sizeable stake in the business as well. We’re in this together.

  • Private health insurance - your health and well-being is paramount. We want to make sure that everyone in the company is supported when it comes to health.

  • Conference, travel and development budget - your development will also grow the business. We want to make sure that you have access to the resources and opportunities you need to be at your best.

raw.title: Research Scientist, Embodied AI
raw.description:
About Niantic Spatial

We are building for the >80% of economic activity that happens beyond the reach of screens. AI has learned from the text, images and video online, but it still lacks an accurate understanding of physical space.

That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.

In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.

Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.

About the Role

Niantic Spatial makes the physical world computable, helping people and machines collaborate safely by aligning how they understand reality. One of the fundamental problems we're helping autonomy teams and engineers overcome is the sim-to-real gap for visual-spatial understanding. We're applying our team's decades of experience encoding the world precisely as it is at Google Maps, Google Earth, and Niantic Labs to build the scalable real-to-sim stack for embodied AI.

Niantic Spatial's R&D Team in London is seeking a Research Scientist to push the frontiers of Spatial AI, advancing our Large Geospatial Model as a dedicated member of the Embodied AI group. You will invent and develop algorithms and systems that sit at the cross-section of computer vision, machine learning, AI, graphics, and robotics.

We're passionate about discovery, so we're looking for scientists who want to learn, publish, teach, and deploy every new invention.

What You'll Do

  • Develop New Spatial Representations - Develop new spatial representations that embodied AI can learn from, train in, and act on.

  • Advance Real-to-Sim Pipelines - Advance real-to-sim pipelines connecting real-world observations, 3D reconstruction, simulation, and robotic policy learning.

  • Solve Emerging Spatial Problems - Solve emerging problems that relate to spatial intelligence, 3D scene representation, training data, model efficiency, and interactive systems.

  • Take Capabilities Through to Evidence - Take new capabilities through to evidence: what changed for the policy, not only what changed in the reconstruction.

  • Build Prototypes - Build proof of concept prototypes, initially for internal use, where some will need to run at production scale on customer data.

  • Collaborate Across Research and Product - Collaborate closely with researchers, engineers, and product partners to bring novel models to production.

  • Publish Your Work - Publish and present your work.

What You'll Bring

  • A PhD in computer vision, robotics, graphics, machine learning, or a related field, or equivalent research experience, with a publication record at top venues.

  • Substantial expertise in robotics or embodied AI, including experience in sim-to-real transfer, domain randomization, policy evaluation, and simulation-based learning.

  • Deep experience with 3D scene representations: Gaussian splatting, neural fields, meshes, point clouds, or implicit representations.

  • You have applied generative or diffusion models to 3D data, such as scene completion, inpainting, relighting, or novel view synthesis from sparse capture.

  • You have worked on 3D semantics, open-vocabulary scene understanding, or scene graphs.

  • Proficiency in Python and Deep Learning libraries such as PyTorch.

  • GPU or graphics programming experience, such as custom CUDA kernels, shaders, or differentiable rendering.

  • A track record of contributing to widely used open-source research codebases.

Nice to Have

  • Proficiency in C++.

Compensation & Benefits

Base salary range of £103,500 to £202,500. Compensation also includes an annual bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package.

Location & Work Model

This role is based in our London office, with three days per week in office.

Inclusive Application

We know the strongest candidates don't always tick every box. If you're excited about this role and believe you could do it well, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't match every qualification listed - you may be exactly who we're looking for.

Equal Opportunity

Niantic Spatial is an equal opportunity employer. Individuals seeking employment at Niantic Spatial are considered without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, creed, age, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding or related medical conditions), marital status, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, or any other protected category under applicable laws. Niantic Spatial will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in accordance with applicable laws. Please contact your recruiter if you want to request an accommodation for the job application or interview process.

Candidate Privacy

I understand that by submitting my job application, the information I provide as part of that application will be used in accordance with Niantic Spatial's Privacy Notice for Job Applicants and Candidates https://www.nianticspatial.com/applicant-privacy-notice.

raw.title: AI Solutions Lead
raw.description:
Our Mission:

Omnea is the agentic operating system for procurement.

Procurement touches every pound a business spends, yet requests still stall for weeks and approvals get lost in inboxes. Our AI-first platform changes that: our agents capture requests, route approvals, onboard suppliers, flag risk and track every renewal, while anyone in the business can ask a question and get an answer grounded in their own company’s data. Buying becomes painless for everyone, procurement gets a seat at the table, and our customers have saved more than 100,000 hours of manual work so far.

Companies like Spotify, PayPal, T. Rowe Price, JustEat, Adyen and S&P Global run procurement on Omnea. We’re backed by $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners and Accel, and we’ve been named the UK’s number one startup in the Startups 100, ranked 11th on Sifted’s 2026 list of Europe’s fastest-growing companies, and recognised as one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies.

Talent density matters more to us than almost anything else. We keep the bar high in every team, so everyone here has real ownership and real impact. Our team is full of former founders and operators who’ve scaled unicorns, and we’re looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers alongside them.

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here.

The Role

AI is changing what it means to deploy enterprise software. Configuring a customer's procurement workflows used to mean weeks of manual setup, integration by integration, edge case by edge case. Increasingly, that first-draft build work can be directed rather than done by hand: AI agents can generate workflow configurations, draft integration mappings, and produce the initial pass on a customer's setup.

The job shifts with it. Instead of building every workflow yourself, you specify exactly what needs to exist, direct AI to build it, and apply the judgment AI can't: is this the right configuration for this customer's approval policy, will Legal and Finance actually sign off on it, does it hold up once real spend starts flowing through it. In practice, that might mean catching that the approval chain AI just drafted works perfectly for HQ, but misses a regional delegation-of-authority rule that would fail an audit in the customer's APAC entity.

As Omnea's AI Solutions Lead, you own deployment of the Omnea platform end to end - typically running 3-5 enterprise deployments concurrently - for some of Europe's most recognisable companies. You advise customers on the best-fit configuration, direct AI-assisted build work to get there fast, and validate every output against what the customer actually needs. You'll also deal with the politics that come with every enterprise rollout: the Legal team wanting one more sign-off, the Finance stakeholder who doesn't trust the new approval flow, the exec sponsor who's gone quiet. You become the internal voice of the customer, and you're judged on outcomes you can point to: time to launch, post-go-live CSAT, and whether that customer becomes a case study or reference.

This is an early hire on Omnea's customer team, working directly with our sales, customer, product, and engineering leadership. The future shape of the role is yours to define!

What You'll Do

Discover and design

  • Run discovery with customer stakeholders across Procurement, Finance, Legal, and IT, and translate their process into an Omnea configuration

  • Design the target workflow: approval chains, routing logic, integrations, and the edge cases that make procurement hard

  • On a deployment with a dozen-plus integrations, you own the sequencing - what has to land first, what blocks what - and the harder calls underneath it: which system is the source of truth for a given entity, and how records reconcile when two systems key that entity differently

  • Define success criteria and a realistic path to go-live with the customer's project sponsor

Build with AI, not instead of it

  • You're not just directing AI to draft your own deliverables faster - you're configuring the specialized agents Omnea's customers rely on every day: an intake agent that knows how to ask a procurement analyst the right follow-up question, a risk agent that flags what actually matters to this customer's Legal team

  • The real leverage comes from chaining agents together - an intake agent that hands clean, structured requests to a risk agent, which in turn routes into approvals with the right context already attached. You design how those agents work as a system, not just individually

  • Writing a spec for one agent is a skill. Writing one that holds up across a chain of agents - where one agent's output becomes another's input - is the actual bar here

  • Validate every AI-generated output against the customer's actual process, policy, and edge cases before anything ships

  • Handle what AI can't: judgment calls on ambiguous requirements, custom logic, and anything that needs a human read on internal politics

Deploy and prove value

  • Present configured workflows to stakeholders, from procurement analysts to CFOs, working through the pushback and internal politics that come with any enterprise rollout, and win their buy-in

  • Run multi-day onsite workshops with customers, coordinating dozens of stakeholders across multiple workstreams at once - a different muscle than a single stakeholder meeting

  • Project-manage the deployment: timelines, blockers, stakeholder alignment, and a clear path to launch, acting as an extension of the customer's team

  • Track adoption after go-live and keep the configuration working as the customer's process evolves

  • Work with Product and Engineering during the design phase, not just after something breaks in the field - you're often the earliest signal on whether a new module will hold up for an enterprise customer, and that shapes what gets built next

What's Different About This Role

  • You'll spend more time specifying and validating than building from scratch. AI produces the first draft; you make sure it's right for this customer

  • Writing instructions AI can act on precisely is a skill you'll build fast here. Vague requests produce vague configurations

  • Judgment matters more, not less. AI speeds up the build, but you decide whether the output is right for this contract, this Board, this customer

  • You'll keep experimenting as our AI tooling evolves, and share what works with the rest of the team

About You

We don't expect you to know how to do all of this on day one. TL;DR: you're ambitious and hard-working, as comfortable directing an AI agent through a tricky configuration as you are presenting a project plan to an exec. You make up for any gap in experience with hunger and a genuine growth mindset. You derive energy from building relationships, shipping projects, and making customers succeed.

The CSE team sits between Customer, Product and Engineering. It's a small, close-knit team with a lot of autonomy, and the scope of the role grows as Omnea does.   • Build and run programmes for new leads, leads sales has passed back, closed-lost deals, and event and webinar follow-up

  • Keep the database healthy: segmentation, enrichment, consent across the UK, EU, and US, and deliverability

  • Report what each programme returns in meetings and pipeline, rather than opens

You'll work with RevOps so the right people reach the right seller quickly, and everyone else goes into nurture.

  • Agree with sales and RevOps what counts as a qualified meeting, who follows up, and by when

  • Build fit and engagement scoring with a clear threshold for alerting sellers, while demo requests always go straight to sales

  • Help set routing rules by territory and account owner, so every demo request reaches the right rep

  • Review lead quality with the sales team every week, and recalibrate scoring every quarter against the deals we win

  • Report conversion and drop-off at each stage of the funnel

  • Run experiments, call the results, and stop the ones that aren't working

  • Join quarterly planning sessions with the marketing team to choose the bigger moments we put our weight behind, then own their delivery

  • Pick up what the quarter needs most, whether that's a paid test, a landing page, or a LinkedIn campaign

  • You're commercial. You think in meetings and pipeline, and you can tell the difference between a programme that's busy and one that's working.

  • You've worked on account-based or event-led programmes. You can walk us through one, from the accounts you chose to the meetings it produced.

  • Experience with tools like Clay, Dreamdata, Userled, or gifting platforms

Overview

We're looking for an exceptional Security Associate to join our Platform Engineering team at Omnea!

This is a great opportunity for someone early in their career who's smart, technically curious and excited to get hands-on with how a fast-growing technology company operates behind the scenes.

You'll be embedded in our Platform Engineering team and collaborate closely with our Operations team to help manage the security, IT infrastructure and compliance processes that keep Omnea running smoothly and securely. From managing our internal IT systems and device fleet to coordinating security audits and working with external auditors, you'll play an important role in ensuring we can scale without compromising on security.

You don't need to be an engineer to join us. We're looking for someone who's comfortable with technology, loves solving problems, and is excited to learn. You'll gain first-hand exposure to the systems, infrastructure and security practices behind a fast-growing enterprise SaaS business, with a pathway to take on more technical responsibilities and grow into Platform Engineering over time.

This is a rare opportunity to learn directly from an experienced engineering team, build a strong technical foundation and make a meaningful impact at one of Europe's fastest-growing startups.

What you can expect

  • Own the day-to-day of security and compliance: You'll help us manage our security and compliance programmes, including SOC 1, SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR and other certifications and frameworks as we grow. You'll be responsible for keeping documentation, evidence and controls up to date, and making sure we're always prepared for the next audit.

  • Become a GRC expert: You'll work extensively with Vanta, our compliance automation platform, monitoring controls, investigating issues, collecting evidence and coordinating with teams across the business to keep us compliant. You'll look for opportunities to automate repetitive tasks and improve how we manage our compliance processes.

  • Help manage our IT systems and devices: You'll support internal IT operations, including laptop provisioning, device fleet management, access controls and employee onboarding and offboarding. You'll get hands-on experience with the tools and systems that support a growing team.

  • Work with auditors and external partners: You'll help coordinate our security audits, manage relationships with external auditors and compliance partners, respond to evidence requests and keep audit projects moving forward. You'll also work with teams across Omnea to ensure we're meeting our security commitments.

  • Improve and automate how we work: We're scaling quickly, and processes that work for 50 people don't necessarily work for 200+. You'll identify inefficiencies, improve our internal workflows and find ways to use technology and automation to make our security and IT operations more scalable.

  • Learn from our Platform Engineering team: You'll work alongside an exceptional team responsible for Omnea's infrastructure, security and developer experience. As you build your knowledge and technical skills, you'll have opportunities to get involved in increasingly technical projects, with a potential pathway into Platform Engineering.

You'll get exposure to a wide range of technologies, work directly with experienced engineers and learn by doing. We don't expect you to know how everything works when you join!

About you

We're looking for someone intelligent, curious and incredibly resourceful. You might be a recent graduate, have a couple of years of experience in a technical or operational role, or be looking to transition into a career in technology.

What matters most is your ability to learn quickly, figure things out independently and take pride in getting the details right.

  • You're smart and a natural problem-solver: You can get your head around unfamiliar problems, work things out for yourself and aren't afraid to dive into something you've never done before. You've got a track record of performing exceptionally well, whether that's academically, professionally or elsewhere.

  • You're technical for a non-technical person: You're comfortable using new software, understanding how different systems work and troubleshooting when something breaks. You might have taught yourself to code, built something using APIs or automation tools, or just be the person everyone comes to when they need help with technology. You don't need an engineering background, but you do need a genuine interest in technology.

  • You're incredibly organised and detail-oriented: You enjoy making sure things are properly documented, processes are followed and nothing slips through the cracks. You can juggle multiple workstreams and take satisfaction in knowing everything is in good shape.

  • You're a strong communicator: You'll work with engineers, employees across the business and external auditors. You can communicate clearly, follow up effectively and build good working relationships with different types of people.

raw.description:
About the team

The AI Deployment Engineering team works closely with frontier startups. We are trusted advisors to, and thought partners with, startups to ensure that OpenAI’s technology is deployed safely and effectively, whilst also partnering with engineering, research, and product to turn those insights into evaluation systems, product improvements, and better model behavior.

This team sits at the intersection of customer reality and model quality. We combine hands-on technical depth with strong product judgment, helping translate complex, high-value use cases into clear signals that can improve both the customer experience and the underlying systems.

About the role

We are seeking a technically proficient, product-minded engineer to help push the frontier of advanced AI with our strategic startup customers. You'll work with some of the most exciting AI startups in the world, helping them optimize their own systems and turning those learnings into durable improvements across OpenAI’s research and products. You will partner deeply on complex workflows, identify the gaps that matter, and help transform those gaps into reproducible evaluations, technical insights - helping shape OpenAI's research and product direction.

This role is well suited to engineers who are equally comfortable debugging a workflow, iterating on prompts or agents, designing evaluations, and collaborating across research and product. You should be excited by ambiguous, high-impact problems and motivated by the opportunity to shape how advanced AI systems improve in practice.

This role is based in Israel. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance.

In this role, you will:

  • Work directly with strategic startup customers to understand critical workflows, uncover failure modes, and identify high-impact opportunities for improvement.

  • Prototype and iterate on prompts, agents, and workflow designs to better understand system behavior and unlock customer value.

  • Synthesize and deliver valuable feedback to the Product and Research teams, turning real usage patterns into clear, reproducible evals, benchmarks, and technical artifacts that improve model and product quality and ensure customer-grounded learnings influence roadmap and model development.

  • Build repeatable tools, patterns, and evaluation approaches that raise the quality bar across multiple use cases.

  • Operate with strong judgment in ambiguous environments, balancing immediate technical problem-solving with longer-term system improvement.

  • Build relationships within the startup ecosystem, serving as a technical partner to both individual customers and the broader community.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

  • Have strong software engineering & AI fundamentals. For example, experience as a startup CTO, software engineer, ML engineer, Data Scientist or equivalent. Experience shipping production systems end-to-end is a strong plus.

  • Have experience as a technical founder, or engineer at an early stage startup

  • Have familiarity with, or interest in, model training pipelines and reinforcement learning.

  • Have experience building AI applications, agents, or evaluation systems, and can reason clearly about model behavior in complex workflows.

  • Are comfortable working directly with highly technical users and translating their challenges into concrete technical signals.

  • Can move fluidly between prototyping, debugging, evaluation design, and cross-functional collaboration.

  • Communicate clearly across technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Bring high agency, strong product sense, and a bias toward building durable improvements rather than one-off fixes

We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

raw.title: Deployment Lead, Semiconductors - London
raw.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team turns research breakthroughs into production-grade systems. We embed deeply with customers to solve high-leverage problems and act as the delivery engine for our most complex large-scale engagements. We move quickly from prototype to production and surface reusable patterns that shape our platform. We operate at the intersection of deployment and development – working closely with OpenAI Research, Product and Partnerships.

About the Role

As a Deployment Lead, you will define how OpenAI delivers complex systems to Semiconductor customers. You will own how solutions are scoped, built, shipped, and adopted across high-value engineering workflows such as RTL design, verification, and physical implementation. You’ll translate business outcomes into a technical plan, run day-to-day execution across FDEs, Researchers, and Customer Engineers, and partner with customer teams to ensure delivery supports their goals.

You will focus on the semiconductor vertical to deploy next-generation AI capabilities. You will own delivery end-to-end: embedding with customers to map workflows and success criteria, ensuring components ship on time, and leading readiness and change management for adoption. You’ll track progress, manage dependencies, make sequencing decisions, and drive 0→1 prototypes through MVP and scale. You will also share field insights with Product and Research to guide roadmap and priorities.

Success will be measured first and foremost by impact - deployments that deliver measurable value against customer goals, drive adoption, and become critical to their workflows. Additional measures of success include delivery reliability (milestones hit, low reopen/churn), operating leverage (patterns reused across deployments), judgment under pressure, and product impact (field signal that shifts roadmaps/architectures).

This is a high-trust, high-autonomy role. Success requires deep technical project management expertise, extreme ownership of outcomes, and an ability to immerse in customer workflows and partner with customer teams to solve complex engineering problems at pace.

This role is based in London. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel between 25-50% is required.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the technical delivery plan for multiple interdependent work streams, translating customer objectives into a roadmap with milestones, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.

  • Run day-to-day engineering execution by tracking and driving delivery across OpenAI FDE and customer teams. Keep progress unblocked and sequenced. Make real-time trade-offs on scope and priority to protect the critical path.

  • Embed with Semiconductor customer teams to land production deployments and drive adoption. Map workflows, shape tools/integrations, and translate requirements into a delivery plan.

  • Shape production deployments that integrate with customer infrastructure, data systems, and engineering toolchains, including export-controlled environments.

  • Partner with Product and Research so platform components and research work streams land in time to support deployment goals.

  • Codify solution patterns and evals. Extract reusable patterns and package field signals to improve product and models.

  • Own value cases and ROI. Set impact hypotheses, baselines, and KPIs; run pre-/post-deployment measurement and report to exec sponsors.

  • Help define how OpenAI engages Semiconductor customers.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Bring 7+ years of customer‑facing technical delivery leadership.

  • Have deep expertise in Semiconductor workflows, including RTL design, verification, EDA tooling, and physical implementation.

  • Track record of successfully leading large, complex, high-stakes customer engagements where customer outcomes depended on tight coordination and fast decision making, ideally involving AI.

  • Excel in high ambiguity environments. Know how to simplify complex and dynamic work.

  • Move fluidly between system level understanding and execution level detail; can dive into customer workflows/data, map constraints, sketch architectures and move ambiguous problems to shipped systems.

  • Think strategically and pattern-match. Able to step back from execution detail, recognize broader trends across deployments, and connect customer needs to scalable, reusable solutions.

  • Have strong technical fluency and sharp sequencing instincts. Confident discussing technical details, pressure-testing architectures, and making trade-offs.

  • Have shipped AI/LLM systems. You understand solution patterns, integration basics, and production pitfalls.

  • You’re a translator with executive presence. You make complex technical trade-offs legible to business leaders and convert strategy into day-to-day technical execution.

  • Enjoy being onsite with customers to accelerate delivery (often 25-50%, sometimes higher).

raw.title: Enablement Lead, Government
raw.description:
About the Team

The Adoption, Innovation, and Transformation team within OpenAI for Government helps government organizations turn OpenAI products into durable capabilities and measurable mission impact.

We work alongside public servants to move from initial exploration to confident, responsible, organization-wide use of AI. Our work combines hands-on enablement, adoption strategy, deployment support, community, content, and practical transformation tailored to government missions and operating environments.

By translating the potential of OpenAI’s technology into better individual workflows, stronger teams, and improved public services, we help government customers deepen adoption, build lasting organizational capability, and spend more time on mission.

About the Role

The Enablement Lead, Government is a specialist role focused on delivering high-impact enablement and adoption services across OpenAI’s product suite. This role is responsible for designing and delivering experiences that support repeatable adoption frameworks, drive sustained activation, expand the breadth and depth of usage, and produce measurable value for government organizations.

This role sits at the intersection of enablement, education, adoption, community, content, and customer experience. It blends strong product fluency, instructional design, customer advisory, and a deep understanding of public service. You will lead live workshops, deliver enablement programs, and design adoption interventions for audiences ranging from front-line public servants and technical practitioners to senior government leaders.

You will be a trusted guide to government customers, helping them learn, share, teach, celebrate successes, and use AI confidently in their day-to-day work. You will help organizations understand not only what OpenAI’s products can do, but how to apply them safely and effectively while respecting their missions, operating environments, workforce needs, and responsibilities to the public.

Success in this role means accelerating customer confidence, increasing product adoption, supporting successful launches and deployments, and helping government organizations translate product capabilities into tangible mission outcomes. You will own outcomes related to activation and sustained usage while helping shape how OpenAI enables and supports public-sector customers at scale.

This role is based in London. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. Travel and regular work from government customer sites are required.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the enablement of OpenAI products, including ChatGPT Enterprise and Agents, helping define effective patterns for responsible adoption across government organizations.

  • Lead government customers through the full enablement lifecycle, from initial onboarding and activation through expansion, optimization, and long-term adoption.

  • Define and manage structured enablement and deployment programs with clear goals, milestones, owners, and measures of success.

  • Design and deliver high-impact engagements—including onboarding sessions, advanced capability training, executive briefings, academies, hackathons, listening sessions, and hands-on mission or workflow labs—for audiences ranging from senior leaders to front-line staff.

  • Guide government leaders, champions, technical teams, and working teams through organizational change by building confidence, establishing effective habits, and translating product capabilities into practical workflows and mission outcomes.

  • Serve as a subject matter expert for designated products, roles, or government mission areas, building deep expertise and identifying emerging public-sector use cases for new product capabilities.

  • Develop government-specific learning journeys, training materials, playbooks, FAQs, demonstrations, use cases, customer impact stories, and communications that enable high-quality adoption programs to scale.

  • Provide timely education for product launches, new features, and capability rollouts, translating product updates into clear and practical relevance for government users.

  • Advise government customers on workforce communications and engagement strategies that build awareness, confidence, participation, and sustained use.

  • Build trusted relationships with government leaders, program owners, technical teams, champions, and front-line public servants, creating experiences that reflect an understanding of their constraints, motivations, and responsibilities to the public.

  • Support government customer communities, events, and peer-learning experiences by keeping resources, discussions, updates, and thought leadership useful and current.

  • Identify and amplify government champions, creative use cases, and meaningful customer outcomes that encourage responsible experimentation, recognize public servants’ contributions, and help other organizations learn.

  • Partner closely with Sales, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Delivery, Product, Global Affairs, Communications, Marketing, Readiness, and other teams to deliver cohesive experiences for public-sector customers.

  • Gather and synthesize government customer feedback, adoption signals, participation data, and engagement outcomes to improve enablement programs and bring the voice of public servants back to Product and other internal stakeholders.

  • Identify patterns across government customers and translate them into scalable programs, content, playbooks, and best practices without losing the human connection required to support public servants effectively.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 6+ years of experience in customer-facing, enablement, instructional, adoption, or transformation roles, engaging executive, business, and technical audiences in government or similarly complex enterprise environments.

  • Understand and value public service and can build credibility with government leaders, program owners, technical teams, and front-line public servants.

  • Possess exceptional presentation, facilitation, and communication skills, particularly when translating complex AI capabilities into clear, accurate, and practical value for audiences with different levels of technical fluency.

  • Have experience designing learning journeys and leading workshops, training programs, executive engagements, customer events, or scaled adoption initiatives.

  • Bring strong practical fluency and enthusiasm across ChatGPT, Agents, and the broader OpenAI product ecosystem, with an understanding of how AI can be applied to real-world government workflows.

  • Are a versatile writer and storyteller who can turn complex information into useful and compelling training materials, presentations, demonstrations, communications, and customer stories.

  • Can connect product capabilities and enablement activities to measurable outcomes such as activation, sustained usage, improved quality, faster delivery, reduced administrative burden, better decision-making, risk reduction, customer satisfaction, or mission impact.

  • Can identify patterns across government customers and convert them into scalable systems, programs, content, and best practices.

  • Are highly organized and comfortable managing multiple workstreams, adapting in live customer environments, and bringing clarity and momentum to ambiguous situations.

  • Bring humility, empathy, curiosity, and a genuine desire to help public servants and colleagues succeed.

  • Are personally committed to fostering the safe and responsible evolution of AI.

This role sits at the intersection of enablement, education, adoption, community, content, and customer experience. raw.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), Cyber - London
raw.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team builds with customers to bring frontier AI into production. Our Cyber FDEs partner with the security and engineering teams that defend globally critical systems, from enterprise software to the core infrastructure it runs on. Cyber FDEs work closely with our Product, Research, and Go-to-Market teams to adapt our products and models to what customers need to defend their systems.

About the Role

You’ll build systems that give defenders an advantage at a scale few engineering teams encounter. You might help an enterprise identify, test, and deploy patches across hundreds of thousands of code repositories, or help a security team analyze petabytes of logs for signs of malicious agents or coordinated attacks. Across these deployments, you’ll build tools that customer engineers can trust to support consequential security decisions.

You’ll work directly with customer security teams, from CISOs to frontline analysts. As AI changes how attackers operate, you’ll help these teams determine where their defenses need to evolve, prioritize what to build, and validate solutions with the engineers who will operate them. Alongside OpenAI’s account teams, you’ll translate security priorities into deployed systems that help defenders cover more ground.

You’ll also help shape what OpenAI builds next. When you identify a gap between what defenders need and what today’s models or products can do, you’ll partner with Research and Product to define, build, and test capabilities that address it.

This role is based in London. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required.

In this role you will:

  • Partner with customer security leaders and OpenAI’s Go-to-Market team to scope engagements, establish responsibilities, and define measurable success criteria.

  • Lead technical design and implementation alongside customer engineers. Integrate agents into security workflows, establish access boundaries, and determine which actions require human review.

  • Build evaluations grounded in the decisions defenders make. For a patching agent, test whether a fix blocks a known exploit while preserving expected application behavior. For a detection system, replay historical attacks alongside normal traffic to measure detection speed and false-positive rates.

  • Guide production rollout with the engineers who will operate the system. Provide the observability and controls they need to understand system behavior, intervene when necessary, and expand adoption with confidence.

  • Translate successful approaches across deployments into reusable tools and engineering practices that other defenders can adopt.

     

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including building and shipping production software.

  • Experience protecting production systems through work in security engineering, infrastructure, SRE, DevOps, or product engineering.

  • Experience building and evaluating AI agents for software engineering workflows.

  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines and practices that maintain code quality, reliability, and security.

  • Ability to navigate unfamiliar codebases and contribute maintainable, production-quality changes.

  • Ability to communicate technical concepts and trade-offs to engineering teams and senior security stakeholders.

Additional experience includes:

Cybersecurity spans many disciplines, and while we’re primarily looking for strong engineering generalists, we’d love to hear about deeper experience in any of the following areas:

  • Security curiosity and experimentation: You read CVE write-ups because you want to understand how things break. You may have built an agent honeypot to test a hypothesis—or prove a point—and enjoy turning a security question into a hands-on experiment.

  • Security community engagement: You enjoy exchanging ideas with defenders, whether that’s discussing security strategy with a CISO at Black Hat or comparing technical approaches with frontline practitioners.

  • Application security: You’ve written CodeQL queries or Semgrep rules, built fuzzing harnesses, or discovered and responsibly disclosed vulnerabilities.

  • Automated remediation: CI/CD is your happy place. You’ve built tooling that turns security findings into tested patches, dependency upgrades, or configuration changes across large codebases.

  • Detection engineering: You’ve written and deployed detections using Sigma, YARA, Splunk, or KQL and tested them against attacker behavior.

  • Cloud and identity security: You’ve designed cloud IAM architectures and investigated abuse of workload identities, role hierarchies, or cross-account trust.

  • Security research: You’ve reverse-engineered malware, developed exploit reproductions, or contributed to vulnerability research.

  • Agent security: You’ve tested agents for prompt injection, tool misuse, or credential exposure and built defenses against them.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

raw.description:
Who We Are

Having surpassed $300M ARR and continuing to grow, Optro helps enterprises transform risk into opportunity through its AI-powered GRC Intelligence Platform. More than 50% of the Fortune 500, including 7 of the Fortune 10, leverage our award-winning technology to move their businesses forward with greater clarity and agility. And our customers love us: Optro is top-rated on G2.com and Gartner Peer Insights.

At Optro, we inspire each other to innovate and are proud of what we are producing. We spend each day thinking of new ways to help our customers and contribute to the greater good of our company and our surrounding communities. We are all about assisting each other and breaking through barriers to create the most loved audit, risk, ESG, and InfoSec platform by our customers. This is how we have become one of the 500 fastest-growing tech companies in North America for the seventh year in a row, as ranked by Deloitte!

Why This Role is Exciting

The Partner Success Manager (EMEA) will lead partner enablement and delivery across EMEA/MENA & APAC acting as Optro's on-the-ground authority for the region. Based in London, this person will set the pace for how partners across these regions are enabled, certified, and supported — building the policies, processes, and solving real delivery challenges that will keep the region running smoothly and independently. You’ll work directly with partners and internal teams to turn strategy into execution—testing, refining, and improving how Optro enables partner success.

Key Responsibilities

Reporting into the Director of Partner Services, this role is designed for an experienced leader who can own the EMEA/MENA/APAC region — setting direction, building policy and process, and making sound decisions independently. As a Partner Success Manager (EMEA), you will support the execution and delivery of Optro’s partner services strategy by owning key partner relationships, enablement initiatives, and delivery outcomes.

raw.title: Senior Solar PV Engineer – Southampton
raw.description:
Position Summary

Location: South East England – based within ~30 miles of Southampton

Are you an experienced electrician who enjoys fault-finding more than fitting? Otovo is building its UK field service team and we’re looking for a senior Solar PV & Battery Service Engineer to lead our service work across the South East.

The role is mainly service, maintenance and repair: you’ll take on the more complex solar PV and battery faults, work independently across the region, and help set the standard as the team grows. It suits a qualified electrician with solar PV experience who likes solving problems and looking after homeowners.

Key Responsibilities

  • Diagnose, troubleshoot and repair domestic solar PV systems, inverters, battery storage (EESS) and associated electrical equipment

  • Lead on complex faults, escalations and warranty repairs across the South East

  • Carry out preventive maintenance, inspection and testing to BS 7671

  • Commission new systems and upgrades, completing certification and documentation correctly

  • Use test equipment such as multifunction testers, clamp meters, insulation testers and thermal imaging cameras

  • Keep accurate service records, test results, reports and photo documentation

  • Follow safe working practices including safe isolation, PPE and working at height

  • Mentor and support junior engineers as the regional team grows

  • Communicate clearly with homeowners about system status and recommended repairs

  • Represent Otovo professionally at customer sites

What We Offer

  • Salary of £44,000 – £50,000 per year

  • Company van and fuel card

  • Paid holidays

  • Full-time, permanent role in a growing renewables company

  • A senior role helping to build Otovo’s UK field service team


Requirements

  • Level 3 electrical qualification and a valid ECS card

  • BS 7671 18th Edition

  • Solar PV experience essential; City & Guilds 2399 preferred (we can support experienced electricians to gain it)

  • Proven hands-on experience installing, servicing or fault-finding domestic solar PV systems

  • Confident fault-finding on inverters and DC/AC circuits, working independently

  • Full UK driving licence

  • Comfortable working at height, on roofs and outdoors in all weather

  • Strong communication and customer service skills

  • Based within ~30 miles of Southampton and willing to travel across the South East

Nice to Have

  • Battery storage (EESS) training or experience

  • Inspection & Testing qualification (e.g. City & Guilds 2391)

  • Experience leading or mentoring other technicians

  • EV charger installation experience
