  • Own joiner, mover and leaver processes across all locations, making sure they are secure, auditable and efficient

  • Drive automation, self-service and AI to improve user experience and team efficiency

  • Manage IT vendors, licences and contracts, and support budget planning and cost tracking

  • Work with Security, Engineering and Compliance to keep IT controls effective in a regulated environment, and provide evidence for audits

  • Act as the final escalation point for complex technical issues and major IT incidents


What we’re looking for

  • 7+ years in IT Support, IT Operations or Service Desk environments, including at least 2 years line managing an IT team

  • A track record of building, coaching and retaining high-performing, inclusive teams, including running 1:1s, performance reviews and difficult conversations

  • Experience supporting or leading IT strategy and change programmes in a scaling organisation

  • Strong hands-on background with macOS and MDM platforms such as Jamf or Kandji

  • Experience owning ITSM platforms (e.g. Jira, Zendesk, Freshdesk), defining SLAs and reporting service metrics to senior stakeholders

  • Experience managing vendors, licences and IT budgets

  • Knowledge of cloud platforms such as AWS and Google Cloud

  • Good understanding of security and compliance in IT operations, such as access management, endpoint security and audit evidence

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management, and confident presenting to senior leaders

  • Willingness to travel to our office locations in Kent and London as needed


Nice to haves

  • Direct experience scaling IT functions in high-growth tech environments

  • Experience in fintech, financial services or another regulated industry (e.g. ISO 27001, SOC 2 or FCA-regulated environments)

  • Experience supporting international offices or expansion into new markets

  • Experience with network management and troubleshooting

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

  3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

About the role

This role is for someone wanting to start a career in operations within a financial services firm. You'll join as a Graduate focused on working complaints and train to become a fully competent Complaints Officer, investigating and resolving our more complex customer interactions across loans, cards and auto-finance. A critical role to help the business understand how it can serve customers better.

This is a casework role. From early on you will hold your own caseload, speak to customers directly, make decisions on whether we got it right, and put things right where we didn't. You will be supported through structured training, coaching and quality feedback as you develop in the role

Some of the areas you'll delve into are:

  • The regulatory framework for complaints: FCA regulation, the DISP rules, Consumer Duty, and how the guidance is applied to real cases.

  • Investigation technique: gathering evidence, interrogating system records and call recordings, and testing what actually happened against what should have happened.

  • Decision making and redress: reaching fair and objective outcomes, and calculating and explaining any compensation due.

  • Customer communication: writing final response letters that break complex issues down into plain English.

  • The Financial Ombudsman Service: how cases are referred, how FOS reaches its view, and how we apply those learnings to future cases.

  • Root cause and feedback: spotting the product and process failures behind complaints and feeding them back to frontline and product teams.

Reporting to a Complaints Manager within the Operations Team, you will be responsible for a live caseload and for the quality of the decisions you make on it.

No prior complaints experience needed, we care about how you think, not what you already know. This role requires an ability to learn quickly, work to deadlines and support our customers effectively.

Your team's objectives

Lendable aims to resolve all complaints promptly, ensuring that they are investigated diligently and fairly for customers. We are committed to providing excellent customer service and to reaching the right outcomes for our customers.

Feedback is an important part of how we evolve as a business. The team is encouraged to speak up, take each complaint on its own merits and provide valuable insight back into the business so we can improve and grow.

Our ability to handle complaints effectively for our customers and therefore for us as a business has never been more important than now, as we expand our existing products in the UK and US financial markets.

What you'll be doing

  • Investigating and resolving complaints about our loans, cards and auto-finance products, taking each case on its own merits

  • Self-managing a varied and increasingly complex caseload: prioritising cases, choosing the best contact mechanism for each customer, and working efficiently enough to meet our KPI minimum standards

  • Communicating with complainants in writing and by phone — managing expectations, handling difficult situations with tact and professionalism, and finding solutions to the issues raised

  • Writing professional final response letters that set out our decision, our rationale and the customer's right to refer to the Financial Ombudsman Service

  • Following our complaint handling standards and keeping clear records, making sure every decision is backed by demonstrable evidence and a documented rationale

  • Working to resolve complaints without the customer needing to refer to FOS, and applying the learnings from both internal and FOS outcomes to future cases

  • Feeding back to frontline and product teams on the product and process improvements your cases surface, across Operations and the wider Lendable business

  • Keeping your knowledge of Lendable's products current through effective use and review of our policies, procedures and business tools

  • Turning your hand to other areas of operational need as the business requires

What we're looking for

  • Educated to degree level

  • Exceptional written communication - you can structure an argument and explain a complex decision clearly to someone who is not an expert

  • An aptitude for investigation, analysis, problem-solving and dispute resolution

  • Strong organisation and self-management - you can hold a caseload, prioritise it and work to deadlines without being chased

  • Sound judgment and a sound moral compass: willing to speak up to make sure good customer outcomes stay at the heart of what we do

  • Resilience and adaptability in a fast-paced, changing environment

  • A willingness to learn FCA regulation and the DISP complaint handling rules and guidance

The interview process

We're not a corporation so we try our best to get things moving as quickly as possible. For this role we'd expect:

  • A 15 minute cognitive assessment

  • A quick phone call with one of the Talent team

  • An onsite assessment centre with a role focus and a final stage interview with the Complaints Management team to discuss your fit and capability for the role.

Life at Lendable

  • Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites

You'll work mainly on the Zable app, our financial SuperApp with 2M+ monthly active users. It brings together credit cards, loans, memberships, mobile and more in one place. You'll own complex product areas end-to-end, from discovery and research through to polished, production-ready design. You'll set design direction alongside PMs and Engineering, mentor other designers, and help raise the bar for craft and outcomes across the team.

The ideal candidate

  • 5+ years of product design experience, ideally in fintech or a fast-paced startup

  • Strong mobile app and web experience

  • Customer-obsessed and data-literate: you challenge solution-led briefs and back decisions with evidence

  • Takes real creative risks, and can bring a team along with a clear story for why a bolder direction is right

  • Confident with senior stakeholders, and pushes back when quality or customer outcomes are at risk

  • AI-native: you push past the first obvious output, not just work faster

  • Enjoys raising the bar for other designers through mentoring and feedback

  • Bonus:

    • Designing AI-powered products (explainability, human override)

    • Regulated environments, e.g. Consumer Duty

  • Lead discovery, choosing the right research method and turning findings into clear design direction

  • Own design delivery for your squad, from first flows through to build

  • Work with engineers throughout design, not just at handoff, weighing build cost in your decisions

  • Contribute to the design system, and know when breaking from it is right for the customer

  • Run usability tests and experiments with clear measures of success

  • Use AI across your workflow, including pushing design changes to production yourself

Our design principles

  1. Simplicity wins

    1. If a user has to think too hard, we’ve already lost. We strip away complexity, jargon, and unnecessary steps to make managing finances effortless. Every screen should feel intuitive, focused, and frictionless.

  2. Evidence over ego

    1. We don’t design based on opinions. Everything we build is informed by data, tested, and refined based on real user behavior.

  3. Trust is our best feature

    1. Finance is built on trust. Every design decision should reinforce transparency, security, and user confidence. We prove we care by helping users make financial decisions that empower them.

raw.title: Account Manager, Partnerships
raw.description:
🏷️ Title: Account Manager, Partnerships

👫 Department: Commercial

💰 Salary: £55,000 - £65,000

📄 Contract: Permanent

🎁 Benefits & Culture: See here

📈 Equity: A very generous EMI share offering

🌴 Holiday: 26 days + bank holidays

💗 Mission: Elevate later life for everybody and build the care sector of the future

💻 Office Policy: Hybrid with a minimum of 2 core office days per week

🌍 Office Location: London Bridge, London, UK

 

🔍 The Opportunity:

Lottie is building the AI operating system for social care, changing how the UK finds, manages and pays for care. Most families start looking in a crisis, and many turn first to someone they already trust: their employer, council, the NHS or a charity. We want Lottie to be where those organisations send them.

Partnerships already bring families to Lottie. Through Seniorcare by Lottie, large employers give their people expert support when a relative needs care. Referral partners like Kinly introduce families to our marketplace.

You'll own these partnerships and build the next wave. About half your time goes on growing existing partners, and half on opening new ones across the public sector (like local authorities) and the private and charity sectors. We're early, so you'll shape the proposition from the ground up.

You'll be an individual contributor reporting to our VP Commercial, Matt Morgan. Success means enquiries from your partnerships and, ultimately, families placed in care.

 

💻 What does this role involve?

  • Own our relationships with the employers who use Seniorcare by Lottie, acting as their senior point of contact, keeping them engaged and maintaining the number of employees who use the service.

  • Take over our marketplace referral partnerships, including Kinly, managing performance, commercials and the quality of the enquiries they refer.

  • Build and run a pipeline of new demand-generating partnerships for the marketplace, exploring local authorities, the NHS and national old age charities.

  • Design the commercial model for each new partnership, from referral fees to co-marketing, and negotiate the terms.

  • Track enquiries and placements by partner, so we know which partnerships are working and where to invest next.

  • Work with our Care Experts, marketing and product teams to make every partner referral a great experience for the family and easy for the partner.

 

💪 What problems will you be solving?

  • When a parent suddenly needs care, most families don't start with Google. They ask their employer, their GP or their council. Your job is to make Lottie the first place those organisations think of.

  • A partnership is only as valuable as the families it brings. You'll make sure partner referrals turn into placements, not just leads.

  • Local authorities, the NHS and charities work to different incentives, budgets and timelines from commercial partners. You'll work out where Lottie genuinely helps them, from easing pressure on hospital discharge to supporting families who fund their own care, and build partnerships that last.

 

👀 We think you’ll be a great fit if…

  • You have experience in partnerships, business development or account management, ideally in a marketplace, employee benefits, health or care business.

  • You've grown existing partners and landed new ones from scratch.

  • You're commercially minded: you think in volume, conversion and unit economics, and you're comfortable negotiating terms.

  • You build credibility quickly with very different people, from an HR director to a council commissioner.

  • You use AI to stay on top of everything, so a nine-month council deal and your day-to-day partners both get the attention they need.

 

💔 This role isn’t for you if…

  • You're not passionate about elevating later life for everybody - our mission is at the heart of everything we do.

  • You only want to manage existing relationships, or only want to hunt new ones. This role is both.

  • You need quick wins to stay motivated. Some partnerships will take many months to land, and we measure them by the families they bring, not logos signed.

  • You're not up for using AI and process improvement to move fast in a growing startup.

 

📝 Application

We'd love to see a short video (about 2 minutes) answering this question:

Introduce yourself and tell us why you're interested in Lottie and why you feel you'd be a good fit for the role.

We appreciate this takes time. We receive a high volume of applications and this helps us assess you on more than your CV.

 

🔢 Lottie’s Interview Process

  • Screening interview led by Lottie's Talent Acquisition team - remote

  • Task/exercise, completed independently and talked through with your Hiring Manager - remote

  • Final interview with your Hiring Manager - in person (London Bridge)

 

🤩 Candidate Experience: All candidates will be informed of their application status.

  • Pre-Screen and Screening interview: you'll receive an email notification, but no specific feedback will be provided at this stage.

  • Task/exercise: if you are unsuccessful, you'll receive constructive feedback via email and be offered a debrief call with our Talent team.

  • Final Interview: for final-stage candidates who are not offered the role, we will provide feedback via a phone call.

 

🚀 Meet Lottie

Founded with a mission to build the care sector of the future, Lottie is creating the AI operating system for social care - designed to unlock profitability for care providers and to make finding care as easy as booking a holiday on Airbnb.

Launched in London in July 2021, Lottie has raised over £25m from tier 1 venture capital funds (Accel and General Catalyst) and is widely recognised as one of the UK's fastest growing tech companies. Most recently, Lottie was the acclaimed winner of Deloitte Fast 50, LinkedIn Top Startups, The Sunday Times Tech 2026 and Startups.co.uk Startups 100.

As of today, Lottie offers three core products:

raw.title: Marketing Growth Engineer
raw.description:
TL;DR:
We're looking for a full-stack engineer who wants to sit at the heart of Lovable's marketing engine - making every pound of spend measurable, and every manual workflow a tool. One sprint you're tracing spend from first click to revenue across Meta, Google and newer channels; the next you're shipping landing pages, experiments or an agent that saves the team hours a week. You think in React and APIs, but your first instinct is always: can we measure it, and does it help us grow faster?

Coding skills + excellent taste + growth instincts + marketing obsession = you.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What we’re looking for

  • 5+ years of experience building and growing user-facing products in high-performing teams, ideally including growth work, marketplaces/platforms, or communities.

  • Strong product sense and UX taste for multi-sided systems with creators, learners, and customers - you can see problems from multiple sides and design for all of them.

  • Knowledge of Meta Pixel and Google Ad Network APIs, and experience working with data from ad networks. Experience with TikTok, LinkedIn, Reddit and Beehiiv, plus CTV/podcast tracking, is a plus.

  • Comfortable using data, funnels, analytics, attribution, and A/B testing to shape what you build and how you iterate.

  • Skilled at designing, measuring, and iterating experiments, and thorough in setting up growth systems "right" from the start.

  • Experience collaborating across functions (design, marketing, partnerships, support, data) to launch and grow new product surfaces and ecosystems.

  • Enjoys designing reusable growth, ecosystem, and monetization tools that other builders can plug into, with a pragmatic and detail-oriented mindset.

  • Motivated by helping others succeed and by seeing impact through engagement, measurable results, and revenue - you care about the scoreboard as much as the code.

What you’ll do

In one sentence: You'll sit between marketing and engineering and build whatever we need to grow faster, from the site and tracking to the tools the team uses every day - expect to be driving the thinking here alongside our team leads.

  • Build the tools marketing runs on: Find the manual work slowing the team down and replace it with tools, automations or agents, ideally built on Lovable.

  • Shape what gets built: Work with design, marketing, data and partnerships to decide what's worth doing, then own it end to end.

  • Own how we measure marketing: Make sure every pound of spend can be traced from first click to revenue, across Meta and Google and newer channels like CTV and podcast. This is what lets us scale spend with confidence.

  • Make experimentation cheap & fast: Build the events, funnels and A/B testing setup that let the team test an idea in days and double down on what works.

  • Turn the website into a growth surface: Ship landing pages, signup flows and first-run moments that get new users to value fast, without waiting in a product queue.

  • Keep it Lovable: Growth should feel like part of the product, never bolted on.

Our tech stack

We're building with tools that both humans and AI love:

  • Frontend: React

  • Backend: Golang and Rust

  • Cloud: Cloudflare, GCP, AWS, Many LLM providers

  • DevOps & Tooling: Github Actions, Grafana, OTEL, infra-as-code (Terraform)

About your application

Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.

We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

raw.title: Lead Product Manager
raw.description:
Every team has AI. Few have mastered it. Humans were built to adapt, but AI is now moving faster than most workforces can.

Multiverse is the AI adoption layer: the missing link between the AI tools that companies have invested in and the people expected to use them.

Our ambition is to put AI capability in every worker’s hands. Apprenticeships got us started: we’ve trained over a third of the UK’s data and AI apprentices, worked with a third of the FTSE 100, and generated £2bn+ in verified ROI. Now Mastry, our new adaptive learning platform, takes that further, guiding a company’s AI workforce transformation from start to finish. Mae, our AI guide inside Mastry, is a real-time AI agent that thinks, speaks, listens and sees, working alongside the tools you already use, like Claude and Copilot.

We closed our latest fundraising round in April 2026, with $500m+ raised in total from VC partners including Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Schroders Capital and Lightspeed. With a $2.1bn valuation, we are Europe’s first EdTech double unicorn, and we are just getting started.

If you want to shape how the workforce wins in the AI era, come and join us.

The Opportunity

We are at an inflection point in our journey. Our platform now serves tens of thousands of learners, demand for AI skills is accelerating, and we are investing seriously in the product and technology that will take us to the next stage of scale. This is a role for someone who wants to build the product that gets more people into transformative learning, and upskill people with critical data and AI skills faster.

The Role

We are looking for a Lead Product Manager to own Prescribe: the product that helps a prospective learner find the right programme for their skills and their employer's goals, then takes them to a confident commitment and a successful start. You will be the strategic counterpart to a Senior Engineering Manager, working alongside design and data, and closely with our go-to-market and fulfilment teams.

Growth at Multiverse means getting more people from first interest to a confident start, and it is a product problem, not a marketing problem. You will own the conversion metrics, set the strategy, run the experiments, and drive the outcomes. AI will drive much of the improvement, and you will decide where it helps.

As a Lead, you will work regularly with the most senior leaders across the company. You will report to the Single Threaded Leader for Diagnose & Prescribe and will not manage other product managers. The role is based in London, hybrid, three days a week in the office.

What You'll Own

AI-native product experiences

  • Shape new conversational, AI-first experiences that help learners and customers understand the best programme for their skills and career development.

  • Decide where AI genuinely improves a match and where it only adds noise, and build the evaluation and guardrails that keep it trustworthy in front of real users.

  • Turn learner and customer behaviour into product direction.

Prescription and eligibility

  • Own the logic that connects a learner's skills to a programme and to a customer's levy funding, where mistakes carry a real financial and regulatory cost.

  • Work with Legal, Compliance and Fulfilment to make eligibility and compliance rules configurable and explainable, so business owners can change them without a rebuild.

  • Make every recommendation something a learner and a customer can understand and challenge.

Recommendation, commitment and finalisation

  • Own the journey from recommendation to a learner committing and starting.

  • Identify high-leverage drop-off points and own the experimentation roadmap.

  • Design product interventions that adapt to learner needs and behaviour and shorten the time to a confident start.

  • Collaborate with GTM, Operations and Data teams to improve attribution and the quality of what enters the funnel.

Metrics and experimentation

  • Own conversion from prospect to committed learner, with retention and programme fit as the guardrails.

  • Champion a culture of hypothesis-led, structured experimentation.

Cross-functional Leadership

  • Co-own the strategy and roadmap with your Senior Engineering Manager, with disagreement surfaced early and alignment as your shared deliverable.

  • Involve GTM, Fulfilment and Support before changes ship. They run what we build, so know their biggest pain points.

  • Author the narratives the group needs, from the press release and FAQ (PRFAQ) for your area to the sales-facing briefing for a launch.

  • Represent Prescribe in roadmap conversations with senior leadership.

What We're Looking For

The best candidates will have owned a growth-critical product before, ideally in a B2B or ideally a B2B2C context. You should have hands-on experience shipping AI-powered features and the ability to navigate complexity without losing sight of the learner.

Must-have experience:

  • Substantial experience as a PM with a track record of improving measurable growth metrics (acquisition, activation, retention, automation).

  • Confidence with data: pulling analysis, running cohort studies, and building dashboards.

  • Experience designing and running rigorous A/B and multivariate experiments.

  • Strong instincts for user experience and a focus on sustainable long-term strategies.

  • Ability to build alignment across cross-functional teams without formal authority, including with commercial, GTM and operations counterparts.

  • Hands-on experience building products using AI/LLMs to generate or personalise content.

  • AI Builder mindset with experience of using AI as your engine to drive repeatable and automated systems, processes and artefacts that create step changes in performance and efficiencies.

Strong signals we look for:

  • Familiarity with product-led growth (PLG) in a B2B context.

  • Experience designing personalisation systems, including data models and trigger logic.

  • Previous work in a company that has scaled from hundreds to thousands of users.

  • A point of view on where AI genuinely improves outcomes versus creating noise.

  • A bonus if you've done this in a regulated environment, such as funding, eligibility or compliance-heavy products. Knowledge of UK apprenticeships and the levy is an additional plus.

How you work:

  • Solve for Customer Value: You're direct about data, even when it challenges existing priorities.

  • Drivers, Not Passengers: You think in systems, take completion seriously, and raise bad news as quickly as good.

  • Be Decisive, Even in Ambiguity: You're comfortable with ambiguity and define structure in new spaces.

  • AI to Deliver Outcomes: You have a bias for action (ship, measure, iterate) and ask "how would AI help do this?" before scoping the work.

Not for you if:

This role won't fit if you'd rather write specs than stay close to the data, the design, and the customer. It also won't fit if you see AI as a productivity tweak rather than a step change in how a product team works. And it needs someone who renegotiates scope out loud when it's wrong, not someone who absorbs it and hopes it works out.

What We Offer

  • The opportunity to work on a product that genuinely changes economic trajectories.

  • A team that takes craft seriously and holds a high bar.

  • Direct access to senior leadership and meaningful influence over product direction.

  • A place in a company rebuilding itself as product-powered and AI-native, where you help define the result rather than inherit it.

Benefits

  • Time off: 27 days holiday (including 3 winter shutdown days) and bank holidays, plus 5 extra days off (1 life event, 2 volunteer days and 2 summer shutdown days).

  • Health and wellbeing: Bupa private medical insurance, a medical cash back plan, therapy through Spill and gym access through Wellhub.

  • Equity for all: we believe that when Multiverse wins, we all win, which is why every permanent employee receives share options.

  • Financial security: life insurance at 3x salary, a workplace pension with 4% contribution from us, Cycle to Work and a Tech Scheme.

  • Family support: enhanced maternity and paternity leave, adoption and shared parental leave, paid leave after pregnancy loss, and a workplace nursery scheme.

  • Hybrid working: 3 days a week in the office - except for Coaches & Instructors who come into the office 1 day per month. Plus 10 days a year to work from anywhere.

  • Work perks: quarterly team socials, company-wide events, happy hours, lunch delivered to the office once a week, fully stocked snack bar and a drinks fridge!


Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

We’re an equal opportunities employer. And proud of it. Every applicant and employee is afforded the same opportunities regardless of race, colour, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. This will never change. Read our Equality, Diversity & Inclusion policy here.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

Multiverse is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of our learners. We expect all employees to share this commitment and adhere to our Safeguarding Policy, our Prevent Policy and all other Multiverse company policies. Successful applicants will be required to undertake at least a Basic check via the Disclosure Barring Service (DBS).

raw.title: Sales Engineer
raw.description:
Why Numeric

Every business runs on accounting, but the systems underneath it were built for a different era. Today’s ERPs don’t store a company’s financial data. They store a diluted copy of it. Every contract, lease, and invoice gets flattened into a journal entry, and the context that made it meaningful is thrown away. That’s why accounting teams spend every month re-checking numbers, stitching together spreadsheets, and waiting on engineering, and why AI struggles to do real accounting work. Accounting doesn’t have a reporting problem. It has a data problem.

Enter Numeric: the data platform finance teams run on. We started with the month-end close, where the data problem hurts most, and hundreds of finance teams now run their close on Numeric. That work led us to rebuild the system of record itself. In September 2026 we launched the Financial Data Platform (FDP), a platform built for the agent era. Instead of a journal entry, the real business object enters the system and the accounting is derived from it. Every number is traceable to its source, reporting works on any dimension, and accountants and AI agents finally have enough context to work together. While others bolted AI features onto the old data model, we built a new one.

We have a growing base of customers who love our product, including Anthropic, Plaid, Brex, Betterment, Wealthfront, and Asana. We’ve raised $89M from top-tier investors including IVP, Menlo Ventures, Founders Fund, and 8VC, along with founders and executives from Ramp, Segment, and other category-defining companies. We’re in-person, with teams in New York, San Francisco, and London, and we just shipped the product that will define our next decade. There’s never been a better time to join.

About This Role

As a Sales Engineer, you'll be the technical expert partnering with our sales team, helping accounting & finance leaders understand how Numeric solves their most complex accounting challenges. The product is moving fast, customers are getting more sophisticated, and the SE role is at the center of every major win.

We’re looking for someone with experience in technical selling to the OCFO and can hold their own with a Controller pushing back on the technical detail. This role is your path to owning bigger deals, shaping the playbooks the team runs on, and helping define what world-class presales looks like.

What you'll do

  • Independently lead demos, discovery sessions, and proof-of-concept engagements across mid-market and select enterprise accounts

  • Partner closely with Account Executives to develop technical win strategies and drive deals forward

  • Build credibility with senior finance stakeholders including CFOs, Controllers, and FDs of Finance as a trusted domain expert

  • Gather and synthesize customer feedback to inform product roadmap priorities. Partner closely with PMM and product to shape the future of the platform

  • Develop and maintain reusable demo environments, technical collateral, and enablement materials for the broader tea

About You

  • 3–5 years of total experience, with time as a Sales Engineer/Solution Consultant or Implementation Consultant at an ERP or FP&A platform (e.g., NetSuite, Workday, or Pigment), or time in an accounting & finance org with a passion for more customer-facing work

  • Solid accounting and finance domain knowledge, with the ability to hold a credible conversation with a Controller or CFOs

  • A track record of running demos, POCs, and discovery independently on deals of real complexity

  • Based in the London

Nice To Haves

  • Experience contributing to an SE function at a high-growth startup

  • ACCA/CIMA or formal accounting background

  • Familiarity with accounting close management or financial reporting workflows

How We Work:

This role is in-person in London (in office, with flexibility). We strongly believe we will only be successful if everyone on the team is anchored in our following set of core principles:

  • Brick by Brick: To win, our team needs to show up and execute in each domain every day.

  • Love the Game: We focus on the craft and a deep sense of giving a f*ck. We’re building a company full of people who are equally engaged and motivated.

  • SALY: We refuse to accept “Same As Last Year.” For too long, accounting and finance systems have reflected outdated processes instead of reimagining what’s possible. We’re driven by a first-principles approach to building better solutions.

  • Own the Outcome: We own our results. We typically hire builders and give them large mandates with high-trust. Engineers are responsible not just for code, but for ensuring the product is solving the end problems of the users.

  • Earn the right: We’re impatient to deliver results. We relentlessly iterate, measure, and improve. Every day is an opportunity to beat our prior best, raising the bar for the value we deliver to customers.

Compensation: £80K – £110K • Offers Equity • Offers Commission

raw.title: DevOps - Consultant
raw.description:
Ready to automate, innovate and make a real impact? 

Do you want to build reliable, scalable systems that make a real difference to millions of people? Do you want to work at a certified B Corp with an inclusive and learning culture as part of a diverse team of great people? 
 
If so, Opencast could be the place for you. We’re a growing tech consultancy that creates user-centred solutions with purpose for our clients in government, healthcare and purpose-driven businesses. Working in DevOps, you’ll build and maintain the systems that let teams respond quickly to needs. You’ll work on high-impact projects, helping to build reliable, scalable systems. We align work to industry-recognised roles such as Build & Release Engineer (BRE), Platform Engineer (PLE) or Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) and, where needed, to more specialised areas such as security, cloud hosting, infrastructure or networking. 
 

The Role

At Opencast, we love to keep things simple, and we love automation. 
 
It’s not the same as your standard DevOps Consultant job. Depending on your client’s needs, you’ll take on a range of roles. These will include: 
  • Taking the lead on responding to outages, triaging issues, balancing stakeholder priorities/concerns, and keeping communication channels open with all parties. 
  • Developing, and implementing continuous deployment solutions that help our clients to deliver software faster and more efficiently. 
  • Collaborating with our clients to understand their ways of working and will have an enthusiasm to learn new tools and technologies as needed. 
  • Contributing within Opencast communities.
  • Ensure that work is carried out in accordance with Opencast's quality, environmental, and information security policies and procedures, as well as applicable customer policies, standards, and procedures while working on client. 
We care about building things right. We believe in good DevOps practices and keeping things simple. We want to support you as much as we can on interiorising our approach to DevOps engineering and you supporting others. 
 
We are proud consultants who combine our own experience and approach with our company values. 
 
We are comfortable with new tech. We are empowered, cloud native, vendor agnostic DevOps engineers. We are empathetic, patient and care about quality. 
 
We know when to pick our battles and how to manage expectations. We are humble, inclusive team players that listen and collaborate, with zero egos! 
 
We’re always willing to teach and help others (inside or outside of our team). And we’re always willing to learn. 
 
It’s a varied job that keeps you super technical and excited. 
 

Requirements

This role involves weekly on-site work, and you’ll be required to travel regularly to client locations across the UK. We’re looking for people who value in-person collaboration, enjoy building strong relationships, and are passionate about delivering solutions that make a real difference for our clients. 

Due to the nature of this role, you must either hold active Security Check (SC) clearance or be eligible and willing to undergo the clearance process. 

SC clearance is granted in line with UK Government security vetting requirements. Typically, applicants must have UK citizenship and have lived continuously in the UK for at least the past five years, with no single absence exceeding 28 consecutive days. Nationality and immigration status may also be considered as part of the vetting process. We are unable to progress applications from candidates who do not meet these requirements. 

If you are unsure whether you meet the eligibility criteria, we encourage you to review the guidance or discuss this with us before applying. 

We’re looking to welcome new team members for multiple roles from June 2026 onward. If you’re interested in joining Opencast, we’d encourage you to apply. 

Essential experience

To succeed in this role, you'll have experience working within DevOps and be able to demonstrate, with tangible examples, that you can: 

  • Create, modify, and maintain complex CI/CD pipelines.

  • Create dashboards and visualisations for application performance that proactively identify and address potential problems before they occur.

  • Use automated testing to detect security issues/vulnerabilities in application and/or infrastructure code, thereby detecting issues before it reaches production (aka Shift-Left).

  • Strong experience in operating and maintaining services primarily in any of the BIG three public cloud providers (AWS, Azure, and GCP).

Essential consulting skills 

In addition to DevOps skills, there are essential core skills you need to be an Opencast consultant. You'll need to demonstrate how you: 
  • Contribute to improving ways of working and driving continuous improvements within your teams. 
  • Share knowledge and best practice with fellow consultants, including proactively engaging in client and Opencast communities of practice. 
  • Positively challenge decisions or solutions you don't agree with, striving for the best client outcome.
  • Create lasting value in the projects you work on, ensuring a user-centric, sustainable approach. 
  • Engage with Opencast in a meaningful way, supporting the growth of your practice and wider capability. 
  • Support Opencast's growth plans, by providing case studies and updates into the relevant forums of your project work. 
During the interview process, we'll ask questions to explore your experience across these areas. 

Salary

£50,000 - £60,000 per annum. 
 

What we offer

A competitive package including a 7% employer pension contribution, share options, and a discretionary bonus. You’ll also benefit from 25 days’ holiday and access to 3 annual “life happens” days to support unexpected situations.  We provide wellbeing support, ongoing professional development, volunteering opportunities, and the chance to be part of a genuinely supportive team. 
 

Where you’ll work 

This role requires regular on-site attendance at our HQ, hub offices, and client sites, as well as the ability to work from home. Applicants must be able to travel to offices and client sites across the UK as part of their normal working arrangements, as travel is essential for fulfilling the responsibilities of the role. 
 

We include you 

We welcome candidates from all identities, attributes, ways of thinking and backgrounds to thrive in a career at Opencast. Our aim is for the diversity of our people to be reflected in the solutions we deliver, to help create a fairer society for all.    
 

Interview 

Interviews will be conducted via Microsoft Teams. We’re happy to make adjustments to support your needs. 
 

Want to know more?  

Visit our website or email

raw.description:
Orbital is the AI platform for real estate legal work.

Real estate shapes the world around us: our homes, our workplaces and our cultural landmarks. It’s the infrastructure that powers everyday life and is the world's largest asset class. Yet behind every single deal, real estate and legal teams work hard to navigate decades-old complexity; manually connecting documents, hidden obligations, geo-spatial context, and multiple parties into a path forward. We connect the legal and physical record, so that path is clearer than ever before. Our mission is to make real estate transactions faster, clearer, and less manual.

Here, you'll be part of changing how the deals behind the largest asset class get transacted, and will help shape the future of real estate.

A bit about us:

🚀 We’re building at the forefront of AI technology, without losing the deeply human expertise our clients depend on.

🏢 Orbital is built with former practising real estate lawyers and 250+ years of combined legal expertise. We're purpose-built for the complexity of real estate: accelerating due diligence, drafting and negotiation, and deal coordination with legal-grade precision.

💰 We've just raised a $60m Series B, led by Brighton Park Capital, to accelerate our global expansion – $75m raised to date.

🤝 We're trusted by 5,000+ real estate professionals, spanning UK Magic Circle and US Am Law 100 firms, to household names like M&S. Leading firms like BCLP, Orrick, Goodwin, Womble Bond Dickinson and Clifford Chance rely on Orbital to remove the busywork, freeing legal and real estate teams to focus on sharp judgment, standout client service, and closing deals faster.

💡 Working at Orbital means joining a bold, ambitious team, with the trust to take ownership and make a real impact from day one.

Role Overview 🔎

As a Senior UX Design Engineer, you'll own some of the hardest problems in our product and see them through until they're solved. You'll join our design team, three designers today and growing, and work inside our teams alongside product managers and our product, legal and AI engineers (our legal engineers are former real estate lawyers).

We've built a product that real estate lawyers rely on, and now we're also building for the businesses that own, occupy and develop property. You'll work across both, and much of it is new ground. Nobody here has the full answer yet, and that's the job: you'll get to know the people we build for, work out what they need from us, and build it.

This role is not about polishing screens. Our product is live and trusted by some of the most demanding real estate lawyers and property teams in the world. The hardest design problems here are not about how it looks. They are about whether people can trust it and get their work done.

Your starting point is the users, their work and the product: you notice what isn't working, decide what matters most, and see it through, from the first customer conversation to the version they use.

Here, designers build what they design. With AI coding tools, you'll build your designs into the product yourself, often live for customers the next day. When anyone can build, judgement matters most, and that is the heart of this role.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Find out who you're building for: talk to customers and map who does what inside law firms and property businesses. You'll do it together with the wider team.

  • Design how people work with our AI agents, which do real work on their behalf: what people hand over, how they check it and see where each answer came from, when they step in, what the agent asks about first and what it simply does, and how that shifts as AI improves.

  • Solve first, then refine: get to the right answer with rough, working versions in front of real people, and add polish once the problem is solved.

  • Build and ship interface changes yourself, using AI coding tools in our codebase. Engineering depth is welcome, not required.

  • Keep the product coherent while everyone builds: engineers, legal engineers, product people and coding agents all build interfaces here. Explain why one option beats another so people can make the call themselves, write it down as clear, reusable rules in the codebase for agents to follow, and evolve our design system so it all still feels like one product.


New to design engineering? 🌱

Design engineering is still a new kind of role, and most great candidates won't have had the title. If you're a strong designer with a good sense of product, and you're excited about building what you design, we'd love to hear from you. We'll help you make the shift.

You should apply if: ✍️

  • You go after the hard problem, not the surface one, and own it until it's solved. You judge your work by whether people use it, rely on it and come back.

  • You're comfortable not knowing yet. You form a view, test it with real people, and change it when they tell you something different.

  • You bring design excellence and strong product sense: hierarchy, layout, type, copy, states, navigation and flow, and a clear view of what is worth building.

  • You've designed for experts, people who know their field better than any designer will. You reach for patterns they already know, and never talk down to them.

  • You can say why. You make a call and ship it without waiting for sign-off, explain it in words others can reuse, and change your mind for a good reason. You'd rather guide people than overrule them.

  • You're genuinely excited about AI: what it can do, where it's heading and how to get the most out of it. You already design or build with AI tools, at work or in your own projects, and you want to help shape how AI changes the working day of property professionals.

  • You want to learn how property and legal work gets done. No legal or property knowledge needed.

  • You have owned and shipped product design work, and can walk us through the problem, not just the result.

Desirable

  • Experience at an early-stage or fast-scaling startup, where there was no established process and you helped create one.

Reasons we might not be for you

  • The pace is fast and our ways of working keep evolving. If you prefer clear boundaries between design and engineering, this may not be the role for you.

Why you'll love it here

raw.title: Chief Operating Officer (COO)
raw.description:
London, Full time, £140,000–196,000+

Pivotal Research finds people who can work on the biggest risks facing humanity and gets them working on them.

We have grown from 2 staff in 2024 to 10 today, and our programmes have more than doubled in size every year. We had 75 participants in 2026. In 2027 we plan to have at least 180 participants across five cohorts of our AI safety and biodefense fellowships, start at least two new programmes, and grow to at least 16 staff.

We are hiring a COO to make sure Pivotal runs well now, still runs well at three times the size, and still runs well when we scale beyond that. You will be responsible for the team that supports execution of our programmes, finances, our systems & processes, and the London office. You will start by managing at least 2 people and build the team from there.

You will be the second most senior person at Pivotal and work directly with Tobias Häberli, our CEO, who will focus on strategy, fundraising and new programmes.

Why this role matters

We think the next few years are unusually important. AGI could bring enormous benefits, and could also cause existential catastrophes. Reducing those risks depends on getting capable people working on the right problems early enough.

Since 2024, 135 fellows have participated in our programmes. Alumni have gone on to roles at METR, Apollo Research, UK AISI, and GovAI, as well as AI Safety fellowships and internships at Anthropic and OpenAI. We measure our success by the important work our fellows go on to do, and how much Pivotal helped them get there.

Right now, our ambition is larger than our capacity to execute well at scale. That is the gap the COO will close, and will help us move from 75 participants in 2026 to at least 180 in 2027.

Why work at Pivotal

We are a small, mission-driven team at LISA in London. People build what they think should exist, and disagreement with leadership is welcome. Read more on Working at Pivotal (what we have done so far, what working here is like, and reasons this role might not suit you).

What you will own

You are responsible for the whole of Pivotal outside programme design, research, and fundraising. In practice, that means:

  • Execution. Every programme we run should be excellent. You make sure the infrastructure, systems, and team members supporting each programme work, and you fix what does not.

  • The team. You build and lead the execution team that supports all of our programmes. You decide who we need, make the case for key hires, and run the hiring for your part of the organisation. Early on, Tobias will give input on hires and sign off on final decisions.

  • Scaling. Pivotal needs to grow several times over without becoming worse at what it does. You design how a 16-person organisation runs, and then one that doubles or triples again in the years after. How decisions get made, how money is managed, how new programmes get launched, and how we have operational greatness while we grow.

  • Finance, legal, compliance, systems, and the London office are primarily your responsibility. You will be well-resourced with a team to help you do all of it.

  • Day-to-day leadership in London. Tobias works partly from Switzerland. You are the senior person on the ground, and you make most day-to-day decisions.

This frees Tobias to focus on strategy, fundraising, networking, hiring, finding collaborators, and designing new programmes.

Who we are looking for

The range runs from someone who has already scaled an organisation through rapid growth beyond Pivotal’s current size, to someone who has not done that yet but has a proven track record and shows excellent aptitude for scaling an organisation. Wherever you sit in that range, we want to see some of the following:

  • A record of making things happen. You have taken responsibility for something hard and delivered. People who have worked with you describe you as the person who is on top of things.

  • A record of building and leading a team. You have hired and managed people, set clear expectations, and give direct feedback. You keep teams motivated and supported through rapid growth and intense periods.

  • You build systems. You have improved how a team or organisation works. You can spot where a process will break as demands grow and design systems the team wants to use.

  • You are decisive and high agency. You can prioritise between competing demands, are comfortable deciding with incomplete information, and take ownership of the outcomes. You spot what needs doing and do it without waiting to be asked. When something is broken or missing, you take ownership until it’s fixed.

  • You integrate AI well. AI is becoming increasingly important for how Pivotal works. You should have good judgement about where it helps, and where it does not.

  • You make difficult decisions during difficult times. We expect the stakes of our work to only increase, and AI safety work to get a lot more public attention.

  • Strong commitment to the mission. You do not need a background in AI safety, but you should see it as work worth committing a substantial part of your career to.

  • You are honest and direct. Pivotal is small and moves fast. We need someone who tells us when we are wrong.

Experience in a fast-growing organisation, a start-up, a scale-up or a similar organisation is a strong plus.

What we offer

  • Salary: £140,000–196,000. We can pay more for exceptional candidates.

  • Benefits: Relocation support, a contribution to private health insurance, a personal development budget, childcare support, and an employer pension contribution of at least 5%.

  • Location: London.

  • Hours and start date: Full time. Start as soon as possible, but we’re willing to wait for the right candidate.

  • Visa: We can sponsor a skilled worker visa for this role.

Hiring Process

We try to respect your time at every step.

  1. Written application. A short form about who you are and why this role.

  2. Screening interview. 25–30 minutes, personal.

  3. Work task (paid). A task that reflects the real job.

  4. Personal chat. A conversation with Tobias.

  5. Work trial (paid). Two to three days working with us in London (costs covered).

If you have questions before you apply, write to

  • • Salary £140K – £196K • More possible for exceptional candidates

  • Own core infrastructure foundations across identity, networking, compute, storage, secrets, CI/CD and observability.

Required Skills

  • Proven experience deploying cloud-style infrastructure onto customer-owned, on-premise or bare-metal systems.

  • Experience designing for air-gapped, disconnected, sovereign or similarly restricted production environments.

  • Experience leading a substantial high-assurance audit or compliance programme, such as SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, DEFSTAN 05-138 or FedRAMP.

  • Strong Linux, Kubernetes, infrastructure automation and troubleshooting expertise.

  • The ability to write code and scripts, configure infrastructure primitives and personally debug complex platform issues.

  • Experience designing systems that remain supportable when vendor engineers have limited or no access to the customer environment.

  • Strong technical leadership and the ability to align senior engineers and cross-functional partners.

The Senior Software Engineer (Autonomy) will design, build, and operate software capabilities that improve the mission effectiveness and safety of uncrewed surface vehicles across the UFORCE C2/C4ISR stack.

This role spans Perception Autonomy, Autonomy Behaviours—including collision avoidance (COLAV), target-based manoeuvring and engagement—and Swarm Intelligence. You will take cross-system initiatives from design and implementation through scenario-based verification, field trials, deployment, and iteration.

The role requires strong software engineering and mathematical foundations, with an emphasis on autonomy that remains safe, observable, and useful in real operating conditions—including degraded sensors, different sea states, and GNSS- or RF-challenged environments.

What you’ll do

  • Build production-grade capabilities across perception, autonomous behaviours, COLAV, and multi-USV coordination.

  • Define measurable acceptance criteria for autonomy performance, safety, reliability, and operator trust.

  • Validate perception and behaviours across day/night operations, different sea states, sensor degradation, and GNSS/RF-challenged conditions.

  • Develop swarm capabilities such as task allocation, role assignment, formation control, and distributed sensing.

  • Build scenario libraries, replay tooling, automated metrics, and CI gates to prevent regressions.

  • Introduce structured logging, playback, and failure classification to accelerate field diagnosis.

  • Build operator controls and safeguards that enable crews to use autonomy without continuous engineering support.

  • Collaborate with platform, C2, product, and field teams to define clear interfaces and deliver cross-system capabilities.

What success looks like

  • Perception and COLAV meet agreed performance and safety criteria in representative trials.

  • Swarm capabilities are used routinely in multi-USV exercises and degrade safely under constraints.

  • Operators can configure and use autonomy without day-to-day engineering intervention.

  • Automated scenario testing prevents safety and reliability regressions.

  • Field failures can be reproduced and diagnosed within an agreed timeframe.

  • Capabilities have documented operating envelopes, limitations, and evidence of field readiness.

Required qualifications

  • 7+ years of production software or backend engineering experience.

  • Strong experience with Java, Python, or .NET/C#.

  • Clear communication and cross-team collaboration skills.

  • Experience with robotics, autonomous vehicles, maritime autonomy, or UxV systems.

  • Knowledge of perception, sensor fusion, navigation, planning, or control systems.

  • Experience with COLAV, simulation, replay tooling, or multi-agent systems.

  • Build foundation-model-assisted labeling workflows using tools such as SAM-2, Grounding DINO, open-vocabulary models, LLM steering, and human review.

  • Design self-serve operator workflows using yes/no/maybe feedback and natural-language corrections.

  • Create versioned datasets with lineage, data cards, label provenance, class distributions, and known gaps.

  • Develop active-learning loops that prioritize the highest-value frames for limited operator review.

  • Build reproducible train/eval pipelines with experiment tracking, model packaging, and promotion gates.

  • Design evaluation around held-out anchor sets, leakage prevention, baselines, slice metrics, and automated approve/reject decisions.

  • Package the toolchain for on-prem, air-gapped, regulated, or customer-held environments.

  • Close the field-failure loop by feeding live failures back into the next tune cycle.

  • Lead and grow a small specialist team around curation, auto-labeling, deployment, and onboarding.

  • Field failures become reproducible inputs to the next training cycle.

The world's most demanding investors are busy managing trillions, and ignore anything average. Are you excited by the challenge of making them act?

Are you looking to work in an exceptional entrepreneurial team with ambitious, motivated and extremely driven people? And do you want real ownership from your first week? If so, now is the time to apply for the Growth role at Private Equity Insights.

The mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors.

You will work in sprints and get fast execution under your skin. AI has completely changed the game: You will learn to deploy it to outperform a marketing team of 20+ people, while also learning the fundamentals of copywriting that makes elite investors act, get it to the right investor at a meaningful frequency and deploy what works across every marketing channel.

If you want an ambitious mission, real ownership and the fastest learning curve of your career: apply.

Why United Media

United Media (https://www.united-media.com/) focuses on building large-scale industry media and conferences products in sectors such as insurance, finance, retail, etc. As of today, we have organically launched 8 media companies and acquired one.

What we offer you

  • Master the highest bar in the world. Our audience is the world's most demanding investors. They ignore anything average. If your work can make them act, you can make anyone act.
  • Unlimited growth potential. You will get responsibility before you feel ready. That is how you grow fast. We strongly believe in and have a track record of promoting internally. You can expect coaching and development from leaders, peers and experts.
  • Skills that compound for life. Fast execution, copywriting, pricing, conversion optimisation, structured problem solving, and the ability to create impact anywhere in the business at scale.
  • Ownership from the very start. You own outcomes, not tasks. We agree the goal, and you find the way.
  • Travel opportunity. You will be joining our 10+ conferences.

What you will do

Responsibilities in this job will vary, however, feed into the mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors. They will be mostly centered around the following:

  • Build the audience. Identify, target, and convert every fund into our community, and make sure each one receives the right message, at the right time, and never one too many.
  • Own marketing channels that drive revenue. Through existing and new marketing channels, you execute activities that ultimately will drive revenue
  • Write copy that persuades. Every email, landing page and post. Become the best copywriter and leverage it at scale with AI.
  • Sprint, test, implement. Measure the impact of all experiments you run, test offers, copy, prices and pages until the numbers move.
  • Build systems, not one-offs. Anything you do twice becomes a playbook or an AI workflow, so the next win takes less effort than the last.
  • Do whatever it takes to win. Some days that means designing an AI workflow. Some days it means checking investors in at the registration desk at 7am. Nobody here is too good for the work that deliver value for investors and fund managers.

What we expect from you

  • 1 to 3 years of experience
  • Min. a bachelor or master degree with great results
  • A UK work permit. We do not sponsor visas.
  • Strong work ethic with a sense of urgency
  • Exceptional drive and desire to be the best at what you do
  • Proactive approach and sense of ownership/responsibility of everything you do
  • A humble approach and share our passion for building companies and developing people
  • Interested in continuous learning and proactively searching for ways to optimise

Practical details

Full-time, in person from our London office (WeWork), 5 days a week. Expect to travel for work about 20 days a year. The start date is flexible.

raw.title: Go-To-Market
raw.description:
Growth at United Media

The world's most demanding investors are busy managing trillions, and ignore anything average. Are you excited by the challenge of making them act?

Are you looking to work in an exceptional entrepreneurial team with ambitious, motivated and extremely driven people? And do you want real ownership from your first week? If so, now is the time to apply for the Growth role at Private Equity Insights.

The mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors.

You will work in sprints and get fast execution under your skin. AI has completely changed the game: You will learn to deploy it to outperform a marketing team of 20+ people, while also learning the fundamentals of copywriting that makes elite investors act, get it to the right investor at a meaningful frequency and deploy what works across every marketing channel.

If you want an ambitious mission, real ownership and the fastest learning curve of your career: apply.

Why United Media

United Media (https://www.united-media.com/) focuses on building large-scale industry media and conferences products in sectors such as insurance, finance, retail, etc. As of today, we have organically launched 8 media companies and acquired one.

What we offer you

  • Master the highest bar in the world. Our audience is the world's most demanding investors. They ignore anything average. If your work can make them act, you can make anyone act.
  • Unlimited growth potential. You will get responsibility before you feel ready. That is how you grow fast. We strongly believe in and have a track record of promoting internally. You can expect coaching and development from leaders, peers and experts.
  • Skills that compound for life. Fast execution, copywriting, pricing, conversion optimisation, structured problem solving, and the ability to create impact anywhere in the business at scale.
  • Ownership from the very start. You own outcomes, not tasks. We agree the goal, and you find the way.
  • Travel opportunity. You will be joining our 10+ conferences.

What you will do

Responsibilities in this job will vary, however, feed into the mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors. They will be mostly centered around the following:

  • Build the audience. Identify, target, and convert every fund into our community, and make sure each one receives the right message, at the right time, and never one too many.
  • Own marketing channels that drive revenue. Through existing and new marketing channels, you execute activities that ultimately will drive revenue
  • Write copy that persuades. Every email, landing page and post. Become the best copywriter and leverage it at scale with AI.
  • Sprint, test, implement. Measure the impact of all experiments you run, test offers, copy, prices and pages until the numbers move.
  • Build systems, not one-offs. Anything you do twice becomes a playbook or an AI workflow, so the next win takes less effort than the last.
  • Do whatever it takes to win. Some days that means designing an AI workflow. Some days it means checking investors in at the registration desk at 7am. Nobody here is too good for the work that deliver value for investors and fund managers.

What we expect from you

  • 1 to 3 years of experience
  • Min. a bachelor or master degree with great results
  • A UK work permit. We do not sponsor visas.
  • Strong work ethic with a sense of urgency
  • Exceptional drive and desire to be the best at what you do
  • Proactive approach and sense of ownership/responsibility of everything you do
  • A humble approach and share our passion for building companies and developing people
  • Interested in continuous learning and proactively searching for ways to optimise

Practical details

Full-time, in person from our London office (WeWork), 5 days a week. Expect to travel for work about 20 days a year. The start date is flexible.

raw.title: Marketing Automation Engineer
raw.description:
Growth at United Media

The world's most demanding investors are busy managing trillions, and ignore anything average. Are you excited by the challenge of making them act?

Are you looking to work in an exceptional entrepreneurial team with ambitious, motivated and extremely driven people? And do you want real ownership from your first week? If so, now is the time to apply for the Growth role at Private Equity Insights.

The mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors.

You will work in sprints and get fast execution under your skin. AI has completely changed the game: You will learn to deploy it to outperform a marketing team of 20+ people, while also learning the fundamentals of copywriting that makes elite investors act, get it to the right investor at a meaningful frequency and deploy what works across every marketing channel.

If you want an ambitious mission, real ownership and the fastest learning curve of your career: apply.

Why United Media

United Media (https://www.united-media.com/) focuses on building large-scale industry media and conferences products in sectors such as insurance, finance, retail, etc. As of today, we have organically launched 8 media companies and acquired one.

What we offer you

  • Master the highest bar in the world. Our audience is the world's most demanding investors. They ignore anything average. If your work can make them act, you can make anyone act.
  • Unlimited growth potential. You will get responsibility before you feel ready. That is how you grow fast. We strongly believe in and have a track record of promoting internally. You can expect coaching and development from leaders, peers and experts.
  • Skills that compound for life. Fast execution, copywriting, pricing, conversion optimisation, structured problem solving, and the ability to create impact anywhere in the business at scale.
  • Ownership from the very start. You own outcomes, not tasks. We agree the goal, and you find the way.
  • Travel opportunity. You will be joining our 10+ conferences.

What you will do

Responsibilities in this job will vary, however, feed into the mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors. They will be mostly centered around the following:

  • Build the audience. Identify, target, and convert every fund into our community, and make sure each one receives the right message, at the right time, and never one too many.
  • Own marketing channels that drive revenue. Through existing and new marketing channels, you execute activities that ultimately will drive revenue
  • Write copy that persuades. Every email, landing page and post. Become the best copywriter and leverage it at scale with AI.
  • Sprint, test, implement. Measure the impact of all experiments you run, test offers, copy, prices and pages until the numbers move.
  • Build systems, not one-offs. Anything you do twice becomes a playbook or an AI workflow, so the next win takes less effort than the last.
  • Do whatever it takes to win. Some days that means designing an AI workflow. Some days it means checking investors in at the registration desk at 7am. Nobody here is too good for the work that deliver value for investors and fund managers.

What we expect from you

  • 1 to 3 years of experience
  • Min. a bachelor or master degree with great results
  • A UK work permit. We do not sponsor visas.
  • Strong work ethic with a sense of urgency
  • Exceptional drive and desire to be the best at what you do
  • Proactive approach and sense of ownership/responsibility of everything you do
  • A humble approach and share our passion for building companies and developing people
  • Interested in continuous learning and proactively searching for ways to optimise

Practical details

Full-time, in person from our London office (WeWork), 5 days a week. Expect to travel for work about 20 days a year. The start date is flexible.

raw.description:
About Unity Advisory

Unity Advisory is a modern advisory business built for today's CFO, with connected solutions across finance, deals and tax. Focussed on client outcomes, seasoned experts lead every engagement, in an operating model powered by AI and free from audit conflict.

Unity Advisory is a new kind of partner for the office of the CFO. Founded by senior leaders from the world's top advisory firms and backed by Warburg Pincus, we provide integrated finance, commercial, tax and deals support: expert advice, sharper execution, and delivery models built around how organisations operate today. CFOs need trusted advisers without legacy complexity, so we pair expert human judgement with proprietary AI workflows and smart automation, free from audit conflicts.

The Role

We built our deals practice around the client's decision: whether to buy, whether to sell, at what price, on what terms. We work alongside our clients rather than at arm's length, in the room while the deal decision is being made, and our support carries on beyond signing: into the 100-day plan, the hold period and the eventual exit. And that support draws on the whole firm: our tax, finance and commercial specialists work as one team with the deals practice, so the advice a client gets after signing is as integrated as the diligence that came before it.

We're looking for a Manager to join our Financial Due Diligence team. You'll run buy-side and sell-side engagements day to day: getting into the numbers, managing the team on the ground, and making sure clients get clear, well-supported findings on time.

You'll bring solid FDD or transaction services experience from a Big 4 or top-tier advisory firm, and own an engagement from scoping through to final findings. What You'll Do

• Manage buy-side and sell-side financial due diligence engagements from scoping through to completion.

What You'll Bring

• Hands-on experience managing buy-side and sell-side FDD assignments from start to finish.

• Strong technical grounding in accounting and the deal issues that matter most: quality of earnings, working capital, and cash flow.

• A track record of being an excellent team player in multidisciplinary engagements.

• Clear and confident communication (both written and verbal) with clients and senior stakeholders.

• Curiosity and genuine interest in how technology and AI evolve financial due diligence practice and playing a key role in shaping it.

raw.title: Forward deployed engineer, energy
raw.description:
About Watershed

Watershed is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team.

We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us!

The role

Forward Deployed Energy Engineers are a new role at Watershed, combining energy and advisory expertise with product-building skills and commercial instinct. You’ll operate at the cutting edge with Watershed customers to build and deploy the next generation of enterprise energy management.

Energy is one of the largest costs on a big company’s P&L and one of its largest sources of emissions. Yet most enterprises have no one who owns how energy is purchased, consumed and reduced across all their sites. Watershed is building the product that changes that, and it’s the company’s biggest bet for its next chapter.

We already help many of the world’s largest companies measure and cut their emissions, and our clean energy business has executed more than $100M in purchases. Now we’re building energy management from zero to one, with engagements underway with a small group of customers today and scaling in 2027.

You’ll work with enterprises that spend tens of millions a year on electricity, embedded in their energy programmes. Starting from the energy data already in Watershed, you’ll find where they’re overspending, deliver the savings, prototype with AI what should become product, and help customers implement solutions, including buying clean power. The goal is an energy programme that wins backing from their CFO and facilities teams. This is a high-ownership role on a small, high-output team, with a direct line to commercial outcomes and real say in what we build. It reports directly to Watershed’s head of energy and decarbonization.

What you'll do

  • Deliver energy engagements with measurable results: Run deep engagements with a handful of customers at a time: change tariffs, upgrade equipment, find and cut waste, and show the savings.

  • Win customers who vouch for us: Earn the trust of facilities and finance leads so they would tell a peer to work with Watershed.

  • Turn what works into product: Spot the problems that repeat across customers, prototype with AI, and work with our engineers to build an AI-led product for many.

  • Close clean energy deals: Help customers sign deals with existing clean power products (eg EACs, fixed-price VPPAs), yourself or alongside our account teams.

  • Make the team smarter on energy: Be the person colleagues go to on tariffs, loads and what actually cuts a bill.

You might be a fit if you

  • Know how commercial and industrial sites use and buy energy (tariffs, loads, HVAC and controls, procurement) from time at an ESCO, an energy consultancy, an engineering firm or an energy-tech company.

  • Have built things: scripts, models, prototypes or AI-assisted workflows, and can show us one. Prototype-quality code is enough; moving fast matters most.

  • Are fluent with data tools (Excel, SQL or Python) and LLM tools, and can turn messy meter and bill data into something a customer acts on.

  • Have run client work from scoping to outcome, and are as credible with a facilities manager as with a CFO.

  • Can tell a compelling story with data, from raw numbers to insight to a recommendation someone signs off. You've originated work or supported deals, and want to get better at selling.

  • Are energised to build a new product and service, to be on the front lines of building a new business, and to leave a legacy as part of a fast-moving team.

Nice to have

  • Experience with clean power deals (PPAs, VPPAs, fixed-price power contracts, and energy attribute certificates like RECs, GOs and REGOs).

  • Hands-on work with utility bill, half-hourly or building management system data.

  • A few years in consulting or advisory.

Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles)

Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. Certain jobs are open to being remote and will be specifically noted on the jobs page and in the job description if so.

What’s the interview process like?

It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. Next steps can vary by role, but usual next steps are a skill or experience interview (e.g. a coding interview for an engineer, a portfolio review for a designer, deeper experience call for other roles) which leads to a virtual or in person interview panel. We prioritize transparency and lack of surprise throughout the process.

What if I need accommodations for my interview?

At Watershed, we are dedicated to ensuring an inclusive recruitment process. We provide reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities, long-term conditions, mental health needs, religious observances, neurodivergence, or pregnancy-related support requirements. If you need assistance during your process, please contact your recruiter.

Account Executive - Enterprise

London

Wordsmith

Wordsmith is building the legal operations platform for in-house teams, and we are growing fast.

We believe in-house legal is becoming one of the most important functions in the AI era. Every business is moving faster, but legal work is still too often scattered across inboxes, chats, documents, and disconnected systems.

Wordsmith brings that work into one system. Requests come in from across the business, AI agents handle the routine, lawyers stay in control where judgment matters, and every step is captured as work happens.

We are built for in-house legal, not law firms. Our goal is to help legal teams move faster, reduce unnecessary external counsel spend, and become a function the business can run with.

More than 500 companies, including Financial Times, Safelite, Trip.com, Canva, Starling, and Sage, use Wordsmith. Backed by $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe, and others, we are building one of the defining companies in legal AI.

The Role

We’re hiring an Enterprise Account Executive to lead complex, high-value deals across large organisations.

You’ll be responsible for building and progressing a focused set of strategic opportunities. This means navigating multiple stakeholders, building internal champions, and creating alignment across legal, technical, and commercial teams.

You’ll work closely with Legal Engineers, Product, and Leadership, but you own the deal strategy and the outcome.

What you’ll do

  • Own a portfolio of high-value, enterprise opportunities

  • Build and execute deal strategies across complex buying groups

  • Navigate stakeholders across Legal, Finance, Security, IT, and Procurement

  • Develop strong champions and drive internal alignment within accounts

  • Lead longer sales cycles (6–12+ months) with clear structure and momentum

  • Partner closely with GTM Legal Engineers on solution design

  • Maintain accurate forecasting and clear deal visibility

What we’re looking for

  • Experience closing complex enterprise SaaS deals

  • Track record of landing and expanding high-value accounts

  • Strong stakeholder management across multiple functions

  • Ability to build champions and navigate internal politics

  • Structured, strategic approach to deal management

  • High ownership and accountability for outcomes

How we work

We’re an in-office team. We work together because it makes us faster, sharper, and more effective. You should expect to be in the office or out visiting clients as your default.

This is a high performance environment. We set a high bar, move quickly, and expect people to take ownership of real problems.

There isn’t always a clear path. The people who do well here figure things out, stay close to the work, and keep pushing until they get to the right outcome.

This role requires patience, structure, and strong judgement. You’ll be trusted to run complex deals with a high degree of autonomy.

Why Wordsmith

We’re in a period of strong momentum — growing quickly, winning new customers, and expanding into larger accounts.

The product is landing well, the market is ready, and the team is scaling to meet demand.

If you want to be in the room, close meaningful deals, and grow quickly in a high bar environment, this is one of the best places to do it.
